Name: Employee Entry Management
Summary: Manage everyday workforce entry with badges, readers, turnstiles, and door schedules.
Description: Day-to-day entry for staff at staffed sites. Security sets door schedules and tailgating rules, handles lost badges, and reports forced or denied doors. HR decides who is hired or leaves; this service acts on that feed.
In Scope: Badge-based entry for employees at staffed sites, door schedules, tailgating rules, and lost-badge handling.
Out of Scope: Visitor processing, contractor vetting, and HR decisions about who is hired or terminated.
Deliverables: An entry policy per site, a door schedule register, and a monthly report of denied entries and forced doors.
Prerequisites: An HR feed of joiners and leavers, a badge system of record, and a named facility owner per site.
Lead Time: Standard badge or access request fulfilled within 2 business days of manager approval.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Standard request fulfilled within 2 business days / urgent removal within 1 hour
Escalation Path: Access granted without approval, or a leaver badge still active, escalates to the facility security manager and the identity lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Tailgating, use of lost or shared badges, and former employees entering after termination.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of leaver badges disabled within 1 hour, tailgating events per site per month, and lost-badge replacement time.

Name: Visitor Management
Summary: Register, badge, and escort visitors and contractors, and keep a reliable visitor log.
Description: Visitors are pre-registered by a host, checked against ID at reception, and badged for the day. Hosts own escort duty. Security keeps the log and follows up on badges that are not returned.
In Scope: Pre-registration, ID checks, visitor badges, host escort rules, and visitor log retention at reception.
Out of Scope: Employee badge issuance, event security planning, and background screening of visitors.
Deliverables: A visitor procedure, a retained visitor log, and a monthly report of unescorted or overdue visitors.
Prerequisites: A visitor management system or log, trained reception staff, and a host responsibility statement.
Lead Time: Same-day pre-registration for individual visitors; group visits need 2 business days of notice.
SLA Response Target: Walk-in visitor processed at reception within 10 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Pre-registered visitor badged within 5 minutes of arrival / unreturned badge followed up the same day
Escalation Path: A visitor who refuses an ID check, or is found unescorted in a work area, escalates to the reception supervisor and the security operations manager immediately.
Threats Addressed: Unescorted visitors reaching work areas, social engineering at reception, and visitor badges kept after departure.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of visitors pre-registered, unreturned visitor badges per month, and unescorted-visitor incidents.

Name: Restricted-Area Access
Summary: Authorize and enforce entry to sensitive rooms such as server rooms, labs, and vaults.
Description: Each restricted room has a named owner who approves its access list. Security enforces the list at the door and runs a quarterly owner attestation. General office entry is handled by employee entry management.
In Scope: Access lists, two-person rules, and authorization for data centers, labs, cash rooms, and other restricted areas.
Out of Scope: General office entry, building design changes, and IT access to the systems inside the room.
Deliverables: A restricted-area access list per room, a quarterly owner attestation, and an access exception log.
Prerequisites: A designated owner for each restricted area, a badge system that supports access groups, and an approval workflow.
Lead Time: Restricted-area access granted within 2 business days of the area owner's approval.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Standard request fulfilled within 2 business days / urgent removal within 1 hour
Escalation Path: Entry by a badge not on the restricted list, or a restricted door held open, escalates to the area owner and the security operations manager immediately.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized entry to sensitive rooms, privilege creep on access groups, and insider tampering with equipment.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of restricted lists attested on time, entries by unapproved badges, and stale access removed per review.

Name: Physical Key Management
Summary: Issue, track, audit, and recover mechanical keys and lock combinations.
Description: A register of every key and who holds it, kept in a controlled cabinet or electronic key system. Security audits holdings and recommends a rekey when a master key goes missing. Badge access is a separate service.
In Scope: Issue, tracking, rekeying, and audit of mechanical keys, key cabinets, and master key systems.
Out of Scope: Electronic badge management, locksmith hardware purchasing, and vehicle fleet keys.
Deliverables: A key register with holders, a key cabinet audit record, and a rekey recommendation when a master key is lost.
Prerequisites: A current key inventory, a lockable key cabinet or electronic key system, and a locksmith contact.
Lead Time: Key issued within 3 business days of approval. A rekey after a lost master key is scheduled within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Key issued within 3 business days / rekey decision within 2 business days of a lost master key
Escalation Path: A lost master or grand-master key escalates to the facility security manager the same day for a rekey decision.
Threats Addressed: Lost or copied master keys, keys held by former staff, and unlogged key use for restricted rooms.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of keys accounted for at audit, lost keys per quarter, and time to rekey after a master key loss.

Name: Physical Credential Issuance and Revocation
Summary: Produce, activate, and revoke photo badges and access cards for staff and contractors.
Description: Badges are printed and encoded only after identity is checked and HR or the sponsoring manager confirms the start. Revocation is driven by the leaver feed and reconciled daily, so departed staff do not keep working cards.
In Scope: Printing, encoding, activating, suspending, and revoking photo badges and access cards for the workforce and contractors.
Out of Scope: Logical account provisioning, door hardware changes, and visitor passes.
Deliverables: An issuance and revocation procedure, a daily revocation reconciliation, and a badge inventory report.
Prerequisites: An authoritative HR and contractor feed, a badge printer and encoder, and photo capture at onboarding.
Lead Time: Badge ready on the start date when HR submits the joiner at least 3 business days ahead.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Standard request fulfilled within 2 business days / urgent removal within 1 hour
Escalation Path: Access granted without approval, or a leaver badge still active, escalates to the facility security manager and the identity lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Active badges held by leavers, cloned access cards, and badges issued without identity verification.
KPIs and Metrics: Median time to revoke after termination, badges issued without approval, and orphaned active badges found at reconciliation.

Name: Fence and Barrier Protection
Summary: Inspect and maintain fences, walls, bollards, and anti-ram barriers at the site boundary.
Description: The perimeter line is walked on a schedule and every breach or defect becomes a work order with photos. Urgent gaps get a guard or temporary repair the same day. New construction is outside this service.
In Scope: Inspection, repair, and condition tracking of fences, bollards, walls, and anti-ram barriers at site perimeters.
Out of Scope: New construction, landscaping that is not security-related, and municipal roadway barriers.
Deliverables: A perimeter condition log, repair work orders with photos, and a semi-annual perimeter risk summary.
Prerequisites: A site plan showing the perimeter line, a facilities maintenance contract, and an inspection schedule.
Lead Time: Perimeter repair or change request assessed within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Breach of the perimeter acknowledged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Temporary repair or posted guard within 4 hours / permanent repair scheduled within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A breached perimeter at a critical site escalates to the security operations manager and the site leader immediately.
Threats Addressed: Fence cutting, climbing aids left near the fence line, and vehicle-borne attacks against building frontage.
KPIs and Metrics: Breaches found per inspection, median repair time, and percent of perimeter inspected on schedule.

Name: Gate Security
Summary: Operate and supervise pedestrian and vehicle gates at the site boundary.
Description: Gatehouse staff or the control center run each gate to written post orders. Forced gates and faults are logged and restored quickly so a broken gate is never simply left open.
In Scope: Operation and supervision of pedestrian and vehicle gates, turnstiles, and gatehouse procedures.
Out of Scope: Parking enforcement, traffic management on public roads, and visitor pre-registration.
Deliverables: Gate post orders, a gate fault and forced-entry log, and a monthly gate availability report.
Prerequisites: Working gate hardware with remote release, a staffed or monitored gatehouse, and gate post orders.
Lead Time: Perimeter repair or change request assessed within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Breach of the perimeter acknowledged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Temporary repair or posted guard within 4 hours / permanent repair scheduled within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A breached perimeter at a critical site escalates to the security operations manager and the site leader immediately.
Threats Addressed: Tailgating vehicles, forced gates, and gates left open after a fault.
KPIs and Metrics: Gate uptime, forced-gate events per month, and time to restore a failed gate.

Name: Vehicle Entry Control
Summary: Screen, authorize, and log vehicles entering the site and its loading docks.
Description: Vehicles need a valid permit or a booked delivery to enter. Unscheduled deliveries are screened in a holding area, and refused vehicles are logged. Parking allocation is not part of this service.
In Scope: Vehicle permits, plate checks, delivery vehicle screening, and controlled entry to loading docks and car parks.
Out of Scope: Fleet management, parking allocation disputes, and law enforcement traffic stops.
Deliverables: A vehicle permit register, a delivery screening procedure, and a log of refused or flagged vehicles.
Prerequisites: A permit system or plate recognition tool, a delivery schedule from receiving, and a screening area.
Lead Time: Vehicle permit issued within 3 business days of request. Deliveries are booked 24 hours ahead.
SLA Response Target: Vehicle at the gate screened within 10 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Permit request decided within 3 business days / refused vehicle reported in the same shift
Escalation Path: A vehicle that refuses screening, or an unscheduled vehicle stopping near a critical building, escalates to the shift supervisor and to police when needed.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized vehicles on site, concealed items in deliveries, and vehicles staged near critical buildings.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of vehicles with valid permits, refused entries per month, and unscheduled deliveries screened.

Name: Public/Restricted Area Separation
Summary: Define public, controlled, and restricted zones in each building and the barriers between them.
Description: Security produces a zoning plan for each site, sets the control required at each boundary, and lists the gaps. Facilities and project teams build the fixes. Interior design and fire code are out of scope.
In Scope: Definition of public, controlled, and restricted zones in a building and the barriers and controls between them.
Out of Scope: Interior design, fire code compliance decisions, and furniture layout.
Deliverables: A zoning plan with marked boundaries, a control requirement per boundary, and a list of gaps against the plan.
Prerequisites: Current floor plans, a list of sensitive functions per floor, and a facilities contact for each site.
Lead Time: Zoning review starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Zoning recommendation delivered within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A design that puts restricted assets in a public zone escalates to the facility security manager and the project sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Public visitors wandering into work areas, shoulder surfing from lobbies, and unlocked internal doors.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of sites with an approved zoning plan, boundary gaps open beyond 90 days, and zone violations reported.

Name: High-Security Area Designation
Summary: Set the criteria for high-security areas, designate rooms against them, and define their minimum controls.
Description: A room becomes high-security only against written criteria and with executive sign-off. Each designation carries a control checklist. The access list itself is run by restricted-area access.
In Scope: Criteria and approval for designating rooms as high-security, and the minimum controls each designation requires.
Out of Scope: Running the access list for the room, equipment purchasing, and IT controls inside the room.
Deliverables: A high-security area register, a designation criteria standard, and a control checklist per designated room.
Prerequisites: An asset criticality list, executive sponsor sign-off, and a budget owner for added controls.
Lead Time: Zoning review starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Zoning recommendation delivered within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A design that puts restricted assets in a public zone escalates to the facility security manager and the project sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Tampering with crown-jewel equipment, theft of sensitive materials, and covert entry to secure rooms.
KPIs and Metrics: Designated areas meeting all minimum controls, designations reviewed on schedule, and open control gaps.

Name: Secure Circulation Routes
Summary: Plan movement routes that keep visitors, deliveries, and valuables away from sensitive areas.
Description: Security maps how staff, visitors, deliveries, and cash or evidence move through a site and recommends routes that avoid restricted zones. Routes are reviewed after layout changes. Wayfinding and accessibility stay with facilities.
In Scope: Design of routes for staff, visitors, deliveries, and cash or evidence movement so they avoid restricted zones.
Out of Scope: Wayfinding signage, accessibility compliance, and elevator maintenance.
Deliverables: A circulation map per site, a route recommendation report, and a list of crossings that need a control.
Prerequisites: Floor plans, delivery and visitor flow data, and input from the site operations lead.
Lead Time: Zoning review starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Zoning recommendation delivered within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A design that puts restricted assets in a public zone escalates to the facility security manager and the project sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Visitors passing restricted rooms, interception of valuables in transit, and unsupervised delivery paths.
KPIs and Metrics: Restricted-zone crossings removed, routes reviewed after layout changes, and incidents on mapped routes.

Name: Camera Coverage Planning
Summary: Decide where cameras go and what they must see to cover entrances and risk areas.
Description: A coverage review per site that ranks blind spots by risk and sets field-of-view and resolution needs for each new position. It plans coverage only. Buying and installing cameras is a separate project.
In Scope: Camera placement, field-of-view and resolution requirements, and coverage gap analysis for entrances and critical areas.
Out of Scope: Purchasing cameras, privacy notices for staff, and coverage of public streets.
Deliverables: A coverage map per site, a gap list ranked by risk, and a camera specification for each new position.
Prerequisites: Site floor plans, a list of critical areas and entrances, and access to the video management system.
Lead Time: Coverage review scheduled within 15 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Planning request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Coverage map and gap list within 15 business days of the site walk
Escalation Path: A critical entrance with no usable camera coverage escalates to the facility security manager and the site leader.
Threats Addressed: Blind spots at entrances, unrecorded theft in stock areas, and unidentifiable faces in recorded footage.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical entrances with full coverage, gap items closed per quarter, and cameras meeting resolution standard.

Name: Live Video Monitoring
Summary: Watch priority camera feeds in real time and act on what operators see.
Description: Control center operators watch an approved list of priority cameras, tag events, and dispatch or escalate. Covert monitoring of individual employees is not part of this service and needs HR and legal involvement.
In Scope: Real-time watching of priority camera feeds by the security control center, with event tagging and escalation.
Out of Scope: Covert surveillance of individual employees, HR investigations, and footage analytics model building.
Deliverables: A monitored camera list, an event log with timestamps, and a shift summary of observed incidents.
Prerequisites: A staffed control center, a video wall or console, and a prioritized camera list approved by the site owner.
Lead Time: New camera added to the monitored list within 5 business days of the site owner's approval.
SLA Response Target: Priority event on a monitored camera actioned within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Responder dispatched within 5 minutes of a confirmed event
Escalation Path: Violence, an intrusion, or a monitored camera going dark escalates to the shift supervisor immediately, and to police when life safety is involved.
Threats Addressed: Intruders on site after hours, violence in public areas, and theft in progress at entrances.
KPIs and Metrics: Events detected live versus after the fact, operator response time, and cameras offline at shift start.

Name: Recorded-Video Retrieval
Summary: Search, export, and release recorded footage for investigations and legal requests.
Description: Footage is released only on an approved request from legal, HR, or investigations. Each export carries a hash and a chain-of-custody record. Requests must arrive before the recording is overwritten at the end of retention.
In Scope: Search, review, export, and secure handover of recorded footage for investigations and legal requests.
Out of Scope: Releasing footage to the media, editing or enhancing footage, and live monitoring.
Deliverables: A footage request log, exported clips with hash and chain-of-custody record, and a retention exception record.
Prerequisites: An approved request from legal, HR, or investigations, a defined retention period, and export tooling.
Lead Time: Standard request fulfilled within 2 business days. Requests must arrive before footage is overwritten at the end of the retention period.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged within 4 business hours / urgent preservation within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Export with hash and chain-of-custody record within 2 business days
Escalation Path: A request near the overwrite deadline, or one under a legal hold, escalates to the security operations manager for immediate preservation.
Threats Addressed: Lost evidence from expired recordings, unauthorized release of footage, and tampered video files.
KPIs and Metrics: Requests fulfilled within SLA, exports with a complete chain of custody, and requests that missed retention.

Name: Video System Maintenance
Summary: Keep cameras, recorders, and video management servers healthy, patched, and recording.
Description: Daily health checks catch dead cameras and full recorders before footage is needed. Firmware is kept on supported versions and faults are repaired with a recorded root cause. New camera projects are out of scope.
In Scope: Health checks, firmware updates, storage monitoring, and repair of cameras, recorders, and video management servers.
Out of Scope: Network switch ownership, new camera installation projects, and footage review.
Deliverables: A daily camera health report, a firmware currency report, and repair tickets with root cause.
Prerequisites: An asset list of cameras and recorders, a maintenance contract, and network access for the maintainer.
Lead Time: New device added to health monitoring within 5 business days of installation.
SLA Response Target: Camera or recorder fault acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Critical-entrance camera restored within 1 business day / other faults within 5 business days
Escalation Path: A recorder failure that stops recording for a whole site escalates to the security systems lead and the maintainer the same day.
Threats Addressed: Silent camera failures, recorders running out of storage, and exploitable camera firmware.
KPIs and Metrics: Camera uptime, mean time to repair, and percent of devices on supported firmware.

Name: Door and Window Monitoring
Summary: Monitor door contacts, glass-break sensors, and held-open alarms on perimeter openings.
Description: Perimeter doors and windows are armed on a schedule and alarm to the control center when forced or held open. Any zone in bypass needs an approval and an end date. Fire alarm monitoring is separate.
In Scope: Door contacts, glass-break sensors, held-open alarms, and after-hours arming of perimeter doors and windows.
Out of Scope: Fire alarm monitoring, door hardware replacement, and HVAC sensors.
Deliverables: A sensor zone list, a held-open and forced-door report, and a bypass register with approvals.
Prerequisites: Installed contacts on perimeter openings, an alarm panel connected to the control center, and arming schedules.
Lead Time: New sensor zone design within 10 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Alarm acknowledged by the control center within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Alarm verified or dispatched within 10 minutes / sensor fault fixed within 2 business days
Escalation Path: An unverified alarm at a restricted area, or a zone left in bypass, escalates to the shift supervisor and the security operations manager.
Threats Addressed: Forced entry through doors, propped-open fire exits, and break-ins through ground-floor windows.
KPIs and Metrics: Forced-door alarms per month, doors held open beyond threshold, and zones in bypass more than 24 hours.

Name: Motion Detection
Summary: Run interior and exterior motion sensors and tune them so real intrusions stand out.
Description: Motion zones are mapped, walk-tested each quarter, and tuned against nuisance alarms. The aim is detection the control center trusts, not a stream of false alarms from wildlife, HVAC, or cleaners.
In Scope: Interior and exterior motion sensors, detection zones, and sensitivity tuning to keep nuisance alarms low.
Out of Scope: Occupancy analytics for real estate planning, lighting control, and camera analytics purchasing.
Deliverables: A motion zone design, a nuisance alarm tuning record, and a quarterly sensor walk-test report.
Prerequisites: Mapped detection zones, an arming schedule, and maintainer access to adjust sensors.
Lead Time: New sensor zone design within 10 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Alarm acknowledged by the control center within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Alarm verified or dispatched within 10 minutes / sensor fault fixed within 2 business days
Escalation Path: An unverified alarm at a restricted area, or a zone left in bypass, escalates to the shift supervisor and the security operations manager.
Threats Addressed: After-hours intruders inside buildings, people hiding after closing, and unauthorized presence in yards.
KPIs and Metrics: Nuisance alarm rate per zone, walk-test pass rate, and time to fix a failed sensor.

Name: Alarm Verification
Summary: Confirm whether an intrusion alarm is real before guards or police are sent.
Description: Operators use cameras, audio, a guard check, or a keyholder call to verify each alarm and record the disposition. Verified alarms go to dispatch. Monthly false-alarm analysis feeds tuning.
In Scope: Confirming whether an intrusion alarm is real using video, audio, guard checks, or keyholder contact before dispatch.
Out of Scope: Police response policy, alarm hardware design, and post-incident investigation.
Deliverables: A verification procedure, an alarm disposition log, and a monthly false-alarm analysis by zone.
Prerequisites: Cameras covering alarm zones, a keyholder list, and a control center with authority to dispatch.
Lead Time: New sensor zone design within 10 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Alarm acknowledged by the control center within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Alarm verified or dispatched within 10 minutes / sensor fault fixed within 2 business days
Escalation Path: An unverified alarm at a restricted area, or a zone left in bypass, escalates to the shift supervisor and the security operations manager.
Threats Addressed: Real intrusions dismissed as false, police fines for false dispatch, and alarm fatigue in the control center.
KPIs and Metrics: Percent of alarms verified within 10 minutes, false dispatch rate, and verified intrusions per quarter.

Name: Physical Alarm Triage
Summary: Sort incoming intrusion, duress, panic, and equipment alarms by priority and start the right response.
Description: Every alarm lands in one queue and is ranked by a written priority matrix, so a duress call is never stuck behind a nuisance sensor. Fire and life-safety alarms follow their own procedures.
In Scope: Sorting incoming intrusion, duress, panic, and equipment alarms by priority and opening the right response.
Out of Scope: Fire and life-safety alarm response, alarm hardware repair, and incident investigation.
Deliverables: An alarm priority matrix, a triage log with dispositions, and a weekly alarm volume and source report.
Prerequisites: An alarm monitoring platform, a documented priority matrix, and trained control center operators.
Lead Time: New alarm type or site onboarded to the alarm queue within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Priority alarm acknowledged within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Priority alarm dispositioned within 15 minutes / routine alarm within 1 hour
Escalation Path: An alarm that is not acknowledged within 5 minutes pages the control center supervisor and the on-call security manager.
Threats Addressed: Duress calls handled too slowly, missed alarms during alarm floods, and repeated nuisance sources masking real events.
KPIs and Metrics: Median acknowledgment time, alarms dispositioned within SLA, and top nuisance sources per week.

Name: Physical Alarm Escalation
Summary: Escalate verified or unresolved alarms to supervisors, keyholders, and security leadership.
Description: A contact tree per site says who is called, in what order, and how fast. Escalations are logged so missed contacts and stale call lists show up in the monthly report.
In Scope: Escalation of verified or unresolved alarms to supervisors, site managers, keyholders, and security leadership.
Out of Scope: Dispatching emergency services, alarm triage, and after-action reporting.
Deliverables: An escalation contact tree per site, an escalation log, and a monthly escalation timeliness report.
Prerequisites: A current contact list with backups, an escalation matrix by alarm priority, and paging tools.
Lead Time: New alarm type or site onboarded to the alarm queue within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Priority alarm acknowledged within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Priority alarm dispositioned within 15 minutes / routine alarm within 1 hour
Escalation Path: An alarm that is not acknowledged within 5 minutes pages the control center supervisor and the on-call security manager.
Threats Addressed: Serious events left with frontline staff, unreachable keyholders, and delayed leadership awareness.
KPIs and Metrics: Escalations reaching a contact within target, failed contact attempts, and contact list accuracy at audit.

Name: Physical Alarm Dispatch Coordination
Summary: Send guards, keyholders, police, or fire to verified alarms and track them to closure.
Description: The control center dispatches the right responder for each verified alarm and records dispatch, arrival, and clear times. Armed response and emergency services command are outside this service.
In Scope: Sending guards, keyholders, police, or fire to verified alarms and tracking them to arrival and closure.
Out of Scope: Running patrol schedules, providing armed response, and emergency services command.
Deliverables: A dispatch log with times, a responder roster per site, and an arrival time report per month.
Prerequisites: A responder roster, radio or phone dispatch tools, and agreements with any external responders.
Lead Time: New alarm type or site onboarded to the alarm queue within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Priority alarm acknowledged within 60 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Priority alarm dispositioned within 15 minutes / routine alarm within 1 hour
Escalation Path: An alarm that is not acknowledged within 5 minutes pages the control center supervisor and the on-call security manager.
Threats Addressed: Slow response to real intrusions, responders sent to the wrong location, and unsupervised response to duress alarms.
KPIs and Metrics: Median dispatch-to-arrival time, dispatches closed with a report, and cancelled false dispatches.

Name: Fixed-Post Coverage
Summary: Staff fixed guard posts at entrances, docks, and control points to an approved schedule.
Description: Posts are staffed to a schedule the site owner has approved, and vacancies are filled within hours. Monthly reports show coverage, overtime, and post checks. Event security and executive protection are separate services.
In Scope: Staffing of fixed guard posts at entrances, docks, and control points against an approved post schedule.
Out of Scope: Event security, executive protection, and armed guarding.
Deliverables: An approved post schedule, a daily post coverage record, and a monthly vacancy and overtime report.
Prerequisites: A guard services contract, approved post locations, and a staffing schedule.
Lead Time: New post or post change staffed within 10 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Post vacancy or guard issue acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Vacant post filled within 2 hours / post order change issued within 5 business days
Escalation Path: An unstaffed critical post, or a guard conduct issue, escalates to the security operations manager and the guard contractor account lead.
Threats Addressed: Unattended entrances, unchallenged intruders, and gaps in coverage at shift change.
KPIs and Metrics: Post coverage percentage, unfilled post hours per month, and post checks passed.

Name: Reception Security
Summary: Handle security at reception, including ID checks, visitor badges, deliveries, and lobby awareness.
Description: Reception staff check ID, issue visitor badges, take deliveries, and watch the lobby. Mystery-visitor tests show whether the front desk resists social engineering. Hospitality and switchboard duties are not included.
In Scope: Security duties at reception desks, including ID checks, visitor badge issue, deliveries, and lobby awareness.
Out of Scope: Corporate hospitality, switchboard services, and mailroom screening.
Deliverables: Reception security procedures, a lobby incident log, and a quarterly reception mystery-visitor result.
Prerequisites: Staffed reception desks, a visitor management system, and reception training material.
Lead Time: Reception procedures for a new site in place within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Visitor or delivery attended at the desk within 5 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Lobby incident handed to the shift supervisor within 10 minutes
Escalation Path: An aggressive visitor, a suspicious package, or a refused ID check escalates to the shift supervisor and, where needed, to police.
Threats Addressed: Social engineering at the front desk, unscreened deliveries, and aggressive visitors in the lobby.
KPIs and Metrics: Mystery-visitor pass rate, lobby incidents per month, and visitor ID check compliance.

Name: Post-Order Management
Summary: Write, approve, and maintain the instructions that tell guards what to do at each post.
Description: Every post has current written orders approved by the site owner and acknowledged by each guard. Orders are reviewed every year and after any layout or risk change, so guards are not left to improvise.
In Scope: Writing, approving, distributing, and acknowledging post orders that tell guards exactly what to do at each post.
Out of Scope: Contract negotiation with the guard provider, guard hiring, and site risk assessment.
Deliverables: A post order library with version history, guard acknowledgment records, and an annual post order review.
Prerequisites: A post list, site risk inputs, and a named site owner who approves each post order.
Lead Time: New or changed post order drafted within 5 business days of a post change.
SLA Response Target: Post order change request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved post order issued within 5 business days
Escalation Path: A post order that conflicts with life-safety procedures escalates to the security operations manager and the site EHS lead.
Threats Addressed: Guards improvising during incidents, outdated instructions after layout changes, and inconsistent enforcement.
KPIs and Metrics: Post orders current within 12 months, guard acknowledgment rate, and incidents traced to unclear orders.

Name: Scheduled Patrols
Summary: Run planned guard patrols with checkpoints and varied timing across buildings and grounds.
Description: Routes and checkpoint tours are tracked electronically so missed rounds show up. Timing is varied to avoid a predictable pattern. Alarm response is handled through dispatch.
In Scope: Planned guard patrols with checkpoints, randomized timing, and tour verification across buildings and grounds.
Out of Scope: Mobile response to alarms, parking enforcement, and safety inspections for code compliance.
Deliverables: Patrol route maps, a checkpoint tour report per shift, and a monthly missed-checkpoint report.
Prerequisites: Defined patrol routes, a guard tour tracking system, and patrol staffing in the post schedule.
Lead Time: New patrol route added within 5 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Patrol exception acknowledged by the control center within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: High-risk exception secured within 1 hour / work order opened within 1 business day
Escalation Path: A missed patrol at a critical site, or a hazard left unsecured, escalates to the shift supervisor and the site leader.
Threats Addressed: Intruders hiding on site, unsecured doors after hours, and slow discovery of damage.
KPIs and Metrics: Checkpoints completed on time, missed tours per month, and findings raised per patrol.

Name: Facility Security Inspections
Summary: Inspect locks, lighting, alarms, cameras, and storage practices against a site checklist during rounds.
Description: Inspections follow a checklist approved by the facility owner and record findings with photos. Each finding goes to a corrective action owner. Building code and safety audits are out of scope.
In Scope: Structured security inspections of locks, lighting, alarms, cameras, and storage practices during patrols.
Out of Scope: Building code inspections, occupational health audits, and IT configuration checks.
Deliverables: An inspection checklist per site, inspection results with photos, and a corrective action tracker.
Prerequisites: A site checklist approved by the facility owner, a reporting tool, and a facilities work order path.
Lead Time: New patrol route added within 5 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Patrol exception acknowledged by the control center within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: High-risk exception secured within 1 hour / work order opened within 1 business day
Escalation Path: A missed patrol at a critical site, or a hazard left unsecured, escalates to the shift supervisor and the site leader.
Threats Addressed: Unlocked doors, failed lighting, disabled cameras, and sensitive material left unsecured.
KPIs and Metrics: Inspection completion rate, findings closed within 30 days, and repeat findings per site.

Name: Patrol Exception Reporting
Summary: Record and route anything abnormal found on patrol, from open doors to hazards.
Description: Patrols log exceptions with time, place, and a photo, and each one is routed to an owner. Weekly trends show repeat locations. Investigating the exception is a separate step.
In Scope: Recording and routing anything abnormal found on patrol, from open doors to hazards to suspicious people.
Out of Scope: Investigating the exception, repairing faults, and HR action for policy breaches.
Deliverables: Exception reports with time, place, and photo, a routing record to owners, and a weekly exception trend summary.
Prerequisites: A reporting tool on patrol devices, owner routing rules, and a work order system.
Lead Time: New patrol route added within 5 business days of a site request.
SLA Response Target: Patrol exception acknowledged by the control center within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: High-risk exception secured within 1 hour / work order opened within 1 business day
Escalation Path: A missed patrol at a critical site, or a hazard left unsecured, escalates to the shift supervisor and the site leader.
Threats Addressed: Ignored security defects, repeated unsecured areas, and lost evidence of suspicious activity.
KPIs and Metrics: Exceptions routed within 1 hour, exceptions closed within target, and repeat exceptions by location.

Name: Physical Security Communications Coordination
Summary: Coordinate radio, phone, and mass-notification traffic between the control center, guards, and sites.
Description: The control center keeps channels, call signs, and site contacts current and runs communications during events. Crisis messaging to media and employees stays with corporate communications.
In Scope: Radio, phone, and mass notification coordination between the control center, guards, sites, and leadership during events.
Out of Scope: Corporate communications to media, crisis communications strategy, and telecom procurement.
Deliverables: A communications plan, radio channel and call-sign register, and an event communications log.
Prerequisites: Radios or push-to-talk tools, a mass notification system, and a current site contact directory.
Lead Time: New site connected to control center procedures within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Inbound call or radio request answered within 30 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Incident coordinated to a responder within 5 minutes / shift handover completed before relief
Escalation Path: A control center outage, or loss of radio contact with a site, escalates to the control center manager and the backup center.
Threats Addressed: Lost coordination during incidents, rumors spreading during emergencies, and unreachable responders.
KPIs and Metrics: Radio checks passed, notification delivery rate, and time to first update during events.

Name: Physical Security Dispatch
Summary: Assign officers and patrols to calls for service from the control center and track them to closure.
Description: Calls for service, escorts, and alarms are dispatched from one board that shows unit status. Every call is closed with a disposition, and monthly reports track dispatch times.
In Scope: Dispatching guards and mobile patrols to calls for service, alarms, and escorts, and tracking them to closure.
Out of Scope: Emergency medical decisions, alarm triage, and law enforcement command.
Deliverables: A computer-aided or manual dispatch log, a unit status board, and a monthly dispatch performance report.
Prerequisites: A dispatch console, a list of available units per shift, and agreed call-for-service categories.
Lead Time: New site connected to control center procedures within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Inbound call or radio request answered within 30 seconds
SLA Resolution Target: Incident coordinated to a responder within 5 minutes / shift handover completed before relief
Escalation Path: A control center outage, or loss of radio contact with a site, escalates to the control center manager and the backup center.
Threats Addressed: Slow response to calls, units sent without critical information, and unrecorded incidents.
KPIs and Metrics: Median dispatch time, calls closed with a disposition, and calls awaiting a unit beyond target.

Name: Physical Security Shift Handover
Summary: Hand over open events, faults, and watch items cleanly between control center and guard shifts.
Description: Each shift change uses a standard template and a signed log, so bypassed alarms, open incidents, and watch items carry forward. Scheduling and timekeeping are not part of this service.
In Scope: Structured handover between control center and guard shifts covering open events, faults, and watch items.
Out of Scope: Shift scheduling, timekeeping, and payroll for guards.
Deliverables: A shift handover template, a signed handover log, and an open-items list carried across shifts.
Prerequisites: A handover template, overlapping shift times, and a shared log tool.
Lead Time: The handover template is used from the first shift at a new site.
SLA Response Target: Handover briefing starts within 15 minutes of shift change
SLA Resolution Target: Signed handover log completed before outgoing staff leave
Escalation Path: An open priority incident that the incoming supervisor has not accepted escalates to the control center manager.
Threats Addressed: Open incidents dropped between shifts, forgotten bypassed alarms, and lost context on watch items.
KPIs and Metrics: Handovers completed on time, open items aged over 24 hours, and incidents caused by missed handover.

Name: Unauthorized-Entry Incident Response
Summary: Respond to intruders, trespassers, and confirmed unauthorized entry.
Description: Responders challenge or escort the person, call police when needed, and record the failed control. Prosecution decisions and long-term perimeter redesign are outside this service.
In Scope: Responding to intruders, trespassers, and confirmed unauthorized entry, including challenge, escort, and police contact.
Out of Scope: Cyber intrusion response, prosecution decisions, and long-term perimeter redesign.
Deliverables: An incident report, a timeline of entry and response, and a recommendation for the control that failed.
Prerequisites: Trained responders, a response procedure, and a police liaison contact for each site.
Lead Time: Standing response service. Engaged as soon as an incident is reported.
SLA Response Target: Priority physical incident attended within 15 minutes on staffed sites
SLA Resolution Target: Scene secured within 30 minutes / incident report filed within 1 business day
Escalation Path: An incident with injury, weapons, or loss of critical assets escalates to the security operations manager and emergency services immediately.
Threats Addressed: Trespassers reaching sensitive areas, theft or sabotage by intruders, and repeat entry through the same gap.
KPIs and Metrics: Response time to confirmed entry, incidents contained without injury, and repeat entries by gap.

Name: Physical Theft Response
Summary: Take immediate action when a theft of equipment, stock, or personal property is reported.
Description: Responders check the scene, hold footage before it is overwritten, and tell IT straight away when a device that holds data is missing. The full investigation is handled by theft investigation.
In Scope: Immediate response to reported theft of equipment, stock, or personal property, including scene checks and footage holds.
Out of Scope: Insurance claims handling, HR disciplinary action, and the full theft investigation.
Deliverables: A theft report, a footage preservation request, and an asset loss notice to the owner and IT.
Prerequisites: An asset register, camera coverage where possible, and a reporting path for staff.
Lead Time: Standing response service. Engaged as soon as an incident is reported.
SLA Response Target: Priority physical incident attended within 15 minutes on staffed sites
SLA Resolution Target: Scene secured within 30 minutes / incident report filed within 1 business day
Escalation Path: An incident with injury, weapons, or loss of critical assets escalates to the security operations manager and emergency services immediately.
Threats Addressed: Loss of laptops holding data, stock shrinkage, and delayed reporting that loses evidence.
KPIs and Metrics: Thefts with footage preserved within 24 hours, recovered assets, and lost devices reported to IT the same day.

Name: Physical Scene Protection
Summary: Secure and preserve an incident scene until investigators, police, or safety teams arrive.
Description: Responders set a cordon, log everyone who enters, and photograph the scene before handover. The service protects evidence. It does not analyze it.
In Scope: Securing and preserving an incident scene until investigators, police, or safety teams arrive.
Out of Scope: Forensic analysis of the scene, medical treatment, and public statements.
Deliverables: A scene log of who entered and when, cordon photos, and a handover record to the investigator.
Prerequisites: Cordon supplies, a scene log template, and responders trained in scene preservation.
Lead Time: Standing response service. Engaged as soon as an incident is reported.
SLA Response Target: Priority physical incident attended within 15 minutes on staffed sites
SLA Resolution Target: Scene secured within 30 minutes / incident report filed within 1 business day
Escalation Path: An incident with injury, weapons, or loss of critical assets escalates to the security operations manager and emergency services immediately.
Threats Addressed: Contaminated evidence, unauthorized people entering a scene, and disputes over what happened.
KPIs and Metrics: Scenes with a complete entry log, time to cordon, and investigator acceptance of the handover.

Name: Evacuation Support
Summary: Support building evacuations with door release, assembly point control, and headcount reconciliation.
Description: Security works with floor wardens to clear buildings, control assembly points, and reconcile headcount against badge data. No one re-enters until the all-clear. Fire system design is out of scope.
In Scope: Security support for building evacuations, including door release, assembly point control, and headcount reconciliation.
Out of Scope: Fire system design, warden recruitment, and medical first aid.
Deliverables: An evacuation support procedure, an assembly point plan, and a post-evacuation headcount report.
Prerequisites: A site emergency plan, warden assignments, and a way to reconcile badge data with assembly headcount.
Lead Time: Site emergency plan coordination starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Emergency activation acknowledged within 5 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Accountability report to leadership within 60 minutes of evacuation
Escalation Path: An emergency with missing personnel, or failed alerting, escalates to the crisis management lead and emergency services immediately.
Threats Addressed: Unaccounted staff after evacuation, re-entry before all-clear, and theft during evacuations.
KPIs and Metrics: Time to complete headcount, unaccounted persons per drill, and drills completed on schedule.

Name: Shelter-in-Place Support
Summary: Run lockdown and shelter-in-place actions, including door locking and communication with sheltering staff.
Description: When a threat is outside or inside the building, the control center alerts staff, locks the doors it controls, and keeps sheltering staff informed. Police tactics and threat assessment belong to others.
In Scope: Lockdown and shelter-in-place actions, such as door locking, alerting, and communication with sheltering staff.
Out of Scope: Threat assessment of the external event, law enforcement tactics, and HR welfare follow-up.
Deliverables: A shelter-in-place procedure, a lockdown door list, and an after-drill improvement note.
Prerequisites: A mass notification tool, remotely lockable doors where possible, and trained floor wardens.
Lead Time: Site emergency plan coordination starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Emergency activation acknowledged within 5 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Accountability report to leadership within 60 minutes of evacuation
Escalation Path: An emergency with missing personnel, or failed alerting, escalates to the crisis management lead and emergency services immediately.
Threats Addressed: Active threats entering buildings, staff moving into danger, and confused alerting during lockdown.
KPIs and Metrics: Time from alert to lockdown, lockdown doors that failed, and staff reached by notification.

Name: Emergency-Services Liaison
Summary: Act as the single contact with police, fire, and ambulance services before and during incidents.
Description: A named liaison per site meets responders, provides site plans and access, and keeps a log during the incident. Familiarization visits are held before anything goes wrong.
In Scope: Single point of contact with police, fire, and ambulance services during incidents and in planning visits.
Out of Scope: Media liaison, regulatory reporting, and legal privilege decisions.
Deliverables: A liaison contact register, pre-incident site familiarization visits, and a liaison log per incident.
Prerequisites: Named liaison roles per site, site plans to share with responders, and access cards for responders.
Lead Time: Site emergency plan coordination starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Emergency activation acknowledged within 5 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Accountability report to leadership within 60 minutes of evacuation
Escalation Path: An emergency with missing personnel, or failed alerting, escalates to the crisis management lead and emergency services immediately.
Threats Addressed: Slow emergency service arrival, responders unable to enter buildings, and poor information at the scene.
KPIs and Metrics: Responder arrival-to-access time, familiarization visits completed, and liaison log completeness.

Name: Physical Incident Initial Reporting
Summary: Capture first reports of physical security incidents in a standard form.
Description: Staff, guards, and the control center report incidents through one form or portal, so investigators get the key facts and nothing is lost in email. Safety-only near misses go to EHS.
In Scope: Capturing first reports of physical security incidents from staff, guards, and the control center in a standard form.
Out of Scope: Investigating the incident, cyber incident reporting, and safety-only near misses.
Deliverables: A physical incident report form, a report register, and a monthly incident volume report by site.
Prerequisites: A reporting form or portal, incident categories, and awareness for staff on how to report.
Lead Time: Reporting channel available on day one. After-action reviews scheduled within 10 business days of closure.
SLA Response Target: Incident report acknowledged within 1 business hour
SLA Resolution Target: Initial report routed within 4 business hours / after-action review within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A report involving injury, weapons, or regulatory impact escalates to the security operations manager and legal the same day.
Threats Addressed: Unreported thefts and threats, missing details for investigators, and incidents lost in email.
KPIs and Metrics: Reports filed within 24 hours of the event, reports missing key fields, and reports by category.

Name: Physical Incident Escalation
Summary: Move serious physical incidents to the right leaders, legal, HR, and crisis teams by severity.
Description: A severity matrix decides who must be told and how fast, and the duty manager has authority to escalate. Notifications are logged so leadership is not surprised.
In Scope: Moving serious physical incidents to the right leaders, legal, HR, and crisis teams by defined severity criteria.
Out of Scope: Front-line response, investigation work, and crisis management decisions.
Deliverables: A severity and escalation matrix, an escalation log, and notification records for each serious incident.
Prerequisites: Defined severity criteria, a leadership contact list, and authority for the duty manager to escalate.
Lead Time: Reporting channel available on day one. After-action reviews scheduled within 10 business days of closure.
SLA Response Target: Serious incident escalated to the duty manager within 15 minutes of the report
SLA Resolution Target: Leadership and legal notified per the matrix within 1 hour
Escalation Path: If the duty manager cannot be reached within 15 minutes, the next level on the matrix and the security operations manager are called together.
Threats Addressed: Serious incidents handled at the wrong level, late legal awareness, and leadership surprised by events.
KPIs and Metrics: Escalations within target time, incidents reclassified after review, and missed notifications.

Name: Physical Incident After-Action Review
Summary: Review significant physical incidents to find the control failures and assign fixes.
Description: An independent facilitator walks through what happened, finds the root cause, and assigns owned improvements. The review is about controls, not blame. Disciplinary findings are out of scope.
In Scope: Structured review after significant physical incidents to find control failures and assign improvements.
Out of Scope: Disciplinary findings, legal liability opinions, and cyber post-incident review.
Deliverables: An after-action report, a root-cause summary, and an improvement action tracker with owners.
Prerequisites: Incident records, participant availability, and a facilitator independent of the incident.
Lead Time: Reporting channel available on day one. After-action reviews scheduled within 10 business days of closure.
SLA Response Target: Review scheduled within 5 business days of incident closure
SLA Resolution Target: After-action report issued within 15 business days of closure
Escalation Path: A review that finds a repeated root cause, or a fix that is still unfunded, escalates to the security operations manager and the site leader.
Threats Addressed: Repeat incidents from the same root cause, lessons lost after staff turnover, and unfunded fixes.
KPIs and Metrics: Reviews held within 15 business days, actions closed on time, and repeat incidents by root cause.

Name: Theft Investigation
Summary: Investigate thefts of company or employee property using footage, access logs, and interviews.
Description: Investigators work from a plan, build an evidence index, and report substantiated findings and recommended controls. Disciplinary and prosecution decisions stay with HR and legal.
In Scope: Fact-finding into thefts of company or employee property, including footage review, interviews, and access log analysis.
Out of Scope: Prosecution decisions, disciplinary outcomes, and insurance negotiation.
Deliverables: An investigation plan, an evidence index, and a findings report with recommended controls.
Prerequisites: A theft report, preserved footage and access logs, and legal approval for interviews.
Lead Time: Investigation scoped within 3 business days of an approved referral.
SLA Response Target: Referral acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Preliminary findings within 10 business days / final report within 30 business days
Escalation Path: An investigation that implicates a senior leader, or uncovers criminal activity, escalates to legal and the chief security officer.
Threats Addressed: Repeated internal theft, organized theft from stock areas, and loss of data-bearing devices.
KPIs and Metrics: Cases closed within 30 business days, cases with a substantiated finding, and recovered value.

Name: Unauthorized-Access Investigation
Summary: Find out how someone entered an area without authority, using badge, video, and witness evidence.
Description: Investigators reconstruct the entry and name the control that failed, such as tailgating, a shared badge, or faulty door hardware. Remediation is assigned to the control owner.
In Scope: Investigation of how someone entered an area without authority, combining badge, video, and witness evidence.
Out of Scope: Cyber account compromise investigation, HR discipline, and perimeter redesign.
Deliverables: A reconstruction of the entry, a list of failed controls, and a findings report with remediation.
Prerequisites: Badge system logs, camera footage, and the incident report with times.
Lead Time: Investigation scoped within 3 business days of an approved referral.
SLA Response Target: Referral acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Preliminary findings within 10 business days / final report within 30 business days
Escalation Path: An investigation that implicates a senior leader, or uncovers criminal activity, escalates to legal and the chief security officer.
Threats Addressed: Tailgating rings, shared badges, insider assistance, and failed door hardware.
KPIs and Metrics: Root cause identified per case, control fixes completed, and repeat entries by method.

Name: Property-Damage Investigation
Summary: Investigate vandalism, sabotage, and suspicious damage to facilities and security equipment.
Description: Investigators assess the damage, gather evidence, and decide whether it was accidental or deliberate. Repairs and insurance claims are handled by facilities and risk.
In Scope: Investigation of vandalism, sabotage, and suspicious damage to facilities, vehicles, and security equipment.
Out of Scope: Repair of the damage, insurance adjusting, and safety engineering assessments.
Deliverables: A damage assessment record, an evidence index, and a findings report that distinguishes accident from intent.
Prerequisites: Photos of the damage, maintenance records, and access logs for the area.
Lead Time: Investigation scoped within 3 business days of an approved referral.
SLA Response Target: Referral acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Preliminary findings within 10 business days / final report within 30 business days
Escalation Path: An investigation that implicates a senior leader, or uncovers criminal activity, escalates to legal and the chief security officer.
Threats Addressed: Sabotage of security equipment, vandalism by former staff, and damage covering up theft.
KPIs and Metrics: Cases with a determined cause, time to findings, and repeat damage at the same location.

Name: Physical Evidence Collection
Summary: Collect, photograph, bag, and label physical evidence and footage from incident scenes.
Description: Trained collectors use evidence kits and a case number from case intake, so evidence holds up with police, HR, or courts. Laboratory and digital forensics are outside this service.
In Scope: Collecting, photographing, bagging, and labeling physical evidence and footage exports from incident scenes.
Out of Scope: Laboratory forensic analysis, digital forensic imaging of devices, and police evidence handling.
Deliverables: An evidence collection procedure, labeled evidence items with photos, and a collection record per case.
Prerequisites: Evidence kits, trained collectors, and a case number from case intake.
Lead Time: Evidence intake available on request. New storage location certified within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Evidence intake acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Evidence logged and sealed within 1 business day of collection
Escalation Path: Broken seals, missing items, or a chain-of-custody gap escalates to the investigations lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Lost or contaminated evidence, unprovable facts in disputes, and evidence rejected by police or courts.
KPIs and Metrics: Items collected with a complete record, evidence challenged in review, and time from incident to collection.

Name: Physical Evidence Chain of Custody
Summary: Record every transfer of each evidence item from collection to release or destruction.
Description: Each item has a unique identifier and a custody form, and every handover is signed and timed. An annual audit checks for gaps that would make evidence unusable.
In Scope: Recording every transfer of each evidence item from collection to release or destruction.
Out of Scope: Evidence analysis, legal hold decisions, and storage facility management.
Deliverables: A chain-of-custody form per item, a transfer log, and an annual custody audit report.
Prerequisites: Unique evidence identifiers, custody forms, and named custodians.
Lead Time: Evidence intake available on request. New storage location certified within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Evidence intake acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Evidence logged and sealed within 1 business day of collection
Escalation Path: Broken seals, missing items, or a chain-of-custody gap escalates to the investigations lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Broken custody that makes evidence unusable, tampering claims, and missing items.
KPIs and Metrics: Items with an unbroken custody record, audit exceptions, and transfers recorded within 1 hour.

Name: Physical Evidence Storage
Summary: Store evidence in locked, access-controlled lockers or rooms with retention and release rules.
Description: Only named custodians can enter the evidence room. Items are held to a legal retention standard and reconciled twice a year. Digital forensic images are stored elsewhere.
In Scope: Secure storage of evidence in locked, access-controlled lockers or rooms with retention and release rules.
Out of Scope: Storage of digital forensic images, records management for business documents, and police property rooms.
Deliverables: An evidence room access log, a retention and release schedule, and a semi-annual inventory reconciliation.
Prerequisites: A lockable evidence room or locker, restricted access, and a retention standard approved by legal.
Lead Time: Evidence intake available on request. New storage location certified within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Evidence intake acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Evidence logged and sealed within 1 business day of collection
Escalation Path: Broken seals, missing items, or a chain-of-custody gap escalates to the investigations lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Theft or tampering of stored evidence, early destruction, and evidence kept beyond legal need.
KPIs and Metrics: Inventory reconciliation accuracy, items past retention, and unauthorized room entries.

Name: Physical Investigation Case Intake
Summary: Receive, screen, and open investigation cases from incident reports, hotlines, and referrals.
Description: Referrals are screened against written criteria, opened as cases, and assigned to an investigator with no conflict of interest. Declined referrals are recorded with a reason.
In Scope: Receiving, screening, and opening investigation cases from incident reports, hotlines, and management referrals.
Out of Scope: Running the investigation, HR grievance processes, and cyber incident ticketing.
Deliverables: A case intake form, a screening decision record, and an open-case register with assigned investigators.
Prerequisites: A case management tool or register, screening criteria, and a referral path from reporting channels.
Lead Time: Case opened within 1 business day of an accepted referral.
SLA Response Target: Referral triaged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Case assigned within 2 business days / findings report issued within 5 business days of investigation close
Escalation Path: A case that ages past 60 days, or a conflict of interest, escalates to the investigations lead.
Threats Addressed: Serious allegations not investigated, duplicate cases, and conflicts of interest in assignment.
KPIs and Metrics: Referrals screened within 1 business day, cases declined with reasons, and open cases per investigator.

Name: Physical Investigation Documentation
Summary: Keep interview notes, evidence references, and activity logs to a standard that survives review.
Description: Case files follow a template, sit in a restricted location, and get a quality check at closure. Final reports and legal privilege decisions are separate.
In Scope: Interview notes, evidence references, and activity logs kept to a standard that supports later review or legal use.
Out of Scope: Writing the final report, legal privilege decisions, and personnel file updates.
Deliverables: A case file standard, a case activity log, and a quality check record per closed case.
Prerequisites: A secure case file location, documentation templates, and investigator training.
Lead Time: Case opened within 1 business day of an accepted referral.
SLA Response Target: Referral triaged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Case assigned within 2 business days / findings report issued within 5 business days of investigation close
Escalation Path: A case that ages past 60 days, or a conflict of interest, escalates to the investigations lead.
Threats Addressed: Unsupported findings, lost interview records, and case files exposed to the wrong people.
KPIs and Metrics: Case files passing quality check, documentation gaps found in review, and access exceptions.

Name: Physical Investigation Findings Reporting
Summary: Issue final investigation reports with substantiated facts, conclusions, and recommended changes.
Description: Reports state what the evidence supports and recommend control or policy fixes, which are then tracked. Leadership receives a quarterly trend summary. Disciplinary decisions stay with management.
In Scope: Final investigation reports with substantiated facts, conclusions, and recommended control or policy changes.
Out of Scope: Deciding disciplinary or legal action, public statements, and cyber incident reporting.
Deliverables: A findings report, a recommendation tracker, and a quarterly investigation trend summary for leadership.
Prerequisites: A completed case file, legal review where required, and a named decision-maker for each case.
Lead Time: Case opened within 1 business day of an accepted referral.
SLA Response Target: Referral triaged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Case assigned within 2 business days / findings report issued within 5 business days of investigation close
Escalation Path: A case that ages past 60 days, or a conflict of interest, escalates to the investigations lead.
Threats Addressed: Repeated incidents because findings were not acted on, and biased or unsupported conclusions.
KPIs and Metrics: Reports issued on time, recommendations implemented, and findings challenged after issue.

Name: Access-Control System Design
Summary: Design door readers, controllers, locks, and access system integration for new sites and renovations.
Description: Security turns architectural drawings into a door schedule, a system architecture, and reader and lock choices that meet the access standard. Installation and fire egress sign-off belong to others.
In Scope: Design of door readers, controllers, locks, and access system integration for new sites and renovations.
Out of Scope: Installing the hardware, IT network design, and fire egress compliance sign-off.
Deliverables: A door schedule with reader and lock types, a system architecture diagram, and a design review record.
Prerequisites: Architectural drawings, site zoning plan, and the corporate access control standard.
Lead Time: Design engagement starts within 15 business days of a funded project.
SLA Response Target: Design request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Concept design within 20 business days / final design review within 10 business days of drawings
Escalation Path: A design that leaves a critical entrance uncovered, or needs unbudgeted hardware, escalates to the facility security manager and the project sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Weak readers that can be cloned, unmonitored doors, and access systems that fail open.
KPIs and Metrics: Designs meeting the access standard, change orders caused by design gaps, and doors covered by readers.

Name: Surveillance System Design
Summary: Design camera positions, recording capacity, video network, and retention for new sites and upgrades.
Description: Designs start from the coverage plan and size storage to the retention standard. Camera networks are kept separate from corporate networks. Installation and monitoring staffing are separate.
In Scope: Design of camera positions, recording capacity, video network, and retention for new sites and upgrades.
Out of Scope: Installation, network hardware purchasing, and live monitoring staffing.
Deliverables: A camera layout drawing, a storage and retention calculation, and a camera specification sheet.
Prerequisites: Floor plans, the coverage planning report, and the retention standard.
Lead Time: Design engagement starts within 15 business days of a funded project.
SLA Response Target: Design request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Concept design within 20 business days / final design review within 10 business days of drawings
Escalation Path: A design that leaves a critical entrance uncovered, or needs unbudgeted hardware, escalates to the facility security manager and the project sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Coverage gaps at critical areas, insufficient recording retention, and unsegmented camera networks.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical areas covered at design review, storage sized for retention target, and design rework items.

Name: Alarm System Design
Summary: Design intrusion, duress, and panic alarm zones, panels, and monitoring links for each site.
Description: Every entry point is covered, duress buttons reach the control center, and panels use a dual communication path. Fire and life-safety alarm design is out of scope.
In Scope: Design of intrusion, duress, and panic alarm zones, panels, and monitoring connections for sites.
Out of Scope: Fire and life-safety alarm design, installation work, and monitoring contract negotiation.
Deliverables: An alarm zone drawing, a panel and communication path design, and an arming schedule recommendation.
Prerequisites: Floor plans, zoning plan, and the monitoring center's connection requirements.
Lead Time: Design engagement starts within 15 business days of a funded project.
SLA Response Target: Design request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Concept design within 20 business days / final design review within 10 business days of drawings
Escalation Path: A design that leaves a critical entrance uncovered, or needs unbudgeted hardware, escalates to the facility security manager and the project sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Unprotected entry points, alarm signal loss, and duress buttons that do not reach the control center.
KPIs and Metrics: Entry points with alarm coverage, dual-path communication designs, and design defects found in testing.

Name: Physical Security System Installation
Summary: Coordinate installers, schedules, site access, and quality checks for security system installations.
Description: Security keeps installers on schedule, controls their site access, and tracks the punch list to closure. Doors are never left unsecured overnight during the work.
In Scope: Coordinating installers, schedules, access, and quality checks for physical security system installations.
Out of Scope: Electrical contracting, general construction management, and design changes.
Deliverables: An installation schedule, daily progress notes, and a punch list tracked to closure.
Prerequisites: An approved design, a selected installer, and site access arrangements.
Lead Time: Installation scheduling starts within 10 business days of an approved design.
SLA Response Target: Installer issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Punch list items closed within 10 business days of acceptance testing
Escalation Path: An installation that will miss the site opening date, or leaves doors unsecured overnight, escalates to the facility security manager and the project manager.
Threats Addressed: Doors left unsecured during works, installers with uncontrolled access, and poor-quality cabling.
KPIs and Metrics: Installations finished on schedule, punch items open at handover, and quality defects found.

Name: Physical Security System Acceptance Testing
Summary: Test installed access, video, and alarm systems against the design before acceptance and payment.
Description: Every device is tested against a written plan and signed off. Defects go back to the installer before the system is accepted. Ongoing maintenance testing is a separate service.
In Scope: Testing installed access, video, and alarm systems against the design before acceptance and payment.
Out of Scope: Ongoing maintenance testing, network penetration testing, and design approval.
Deliverables: An acceptance test plan, a signed test record per device, and a defect list for the installer.
Prerequisites: An approved design, installed and powered systems, and installer presence during tests.
Lead Time: Installation scheduling starts within 10 business days of an approved design.
SLA Response Target: Installer issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Punch list items closed within 10 business days of acceptance testing
Escalation Path: An installation that will miss the site opening date, or leaves doors unsecured overnight, escalates to the facility security manager and the project manager.
Threats Addressed: Accepting systems that do not work, hidden defects, and unsecured default settings.
KPIs and Metrics: Devices passing first test, defects found before acceptance, and retests required.

Name: Physical Security System Commissioning
Summary: Bring tested systems into live operation with monitoring, documentation, and trained operators.
Description: Commissioning connects the system to the control center, collects as-built drawings, trains operators and maintainers, and hands over to maintenance. Warranty claims stay with the project.
In Scope: Bringing tested systems into live operation with monitoring, documentation, training, and handover to maintenance.
Out of Scope: Installer warranty claims, design changes, and daily operation of the control center.
Deliverables: A commissioning checklist, as-built drawings, and an operator and maintainer training record.
Prerequisites: Passed acceptance tests, a maintenance contract, and control center readiness.
Lead Time: Installation scheduling starts within 10 business days of an approved design.
SLA Response Target: Installer issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Punch list items closed within 10 business days of acceptance testing
Escalation Path: An installation that will miss the site opening date, or leaves doors unsecured overnight, escalates to the facility security manager and the project manager.
Threats Addressed: Systems going live without monitoring, missing as-built records, and untrained operators.
KPIs and Metrics: Systems commissioned with full documentation, time from acceptance to live, and post-launch faults.

Name: Physical Security Preventive Maintenance
Summary: Service readers, locks, cameras, panels, batteries, and recorders on a schedule to prevent failures.
Description: A maintenance plan covers every device, with a service record per visit and a quarterly compliance report. Unplanned repairs go through fault diagnosis.
In Scope: Scheduled servicing of readers, locks, cameras, alarm panels, batteries, and recorders to prevent failure.
Out of Scope: Unplanned fault repair, system upgrades, and building services maintenance.
Deliverables: A preventive maintenance schedule, a service record per device, and a quarterly maintenance compliance report.
Prerequisites: A device inventory, a maintenance contract, and access arrangements for maintainers.
Lead Time: New device added to the maintenance plan within 10 business days of commissioning.
SLA Response Target: Critical security system fault acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Critical fault fixed within 8 hours / standard fault within 3 business days
Escalation Path: A fault that disables access control or recording at a critical site escalates to the security systems lead and the maintainer account manager.
Threats Addressed: Battery failures during outages, worn locks failing open, and degraded cameras.
KPIs and Metrics: Maintenance visits completed on schedule, faults found during maintenance, and device age profile.

Name: Physical Security System Fault Diagnosis
Summary: Diagnose and repair faults in access control, video, and alarm systems and record the root cause.
Description: Faults are prioritized by what they disable, and critical doors and cameras are fixed first. Repeat faults per device are tracked so failing hardware gets replaced.
In Scope: Diagnosing and repairing faults in access control, video, and alarm systems and recording root cause.
Out of Scope: Planned upgrades, design changes, and IT network fault diagnosis.
Deliverables: Fault tickets with root cause, a repeat-fault report, and a spare parts usage record.
Prerequisites: A fault reporting channel, maintainer support, and spare parts for critical devices.
Lead Time: New device added to the maintenance plan within 10 business days of commissioning.
SLA Response Target: Critical security system fault acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Critical fault fixed within 8 hours / standard fault within 3 business days
Escalation Path: A fault that disables access control or recording at a critical site escalates to the security systems lead and the maintainer account manager.
Threats Addressed: Prolonged loss of door control, camera blackouts, and alarm communication failures.
KPIs and Metrics: Mean time to repair, repeat faults per device, and critical faults past SLA.

Name: Physical Security System Upgrades
Summary: Plan and deliver firmware, software, and hardware upgrades for physical security platforms.
Description: Upgrades keep platforms on vendor-supported versions and come with a rollback plan and a post-upgrade check. End-of-life devices are tracked to replacement.
In Scope: Planning and delivering firmware, software, and hardware upgrades for physical security platforms.
