Out of Scope: New site design, end-user badge replacement, and IT server patching outside security systems.
Deliverables: An upgrade plan with rollback, a change record, and a post-upgrade verification report.
Prerequisites: A supported version roadmap from the vendor, a test environment or pilot site, and change approval.
Lead Time: New device added to the maintenance plan within 10 business days of commissioning.
SLA Response Target: Critical security system fault acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Critical fault fixed within 8 hours / standard fault within 3 business days
Escalation Path: A fault that disables access control or recording at a critical site escalates to the security systems lead and the maintainer account manager.
Threats Addressed: Unsupported platforms with known flaws, upgrades that break door control, and vendor end of life.
KPIs and Metrics: Platforms on supported versions, upgrades without unplanned outage, and end-of-life devices remaining.

Name: Physical Security Site Surveys
Summary: Survey a facility on site to document its current security posture, assets, and controls.
Description: Surveyors walk the site, photograph controls, and list gaps in priority order. Surveys are most useful for new, acquired, or changed sites. Detailed engineering design is a separate service.
In Scope: On-site surveys that document the current security posture, assets, and controls of a facility.
Out of Scope: Detailed engineering design, cyber assessments, and environmental health and safety audits.
Deliverables: A site survey report, a photo record, and a prioritized list of control gaps.
Prerequisites: Site access, a site contact, and current floor plans.
Lead Time: Assessment scheduled within 20 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Assessment request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days of site visit
Escalation Path: A finding that leaves people or critical assets exposed escalates to the site leader and the chief security officer within 1 business day.
Threats Addressed: Unknown security gaps at new or acquired sites and controls that exist only on paper.
KPIs and Metrics: Sites surveyed on schedule, gaps found per survey, and gaps closed within 6 months.

Name: Physical Security Vulnerability Assessments
Summary: Assess how a facility could realistically be attacked and rate each scenario's likelihood and impact.
Description: Starting from the survey and the local threat profile, the assessment rates scenarios such as forced entry, insider sabotage, and workplace violence and recommends treatment.
In Scope: Threat-based assessment of how a facility could be attacked and the likelihood and impact of each scenario.
Out of Scope: Penetration testing of the site, cyber vulnerability scanning, and insurance underwriting.
Deliverables: A vulnerability assessment report, a risk rating per scenario, and treatment recommendations.
Prerequisites: Site survey results, a threat profile for the location, and asset criticality.
Lead Time: Assessment scheduled within 20 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Assessment request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days of site visit
Escalation Path: A finding that leaves people or critical assets exposed escalates to the site leader and the chief security officer within 1 business day.
Threats Addressed: Forced entry, insider sabotage, workplace violence, and theft of high-value items.
KPIs and Metrics: High-risk scenarios with treatment, assessments within cycle, and residual risk accepted by owners.

Name: Physical Protective-Measure Reviews
Summary: Review whether existing protective measures still fit the threat, the site, and the standard.
Description: Each measure is marked keep, change, or retire, with costs for changes. Measures are not removed without review, and money is not spent on controls that no longer deter.
In Scope: Reviewing whether existing protective measures still match the threat, the site use, and the standard.
Out of Scope: Designing new systems, guard contract renewal, and capital budget approval.
Deliverables: A protective measure review report, a keep-change-retire list, and cost estimates for changes.
Prerequisites: An inventory of current measures, incident history, and the current threat profile.
Lead Time: Assessment scheduled within 20 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Assessment request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days of site visit
Escalation Path: A finding that leaves people or critical assets exposed escalates to the site leader and the chief security officer within 1 business day.
Threats Addressed: Outdated measures that no longer deter, wasted spend, and controls removed without review.
KPIs and Metrics: Measures reviewed on cycle, retirements approved, and incidents at reviewed sites.

Name: Physical Access-Control Testing
Summary: Test readers, locks, anti-passback, and badge revocation with controlled test credentials.
Description: Testers try revoked and out-of-scope test badges door by door and record what works that should not. Failed doors go on a remediation list. Covert third-party penetration tests are separate.
In Scope: Testing readers, locks, anti-passback, and badge revocation by attempting controlled access with test credentials.
Out of Scope: Covert penetration testing by third parties, employee discipline, and lock hardware supply.
Deliverables: A test plan, door-by-door results, and a remediation list for failed doors.
Prerequisites: Test badges, an approved test window, and notice to the control center.
Lead Time: Test or exercise scheduled within 15 business days of plan approval.
SLA Response Target: Test scheduling request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Test report within 10 business days of the test
Escalation Path: A test that finds a critical control does not work escalates to the facility security manager the same day.
Threats Addressed: Revoked badges that still work, doors that fail open, and readers that accept cloned cards.
KPIs and Metrics: Doors passing tests, revoked-badge test pass rate, and failed doors fixed within 10 days.

Name: Physical Alarm Testing
Summary: Walk-test sensors and test duress buttons to confirm alarms reach the control center correctly.
Description: Each zone is tested on a cycle with the monitoring center, and dead sensors or mislabeled zones are repaired. Fire alarm testing follows its own regime.
In Scope: Walk tests, signal tests, and duress button tests to confirm alarms reach the control center correctly.
Out of Scope: Fire alarm testing, alarm system design, and control center staffing.
Deliverables: A test schedule, signal-received records per zone, and a failed-zone repair list.
Prerequisites: Coordination with the monitoring center, test mode procedures, and maintainer support.
Lead Time: Test or exercise scheduled within 15 business days of plan approval.
SLA Response Target: Test scheduling request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Test report within 10 business days of the test
Escalation Path: A test that finds a critical control does not work escalates to the facility security manager the same day.
Threats Addressed: Alarms that never reach the control center, dead duress buttons, and mislabeled zones.
KPIs and Metrics: Zones tested per cycle, signal success rate, and failed zones repaired within target.

Name: Physical Security Response Exercises
Summary: Run drills for intruder, lockdown, evacuation, and alarm response with guards and site staff.
Description: Exercises test the written procedures with the people who would use them and end with owned improvement actions. Cyber tabletop exercises are a separate service.
In Scope: Drills and exercises for intruder, lockdown, evacuation, and alarm response with guards and site staff.
Out of Scope: Cyber tabletop exercises, crisis executive simulations, and real incident response.
Deliverables: An exercise plan, an exercise report with observations, and improvement actions.
Prerequisites: Exercise objectives, participant availability, and site leadership support.
Lead Time: Test or exercise scheduled within 15 business days of plan approval.
SLA Response Target: Test scheduling request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Test report within 10 business days of the test
Escalation Path: A test that finds a critical control does not work escalates to the facility security manager the same day.
Threats Addressed: Slow or confused response in real incidents and untested procedures.
KPIs and Metrics: Exercises run on schedule, objectives met, and improvement actions closed.

Name: Structured-Data Discovery
Summary: Scan databases, warehouses, and SaaS tables on a schedule to find regulated and sensitive fields.
Description: Scanners use read-only accounts and an approved data element dictionary to tag sensitive columns. Each run produces a delta, so new copies of customer or payment data are seen quickly. Fixing schemas stays with the data teams.
In Scope: Scheduled scanning of databases, data warehouses, and SaaS tables for regulated and sensitive data elements.
Out of Scope: Fixing data quality, redesigning schemas, and scanning unstructured file shares.
Deliverables: A structured data inventory by store and table, a sensitive column report, and a delta report after each scan.
Prerequisites: Read-only service accounts for target databases, an approved data element dictionary, and a scanning tool.
Lead Time: New data store added to discovery scans within 10 business days of connection approval.
SLA Response Target: Scan request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Initial discovery results within 10 business days of scan start
Escalation Path: Discovery of restricted data in an unapproved or public location escalates to the data owner and the data protection lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Unknown copies of customer or payment data, shadow analytics tables, and regulated fields in unexpected systems.
KPIs and Metrics: Data stores scanned on schedule, sensitive columns found without an owner, and false-positive rate per scan.

Name: Unstructured-Data Discovery
Summary: Find sensitive documents across file shares, collaboration sites, mailboxes, and cloud drives.
Description: Connectors scan repositories for sensitive files and flag folders that are shared too widely. Findings go to a named owner per business unit. Records classification and eDiscovery are separate.
In Scope: Scanning file shares, collaboration sites, mailboxes, and cloud drives for sensitive documents and files.
Out of Scope: Records management classification of business documents, legal eDiscovery, and database scanning.
Deliverables: An unstructured data findings report, a list of overexposed folders, and recommended owners per location.
Prerequisites: Connectors to file and collaboration platforms, classification patterns, and a remediation contact per business unit.
Lead Time: New data store added to discovery scans within 10 business days of connection approval.
SLA Response Target: Scan request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Initial discovery results within 10 business days of scan start
Escalation Path: Discovery of restricted data in an unapproved or public location escalates to the data owner and the data protection lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Sensitive spreadsheets shared broadly, exports left in personal drives, and stale documents holding personal data.
KPIs and Metrics: Repositories covered, sensitive files with open sharing, and findings remediated within 30 days.

Name: Sensitive-Data Discovery
Summary: Hunt for the highest-risk data types, such as credentials, card numbers, and health records, wherever they sit.
Description: Targeted patterns and validation rules find secrets, cardholder data, and health records outside approved systems. Validated hits go to the owner within days, not at the next audit.
In Scope: Targeted discovery of the highest-risk data types, such as credentials, payment card numbers, health records, and secrets.
Out of Scope: General inventory of all data, data quality tuning, and payment network compliance attestation.
Deliverables: A sensitive data hit report, validated findings with location and owner, and a monthly trend of new exposures.
Prerequisites: Detection patterns for each sensitive type, validation rules to reduce noise, and scanner access to target stores.
Lead Time: New data store added to discovery scans within 10 business days of connection approval.
SLA Response Target: Scan request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Initial discovery results within 10 business days of scan start
Escalation Path: Discovery of restricted data in an unapproved or public location escalates to the data owner and the data protection lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Cardholder data outside the payment environment, exposed secrets in files, and health data in shared folders.
KPIs and Metrics: Validated sensitive hits per month, time from detection to owner notice, and repeat exposures per owner.

Name: Storage-Location Mapping
Summary: Record where each important dataset is stored, including regions, platforms, backups, and replicas.
Description: The map shows every copy of a dataset, including backups and replicas, and the region it sits in. Unowned copies are listed for cleanup. Residency legal decisions are made elsewhere.
In Scope: Mapping where each important dataset is stored, including regions, platforms, backups, and replicas.
Out of Scope: Data residency legal decisions, migration of the data, and capacity planning.
Deliverables: A storage location register per dataset, a region and hosting summary, and a list of unknown or unowned copies.
Prerequisites: An application inventory, platform owner contacts, and discovery scan results.
Lead Time: Mapping engagement starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Mapping request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft map delivered within 15 business days of workshop completion
Escalation Path: A data flow that sends restricted data to an unapproved destination escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead.
Threats Addressed: Data stored in unapproved regions, forgotten replicas, and backups outside protection standards.
KPIs and Metrics: Datasets with a mapped location, copies with no owner, and map accuracy at spot check.

Name: Data-Flow Mapping
Summary: Diagram how sensitive data moves between applications, teams, vendors, and environments.
Description: Flow maps are built with process owners and kept current after change. They show where data travels unencrypted or ends up in test environments. Integration build work is not included.
In Scope: Diagrams of how sensitive data moves between applications, teams, vendors, and environments.
Out of Scope: Network architecture design, integration build work, and data quality lineage.
Deliverables: Data flow diagrams per business process, a list of flows lacking protection, and a change log for the maps.
Prerequisites: Process owner interviews, an integration inventory, and the data classification standard.
Lead Time: Mapping engagement starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Mapping request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft map delivered within 15 business days of workshop completion
Escalation Path: A data flow that sends restricted data to an unapproved destination escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead.
Threats Addressed: Unprotected transfers, data leaking into test environments, and undocumented vendor feeds.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical processes with a current flow map, flows without encryption, and maps updated after change.

Name: External-Sharing Mapping
Summary: Keep an inventory of data shared with partners, vendors, and regulators, with channel and frequency.
Description: The register records what goes to whom, how, and under which agreement. Sharing without a contract, or sharing that outlived one, is flagged for review.
In Scope: Inventory of data shared with partners, vendors, and regulators, including channel, frequency, and data types.
Out of Scope: Contract negotiation, partner onboarding approval, and vendor security assessment.
Deliverables: An external sharing register, a list of sharing without agreements, and a quarterly sharing change report.
Prerequisites: Vendor and partner lists, procurement contract data, and integration owner contacts.
Lead Time: Mapping engagement starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Mapping request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft map delivered within 15 business days of workshop completion
Escalation Path: A data flow that sends restricted data to an unapproved destination escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead.
Threats Addressed: Unapproved disclosure to third parties, sharing that outlives a contract, and oversharing beyond need.
KPIs and Metrics: Sharing arrangements with a mapped agreement, unknown shares found, and register entries reviewed.

Name: Data Owner Assignment
Summary: Name an accountable business owner for each important data domain and record their acceptance.
Description: Every critical dataset gets an owner who decides access, retention, and risk, and who signs to accept the role. Unowned datasets are reported until someone takes them.
In Scope: Naming an accountable business owner for each important data domain and dataset and recording acceptance.
Out of Scope: Day-to-day data handling, IT administration of the platforms, and org chart changes.
Deliverables: A data owner register, signed owner acceptance records, and an unowned dataset report.
Prerequisites: A dataset inventory, executive sponsorship, and a defined owner role description.
Lead Time: Ownership assignments for a new data domain within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Ownership question acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Owner confirmed and recorded within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A critical dataset with no accepted owner after 30 days escalates to the data governance council.
Threats Addressed: Orphaned data with no decision-maker, conflicting access approvals, and unmanaged retention.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical datasets with an accepted owner, unowned datasets aged over 30 days, and owner changes recorded.

Name: Stewardship Responsibilities
Summary: Define and assign data steward duties for classification, quality, access review, and handling.
Description: Stewards do the day-to-day work owners delegate: classifying data, checking access, and applying handling rules. A responsibility matrix makes clear who does what in each domain.
In Scope: Defining and assigning data steward duties for classification, quality, access review, and handling standards.
Out of Scope: Owner-level risk decisions, data engineering work, and security tool operation.
Deliverables: A steward responsibility matrix, steward assignments per domain, and steward onboarding material.
Prerequisites: Data owners in place, a governance operating model, and steward capacity agreed with managers.
Lead Time: Ownership assignments for a new data domain within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Ownership question acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Owner confirmed and recorded within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A critical dataset with no accepted owner after 30 days escalates to the data governance council.
Threats Addressed: Inconsistent classification, unreviewed access, and unclear handling decisions.
KPIs and Metrics: Domains with an active steward, steward tasks completed on time, and steward vacancy duration.

Name: Handling Accountability
Summary: Hold owners, stewards, and users accountable for handling rules through attestation and reporting.
Description: An annual attestation confirms people know and follow the handling rules for their data. Breaches are traced to a domain and an owner so repeat problems are visible.
In Scope: Making owners, stewards, and users accountable for following handling rules through attestations and reporting.
Out of Scope: HR discipline, legal sanctions, and technical enforcement controls.
Deliverables: An annual handling attestation, a non-compliance report by domain, and an accountability section in the data policy.
Prerequisites: Published handling rules, a list of users per domain, and an attestation tool.
Lead Time: Ownership assignments for a new data domain within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Ownership question acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Owner confirmed and recorded within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A critical dataset with no accepted owner after 30 days escalates to the data governance council.
Threats Addressed: Careless handling by trusted users, unclear responsibility after incidents, and ignored handling rules.
KPIs and Metrics: Attestation completion rate, handling breaches traced to an owner, and repeat breaches by domain.

Name: Data Storage Handling Requirements
Summary: Set where and how each classification may be stored, including approved platforms and encryption.
Description: The standard lists approved platforms per classification and the controls each requires. Anything outside it needs a recorded exception. Discovery scans show where reality differs.
In Scope: Rules for where and how each classification may be stored, including approved platforms, encryption, and removable media.
Out of Scope: Selecting storage products, running backups, and records retention schedules.
Deliverables: A storage handling standard by classification, an approved platform list, and an exception register.
Prerequisites: The data classification standard, an inventory of approved storage platforms, and owner input.
Lead Time: Handling guidance question answered within 5 business days. New requirement drafted within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Guidance request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Written requirement or exception decision within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A business need that cannot meet a handling requirement escalates to the data protection lead for a formal exception.
Threats Addressed: Restricted data on personal devices, unencrypted storage, and use of unsanctioned cloud storage.
KPIs and Metrics: Platforms mapped to classifications, storage exceptions open, and violations found by discovery scans.

Name: Data Transmission Handling Requirements
Summary: Set rules for sending data by email, file transfer, API, and physical media for each classification.
Description: Staff get short guidance on how to send each type of data safely and which tools are approved. Misdirected email and personal file-sharing tools are the main problems this addresses.
In Scope: Rules for sending data by email, file transfer, API, and physical media for each classification.
Out of Scope: Building transfer tools, network encryption configuration, and partner contract terms.
Deliverables: A transmission handling standard, an approved transfer method list, and quick-reference guidance for staff.
Prerequisites: The classification standard, an inventory of transfer tools, and messaging platform settings.
Lead Time: Handling guidance question answered within 5 business days. New requirement drafted within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Guidance request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Written requirement or exception decision within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A business need that cannot meet a handling requirement escalates to the data protection lead for a formal exception.
Threats Addressed: Sensitive files emailed in clear text, use of personal file-sharing tools, and data sent to wrong recipients.
KPIs and Metrics: Transfers via approved methods, misdirected email incidents, and transmission exceptions granted.

Name: Data Permitted-Use Requirements
Summary: Define which purposes each data domain may be used for, including analytics, testing, and AI training.
Description: A permitted-use matrix gives analytics and engineering teams a quick answer. New uses go to a decision forum with the data owner. Privacy lawful basis is handled by the privacy team.
In Scope: Rules that define which purposes each data domain may be used for, including analytics, testing, and AI training.
Out of Scope: Privacy lawful basis determinations, analytics model approval, and contract drafting.
Deliverables: A permitted-use matrix per data domain, a use-request decision log, and guidance for analytics teams.
Prerequisites: Data owners, processing purposes documented in privacy records, and a decision forum.
Lead Time: Handling guidance question answered within 5 business days. New requirement drafted within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Guidance request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Written requirement or exception decision within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A business need that cannot meet a handling requirement escalates to the data protection lead for a formal exception.
Threats Addressed: Function creep, use of customer data for unapproved analytics, and production data in test systems.
KPIs and Metrics: Use requests decided within SLA, uses found outside the matrix, and exceptions renewed.

Name: Data Exposure Assessment
Summary: Assess how exposed a dataset or system is through access, sharing, network paths, and public links.
Description: The assessment combines discovery, sharing settings, and audit logs into a ranked list of exposures with quick fixes. Critical exposures go straight to the owner. It is not a penetration test.
In Scope: Assessing how exposed a dataset or system is through access, sharing, network paths, and public links.
Out of Scope: Penetration testing, fixing the exposure, and legal breach determinations.
Deliverables: An exposure assessment report, a ranked exposure list, and recommended quick fixes.
Prerequisites: Discovery and mapping results, platform audit logs, and read access to sharing settings.
Lead Time: Assessment starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Assessment request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days of fieldwork
Escalation Path: A critical exposure of restricted data found during assessment escalates to the data owner and the incident commander the same day.
Threats Addressed: Public links to sensitive files, over-permissioned groups, and internet-reachable data stores.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical exposures found, exposures closed within 30 days, and assessments completed on schedule.

Name: Data Protection-Gap Assessment
Summary: Compare a data domain's current protections with the classification and handling standards.
Description: Assessors check each required control against evidence and rate every gap. The result shows where protection is assumed rather than real, before an auditor finds it.
In Scope: Comparing a data domain's current protections against the classification and handling standards.
Out of Scope: Implementing new controls, audit certification, and privacy compliance review.
Deliverables: A gap assessment report, a control-by-control gap list, and a risk rating per gap.
Prerequisites: Handling standards, owner and steward availability, and evidence of current controls.
Lead Time: Assessment starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Assessment request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days of fieldwork
Escalation Path: A critical exposure of restricted data found during assessment escalates to the data owner and the incident commander the same day.
Threats Addressed: Controls assumed but not in place, inconsistent protection across copies, and audit findings.
KPIs and Metrics: Gaps per domain, high-risk gaps open past target, and domains assessed per year.

Name: Data Protection Remediation Planning
Summary: Turn exposure and gap findings into an owned, sequenced, and funded remediation plan.
Description: Findings become actions with owners, dates, and cost estimates, tracked monthly. The service plans the work and reports progress. Delivery and risk acceptance stay with the owners.
In Scope: Turning exposure and gap findings into a funded, owned, and sequenced remediation plan.
Out of Scope: Doing the remediation work, budget approval, and risk acceptance decisions.
Deliverables: A remediation plan with owners and dates, a cost estimate, and a monthly remediation progress report.
Prerequisites: Assessment findings, owner commitment, and a risk treatment process.
Lead Time: Assessment starts within 15 business days of a scoped request.
SLA Response Target: Assessment request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days of fieldwork
Escalation Path: A critical exposure of restricted data found during assessment escalates to the data owner and the incident commander the same day.
Threats Addressed: Findings that never get fixed, remediation without priority, and repeated audit observations.
KPIs and Metrics: Remediation actions on track, overdue actions, and residual risk reduction.

Name: Data Role-Based Access
Summary: Define data roles and map them to groups so dataset access follows job function.
Description: A role catalog ties each data role to the datasets it may use, and access is granted through groups rather than one-off grants. Role owners approve changes.
In Scope: Defining data roles and mapping them to groups so access to datasets follows job function.
Out of Scope: Application role design outside data platforms, HR job codes, and access recertification.
Deliverables: A data role catalog, a role-to-dataset matrix, and group mappings in the data platform.
Prerequisites: Dataset owners, job function definitions, and an identity platform that supports groups.
Lead Time: Access model design for a new dataset within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Approved access granted within 2 business days
Escalation Path: Access granted without owner approval to restricted data escalates to the identity lead and the data owner.
Threats Addressed: Excess access from ad hoc grants, privilege creep, and inconsistent permissions across platforms.
KPIs and Metrics: Data access via roles versus direct grants, roles without an owner, and role changes approved.

Name: Data Attribute-Based Access
Summary: Use attributes such as region, department, or clearance to control access to rows, columns, and datasets.
Description: Policies are written with the data owner, tested before release, and depend on clean identity attributes. Stale or wrong attributes are reported, because they quietly grant access.
In Scope: Attribute rules, such as region, department, or clearance, that decide access to rows, columns, or datasets.
Out of Scope: Building the identity attributes, data warehouse performance tuning, and role catalog design.
Deliverables: An attribute policy set, a rule test record, and an attribute quality report.
Prerequisites: Reliable identity attributes, a data platform that supports policy-based access, and owner-approved rules.
Lead Time: Access model design for a new dataset within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Approved access granted within 2 business days
Escalation Path: Access granted without owner approval to restricted data escalates to the identity lead and the data owner.
Threats Addressed: Users seeing records outside their region, stale attributes granting access, and policy bypass.
KPIs and Metrics: Policies tested before release, access decisions based on stale attributes, and rule exceptions.

Name: Dataset-Level Permissions
Summary: Grant, scope, and record permissions on individual datasets, tables, and buckets.
Description: Permissions follow a least-privilege standard with owner approval. Wildcard grants and public buckets are removed, and direct grants older than 90 days are reported for cleanup.
In Scope: Granting, scoping, and recording permissions on individual datasets, tables, and buckets.
Out of Scope: Network access, application feature permissions, and data quality issues.
Deliverables: A permission standard, a dataset permission register, and a monthly direct-grant report.
Prerequisites: A data platform with auditable permissions, owner approval workflow, and naming standards.
Lead Time: Access model design for a new dataset within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Approved access granted within 2 business days
Escalation Path: Access granted without owner approval to restricted data escalates to the identity lead and the data owner.
Threats Addressed: Wildcard grants, public buckets, and service accounts with unrestricted read.
KPIs and Metrics: Datasets with least-privilege permissions, wildcard grants removed, and direct grants aged over 90 days.

Name: Data Access Reviews
Summary: Have data owners periodically confirm who can access their sensitive datasets.
Description: Owners get a campaign with the current permission list and must keep or remove each entry. Decisions are recorded, and removals are applied promptly. Rubber-stamping is measured.
In Scope: Periodic owner reviews of who can access sensitive datasets, with keep or remove decisions recorded.
Out of Scope: Application-wide recertification, HR changes, and building new roles.
Deliverables: Review campaigns per dataset, signed owner decisions, and a review completion report.
Prerequisites: A current permission export, assigned reviewers, and a review tool or workflow.
Lead Time: Review campaign launched within 10 business days of the schedule date.
SLA Response Target: Review campaign issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Review completed within 15 business days / revocations applied within 2 business days
Escalation Path: An owner who misses a restricted dataset review escalates to their director and the identity lead.
Threats Addressed: Leftover access after role changes, contractors keeping access, and rubber-stamp approvals.
KPIs and Metrics: Reviews completed on time, access removed per campaign, and reviewer rubber-stamp rate.

Name: Excessive Data-Permission Detection
Summary: Flag users and service accounts holding unused, toxic, or unusual data permissions.
Description: Analytics compare permissions with actual use and peer groups and produce a monthly list of recommended removals. Owners decide. Revocation is a separate step.
In Scope: Analytics that flag users and service accounts with unused, toxic, or out-of-pattern data permissions.
Out of Scope: Revoking the access, user behavior investigations, and role design.
Deliverables: A monthly excessive-permission report, a toxic combination list, and recommended revocations.
Prerequisites: Permission and access log feeds, a peer group model, and owner contacts.
Lead Time: New data platform connected to permission analytics within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Monthly excessive-permission report issued by the 5th business day
SLA Resolution Target: Owner decision on flagged permissions within 10 business days of the report
Escalation Path: An unused admin-level data permission that the owner has not decided on after 30 days escalates to the identity lead.
Threats Addressed: Dormant high-privilege access, toxic combinations, and attackers using over-permissioned accounts.
KPIs and Metrics: Excessive permissions found, permissions removed after detection, and time from detection to decision.

Name: Data Access Revocation
Summary: Remove data access promptly after reviews, role changes, departures, or incidents.
Description: Every trigger becomes a ticket, and every removal is confirmed in the platform. A weekly backlog report keeps revocations from aging.
In Scope: Removing data access promptly after review decisions, role changes, terminations, or incidents.
Out of Scope: Account deletion, offboarding coordination, and building automated provisioning.
Deliverables: A revocation procedure, revocation completion records, and a weekly revocation backlog report.
Prerequisites: Review outcomes or triggers, admin access to data platforms, and a ticket path.
Lead Time: Revocation is triggered by the review, mover, or leaver event. No setup lead time.
SLA Response Target: Revocation ticket picked up within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Access removed within 2 business days / within 1 hour for incident-driven removal
Escalation Path: A revocation that fails, or access restored without approval, escalates to the identity lead and the data owner.
Threats Addressed: Former users keeping data access, delayed removals after incidents, and orphaned service account grants.
KPIs and Metrics: Revocations completed within 2 business days, backlog size, and failed revocations found by audit.

Name: Partner Access Approval
Summary: Review and approve partner and vendor requests to access company data, with scope and expiry.
Description: Requests need a business reason, a signed agreement, and the data owner's input. Approvals carry an expiry date and conditions of use. Vendor security assessment is separate.
In Scope: Reviewing and approving partner and vendor requests to access company data, with scope, duration, and conditions.
Out of Scope: Vendor security assessments, contract drafting, and building the integration.
Deliverables: An approval record with scope and expiry, conditions of use, and an approved partner sharing register.
Prerequisites: A business justification, a signed agreement, and the dataset owner's input.
Lead Time: Partner sharing request assessed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Sharing request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approval decision within 10 business days / emergency revocation within 4 hours
Escalation Path: Sharing that exposes restricted data without an agreement escalates to the data owner, privacy lead, and legal.
Threats Addressed: Partners getting more data than needed, sharing without legal basis, and indefinite access.
KPIs and Metrics: Requests decided within SLA, approvals with an expiry date, and approvals later found out of scope.

Name: Sharing Restrictions
Summary: Apply technical and contractual limits on what partners can do with shared data.
Description: Shares are set up with limits such as no onward sharing, no download, and link expiry, backed by contract clauses. Exceptions are logged with a reason.
In Scope: Technical and contractual restrictions on what partners can do with shared data, such as no onward sharing or download limits.
Out of Scope: Monitoring partner behavior, partner audits, and data loss prevention tuning.
Deliverables: A sharing restriction standard, restriction settings per share, and a restriction exception log.
Prerequisites: Sharing platforms that support restrictions, contract clauses, and owner-defined limits.
Lead Time: Partner sharing request assessed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Sharing request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approval decision within 10 business days / emergency revocation within 4 hours
Escalation Path: Sharing that exposes restricted data without an agreement escalates to the data owner, privacy lead, and legal.
Threats Addressed: Onward disclosure by partners, bulk download of shared data, and links forwarded to unknown people.
KPIs and Metrics: Shares with restrictions applied, restriction exceptions, and violations reported by partners.

Name: Partner Data Sharing Revocation
Summary: End partner access when a contract ends or risk changes, and confirm the data is returned or deleted.
Description: Revocation follows a checklist tied to contract end dates and ends with a deletion or return certificate from the partner. Live shares found after the end date are chased down.
In Scope: Ending partner access when a contract ends, purpose is met, or risk changes, and confirming return or deletion.
Out of Scope: Contract termination negotiation, vendor offboarding outside data, and incident investigation.
Deliverables: A revocation checklist, a deletion or return certificate from the partner, and a closed sharing register entry.
Prerequisites: A current sharing register, contract end dates, and partner contacts.
Lead Time: Partner sharing request assessed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Sharing request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approval decision within 10 business days / emergency revocation within 4 hours
Escalation Path: Sharing that exposes restricted data without an agreement escalates to the data owner, privacy lead, and legal.
Threats Addressed: Ex-partners holding company data, live links after contract end, and unconfirmed deletion.
KPIs and Metrics: Shares revoked by contract end date, deletion certificates received, and live shares found after end.

Name: Encryption at Rest
Summary: Set and verify encryption for disks, databases, files, and backups, including who owns the keys.
Description: The standard defines required encryption by classification and platform. Coverage reports list unencrypted stores with owners. Running the key management service is a separate function.
In Scope: Standards and verification for disk, database, file, and backup encryption, including key ownership.
Out of Scope: Operating the key management service, application-level field encryption code, and storage procurement.
Deliverables: An encryption at rest standard, a coverage report by platform, and a list of unencrypted stores with owners.
Prerequisites: An inventory of data stores, a key management service, and platform encryption options.
Lead Time: Encryption design for a new system within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Encryption question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Standard configuration guidance within 5 business days
Escalation Path: An unencrypted store of restricted data, or an expired certificate on a critical service, escalates to the system owner and the security engineering lead.
Threats Addressed: Data exposure from lost disks, stolen backups, and cloud snapshot leaks.
KPIs and Metrics: Restricted stores encrypted, stores using customer-managed keys, and unencrypted exceptions open.

Name: Encryption in Transit
Summary: Set and check TLS for internal and external connections, approved ciphers, and certificate hygiene.
Description: Scans find weak protocols and expiring certificates before they cause exposure or outages. The standard covers both internal and external traffic.
In Scope: Standards and checks for TLS on internal and external connections, approved ciphers, and certificate hygiene.
Out of Scope: Network firewall configuration, certificate authority operation, and VPN service delivery.
Deliverables: A transport encryption standard, a weak protocol scan report, and a certificate expiry calendar.
Prerequisites: Service and endpoint inventories, a certificate management tool, and scanning access.
Lead Time: Encryption design for a new system within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Encryption question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Standard configuration guidance within 5 business days
Escalation Path: An unencrypted store of restricted data, or an expired certificate on a critical service, escalates to the system owner and the security engineering lead.
Threats Addressed: Interception of data on networks, downgrade attacks, and outages from expired certificates.
KPIs and Metrics: Endpoints with approved TLS, weak protocols found, and certificates renewed before expiry.

Name: Static Masking
Summary: Irreversibly mask copies of datasets before they move to lower environments or are shared.
Description: Masking rules are set per dataset from its field-level classification, and every masked copy is verified before transfer. Live query masking is a separate service.
In Scope: Irreversibly masking copies of datasets before they are moved to lower environments or shared.
Out of Scope: Live query masking, tokenization services, and building test data from scratch.
Deliverables: A masking rule set per dataset, a masked copy verification report, and a masking run log.
Prerequisites: A field-level classification of the dataset, a masking tool, and the target environment.
Lead Time: Masking rules for a new dataset designed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Masking request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Masking configuration delivered within 10 business days
Escalation Path: Unmasked production personal data found in a non-production environment escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Production personal data in development, re-identification of masked copies, and test data leaks.
KPIs and Metrics: Copies masked before transfer, verification failures, and unmasked copies found in scans.

Name: Dynamic Masking
Summary: Mask sensitive fields at query time so lower-privileged users see redacted values.
Description: Policies decide by role who sees full values and who sees masked ones, for example support staff seeing only the last four digits. Unmasking requests are approved and counted.
In Scope: Masking sensitive fields at query time based on the user's role so lower-privileged users see redacted values.
Out of Scope: Permanent masking of copies, row-level filters, and application UI design.
Deliverables: Dynamic masking policies, a role-to-unmasked-field matrix, and a policy test record.
Prerequisites: A data platform that supports dynamic masking, role definitions, and owner-approved rules.
Lead Time: Masking rules for a new dataset designed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Masking request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Masking configuration delivered within 10 business days
Escalation Path: Unmasked production personal data found in a non-production environment escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Support staff seeing full card or ID numbers, overexposure in analytics, and screen scraping of personal data.
KPIs and Metrics: Sensitive fields under masking, policy bypass incidents, and unmasking approvals per quarter.

Name: Test-Data Masking
Summary: Provide masked or synthetic test data that keeps referential integrity, so testing never needs real personal data.
Description: Engineering gets realistic, masked test datasets on a refresh schedule. Real customer data stays out of test logs and developer laptops.
In Scope: Masked or synthetic test datasets that keep referential integrity so testing works without real personal data.
Out of Scope: Running test cycles, test environment provisioning, and performance testing tools.
Deliverables: A test data masking pattern library, masked test datasets, and a refresh schedule.
Prerequisites: Test data requirements from engineering, schema documentation, and masking tooling.
Lead Time: Masking rules for a new dataset designed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Masking request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Masking configuration delivered within 10 business days
Escalation Path: Unmasked production personal data found in a non-production environment escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Real customer data in test logs, developer access to production data, and leaked test databases.
KPIs and Metrics: Test environments using masked data, refresh requests met on time, and test defects caused by masking.

Name: Token Generation
Summary: Replace card numbers, national IDs, and similar values with tokens through a central service.
Description: Applications store tokens instead of sensitive values, which shrinks where that data lives and what is in audit scope. Onboarding comes with an integration guide and token format specifications.
In Scope: Replacing sensitive values, such as card or national ID numbers, with tokens through a central service.
Out of Scope: Payment processing, application business logic, and key ceremony administration.
Deliverables: A tokenization integration guide, token format specifications, and an onboarding record per application.
Prerequisites: A tokenization platform, application owner engagement, and a data element list to tokenize.
Lead Time: New application onboarded to tokenization within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Tokenization service incident acknowledged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Service restored within 1 hour / onboarding request completed within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A token vault outage, or detokenization outside policy, escalates to the security engineering lead and the incident commander.
Threats Addressed: Exposure of card or ID data in application databases, logs, and analytics.
KPIs and Metrics: Applications using tokens, sensitive values still stored in clear, and tokenization latency.

Name: Token Mapping Protection
Summary: Protect the token vault and its mapping tables with encryption, access control, and monitoring.
Description: The vault is the crown jewel of tokenization. Admin access is tightly limited and reviewed quarterly, and the vault keys are rotated on schedule.
In Scope: Protecting the token vault and mapping tables with encryption, access control, and monitoring.
Out of Scope: Application-side token use, payment network audits, and hardware security module procurement.
Deliverables: A vault access control record, a key rotation log, and a quarterly vault access review.
Prerequisites: A hardened vault environment, key management integration, and an admin access list.
Lead Time: New application onboarded to tokenization within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Tokenization service incident acknowledged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Service restored within 1 hour / onboarding request completed within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A token vault outage, or detokenization outside policy, escalates to the security engineering lead and the incident commander.
Threats Addressed: Theft of the token vault, insider access to mappings, and compromise of vault keys.
KPIs and Metrics: Vault admin accounts, keys rotated on schedule, and unauthorized vault access attempts.

Name: Authorized Detokenization
Summary: Let only approved services and people turn tokens back into real values, with full logging.
Description: Each caller needs a documented business case. Every detokenization is logged, and unusual volumes raise an alert. Token generation is a separate service.
In Scope: Controls that let only approved services and users turn tokens back into real values, with full logging.
Out of Scope: Token generation, application authentication, and fraud investigation.
Deliverables: A detokenization policy, an approved caller list, and a detokenization activity report.
Prerequisites: Defined business cases for detokenization, service identities, and vault logging.
Lead Time: New application onboarded to tokenization within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Tokenization service incident acknowledged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Service restored within 1 hour / onboarding request completed within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A token vault outage, or detokenization outside policy, escalates to the security engineering lead and the incident commander.
Threats Addressed: Bulk detokenization by compromised services, curious insiders, and unlogged reveals.
KPIs and Metrics: Detokenization calls by approved callers only, unusual volume alerts, and caller list reviews.

Name: Data Access Logging
Summary: Enable, collect, and keep logs of who read, changed, or exported sensitive datasets.
Description: Sensitive datasets have access logging on and feeding the SIEM, with retention set to support investigations. Analyzing the logs is done by detection services.
In Scope: Enabling, collecting, and retaining logs of who read, changed, or exported sensitive datasets.
Out of Scope: Analyzing the logs for threats, application debug logging, and log platform operation.
Deliverables: A data access logging standard, a log coverage report per dataset, and retention settings.
Prerequisites: Platform audit features, a log pipeline to the SIEM, and a list of sensitive datasets.
Lead Time: New data source logging enabled within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Logging gap alert acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Logging restored within 1 business day / new dataset logging enabled within 10 business days
Escalation Path: Confirmed misuse of restricted data escalates to the SOC lead, the data owner, and the insider risk lead.
Threats Addressed: Undetected misuse, inability to scope breaches, and missing evidence for investigations.
KPIs and Metrics: Sensitive datasets with access logging, log gaps over 24 hours, and retention compliance.

Name: Unusual-Access Detection
Summary: Detect unusual access to sensitive data by users or service accounts.
Description: Rules and baselines flag browsing outside a person's normal pattern, such as a support agent opening hundreds of customer records. Alerts are triaged and confirmed cases escalated.
In Scope: Detection rules and baselines that flag unusual access to sensitive data by users or service accounts.
Out of Scope: Insider case management, permission cleanup, and data loss prevention for email.
Deliverables: Detection rules with tuning notes, a weekly alert summary, and escalated cases.
Prerequisites: Data access logs in the SIEM, user and peer baselines, and a triage process.
Lead Time: New data source logging enabled within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: High-risk data access alert acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Alert triaged within 4 hours / routine finding reported in 2 business days
Escalation Path: Confirmed misuse of restricted data escalates to the SOC lead, the data owner, and the insider risk lead.
Threats Addressed: Compromised accounts browsing sensitive records, insiders snooping, and service account abuse.
KPIs and Metrics: True positive rate, time to triage, and detection coverage by dataset.

Name: Bulk-Download Detection
Summary: Alert when users or apps pull unusually large volumes of records or files from sensitive stores.
Description: Thresholds per store and role catch data theft before resignation, ransomware staging, and compromised accounts. Confirmed cases go to incident response.
In Scope: Alerts when users or apps pull unusually large volumes of records or files from sensitive stores.
Out of Scope: Bandwidth monitoring for network performance, backup job reporting, and insider HR decisions.
Deliverables: Bulk download thresholds per store, alert records, and a monthly bulk activity review.
Prerequisites: Download and query logs, baseline volumes per role, and SIEM integration.
Lead Time: New dataset added to usage monitoring within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: High-severity usage alert acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Alert triaged within 4 hours / confirmed case opened the same day
Escalation Path: A confirmed large export of restricted data escalates to the incident commander and the data owner immediately.
Threats Addressed: Data theft before resignation, ransomware staging, and compromised accounts exfiltrating files.
KPIs and Metrics: Bulk events detected, mean time to triage, and confirmed exfiltration cases.

Name: Unusual-Query Detection
Summary: Monitor database and warehouse queries for unusual joins, full scans, and access to sensitive columns.
Description: Query anomaly rules are tuned with the data teams and catch extraction through injection, curious analysts, and reconnaissance. Query performance work is out of scope.
In Scope: Monitoring database and warehouse query patterns for unusual joins, scans, and access to sensitive columns.
Out of Scope: Query performance tuning, data model design, and database administration.
Deliverables: Query anomaly rules, investigation notes per alert, and a quarterly tuning report.
Prerequisites: Query logs from data platforms, sensitive column tags, and analyst baselines.
Lead Time: New dataset added to usage monitoring within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: High-severity usage alert acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Alert triaged within 4 hours / confirmed case opened the same day
Escalation Path: A confirmed large export of restricted data escalates to the incident commander and the data owner immediately.
Threats Addressed: SQL injection-driven extraction, curious analysts, and reconnaissance on data stores.
KPIs and Metrics: Anomalous queries investigated, false positive rate, and sensitive tables covered.

Name: Export Monitoring
Summary: Watch exports to files, email, removable media, and cloud uploads from sensitive systems.
Description: Export activity is reviewed by system, and unsanctioned destinations are raised with the owner. The goal is visibility and fast escalation, not blocking every export.
In Scope: Watching exports to files, email, removable media, and cloud uploads from sensitive systems.
Out of Scope: Blocking every export, records retention, and approval of new export features.
Deliverables: Export monitoring rules, an export activity report by system, and escalated exfiltration cases.
Prerequisites: Export logs or DLP telemetry, sensitive system list, and owner contacts.
Lead Time: New dataset added to usage monitoring within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: High-severity usage alert acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Alert triaged within 4 hours / confirmed case opened the same day
Escalation Path: A confirmed large export of restricted data escalates to the incident commander and the data owner immediately.
Threats Addressed: Data leaving through reports and spreadsheets, unsanctioned uploads, and USB exfiltration.
KPIs and Metrics: Exports reviewed, unsanctioned destinations found, and cases opened from export alerts.

Name: Secure Ingestion
Summary: Set security requirements for new data feeds, uploads, and pipelines before they go live.
Description: Every new feed is checked for authentication, encryption, and malware scanning against approved patterns. Pipeline build and data quality stay with engineering.
In Scope: Security requirements for new data feeds, uploads, and pipelines, including authentication, encryption, and malware scanning.
Out of Scope: Building the pipelines, data quality validation, and schema design.
Deliverables: An ingestion security checklist, a review record per feed, and approved ingestion patterns.
Prerequisites: A feed design, data classification for the feed, and pipeline owner engagement.
Lead Time: Intake review for a new data feed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Intake review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review decision within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A feed that collects restricted data without approval escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead.
Threats Addressed: Poisoned or malicious files, unauthenticated uploads, and interception of incoming data.
KPIs and Metrics: Feeds reviewed before go-live, feeds without encryption, and ingestion incidents.

Name: Source Validation
Summary: Verify that data sources are authentic and authorized before their data is accepted.
Description: Sources prove who they are with keys or certificates and are listed in a trusted source register. Validation failures are logged per feed and investigated.
In Scope: Verifying that data sources are authentic, authorized, and trustworthy before data is accepted.
Out of Scope: Business validation of data content, vendor due diligence, and API gateway operation.
Deliverables: A source validation standard, a trusted source register, and validation failures logged per feed.
Prerequisites: Source identity mechanisms, such as keys or certificates, and an owner for each source.
Lead Time: Intake review for a new data feed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Intake review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review decision within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A feed that collects restricted data without approval escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead.
Threats Addressed: Spoofed data feeds, data from unauthorized sources, and integrity attacks on analytics.
KPIs and Metrics: Feeds with validated sources, validation failures per month, and untrusted sources removed.

Name: Collection Controls
Summary: Limit what data is collected at the source to what the approved purpose needs.
Description: New forms and feeds are reviewed for fields that are not needed, and over-collection is removed. Notice drafting and consent capture are separate privacy services.
In Scope: Rules that limit what data is collected at the source to what is needed for the approved purpose.
Out of Scope: Privacy notice drafting, consent capture, and form design.
Deliverables: A collection control standard, a review record for new forms and feeds, and a list of over-collection findings.
Prerequisites: Approved processing purposes, form and API designs, and privacy review input.
Lead Time: Intake review for a new data feed within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Intake review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review decision within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A feed that collects restricted data without approval escalates to the data owner and the privacy lead.
Threats Addressed: Over-collection of personal data, collection without notice, and unnecessary sensitive fields.
KPIs and Metrics: New collections reviewed, over-collected fields removed, and findings closed on time.

Name: Retention Implementation
Summary: Configure systems to apply retention schedules, including automatic expiry and legal hold exceptions.
Description: Approved retention rules are set in each system, and legal holds override deletion. A status report shows which systems are configured and where data is held past its date.
In Scope: Configuring systems to apply retention schedules, including automatic expiry and legal hold exceptions.
Out of Scope: Writing the retention schedule, legal hold decisions, and archive platform procurement.
Deliverables: Retention settings per system, an implementation status report, and a legal hold override record.
Prerequisites: An approved retention schedule, system owners, and platform retention features.
Lead Time: Retention rule implemented within 20 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Retention question acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Retention configuration change within 15 business days
Escalation Path: Data held past retention on a restricted system, or a legal hold conflict, escalates to legal and the records manager.
Threats Addressed: Data kept indefinitely, premature deletion of records under hold, and inconsistent retention.
KPIs and Metrics: Systems with retention configured, records past retention, and legal hold override errors.

Name: Archive Protection
Summary: Secure archives with encryption, restricted access, integrity checks, and tamper-evident storage.
Description: Archives hold old records that still matter. Access is reviewed, integrity is checked, and media are stored securely. Retrieval requests and operational backups are separate.
In Scope: Securing archives with encryption, restricted access, integrity checks, and tamper-evident storage.
Out of Scope: Operational backups for recovery, records classification, and archive retrieval requests.
Deliverables: An archive protection standard, an archive access review, and integrity check results.
Prerequisites: An archive inventory, archive platform controls, and named archive custodians.
Lead Time: Retention rule implemented within 20 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Retention question acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Retention configuration change within 15 business days
Escalation Path: Data held past retention on a restricted system, or a legal hold conflict, escalates to legal and the records manager.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized access to old records, archive tampering, and theft of archive media.
KPIs and Metrics: Archives encrypted, access reviews completed, and integrity check failures.

Name: Retention Review
Summary: Check that retention rules are applied and still match legal and business needs.
Description: An annual review compares the schedule with what systems actually do and with current law, and recommends changes. Over-retained data is reported because it increases breach impact.
In Scope: Periodic review of whether retention rules are applied and still match legal and business needs.
Out of Scope: Drafting new laws into rules without legal input, and deleting data directly.
Deliverables: An annual retention review report, a list of misaligned rules, and recommended schedule changes.
Prerequisites: The retention schedule, system retention reports, and legal and records input.
Lead Time: Retention rule implemented within 20 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Retention question acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Retention configuration change within 15 business days
Escalation Path: Data held past retention on a restricted system, or a legal hold conflict, escalates to legal and the records manager.
Threats Addressed: Over-retention that grows breach impact, and rules that drift from legal requirements.
KPIs and Metrics: Rules reviewed per year, misaligned rules fixed, and over-retained volume reduced.

Name: Secure Deletion
Summary: Delete data from systems and cloud services so it cannot be recovered, and record proof.
Description: Deletion follows platform-specific methods, covers replicas, and produces a confirmation record. A quarterly sample checks deletions actually happened.
In Scope: Deleting data from systems and cloud services in a way that cannot be recovered, with confirmation records.
Out of Scope: Physical destruction of media, archive retention decisions, and backup rotation design.
Deliverables: A secure deletion procedure, deletion confirmation records, and a quarterly deletion audit sample.
Prerequisites: Approved deletion triggers, platform deletion methods, and system owner access.
Lead Time: Disposal job scheduled within 5 business days of a valid request.
SLA Response Target: Disposal request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Disposal completed and certified within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A failed or uncertified disposal of restricted data escalates to the data protection lead and the asset owner.
Threats Addressed: Recoverable data after deletion, incomplete deletion across replicas, and failed customer deletion requests.
KPIs and Metrics: Deletions confirmed within SLA, audit samples passing, and replicas missed.

Name: Media Sanitization
Summary: Wipe or destroy drives, laptops, phones, and removable media before reuse, resale, or disposal.
Description: Media are sanitized by type to a written standard, by a tool or certified vendor, and every asset is reconciled to the register with a certificate. Resale negotiation is out of scope.
In Scope: Wiping or destroying drives, laptops, phones, and removable media before reuse, resale, or disposal.
Out of Scope: IT asset resale negotiation, hardware repair, and paper record shredding.
Deliverables: A sanitization standard by media type, certificates of sanitization, and a reconciliation to the asset register.
Prerequisites: An asset disposal process, a certified vendor or wiping tool, and asset tags.
Lead Time: Disposal job scheduled within 5 business days of a valid request.
SLA Response Target: Disposal request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Disposal completed and certified within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A failed or uncertified disposal of restricted data escalates to the data protection lead and the asset owner.
Threats Addressed: Data recovered from resold hardware, lost devices in disposal chains, and uncertified vendors.
KPIs and Metrics: Assets with a sanitization certificate, reconciliation gaps, and vendor audit results.

Name: Paper-Record Destruction
Summary: Destroy paper records holding sensitive data through locked bins and certified shredding.
Description: Locked bins are collected on a schedule and the vendor returns certificates of destruction. Staff awareness keeps sensitive printouts out of open recycling.
In Scope: Locked shred bins, scheduled collection, and certified destruction of paper records holding sensitive data.
Out of Scope: Records retention schedule drafting, digitization projects, and mailroom services.
Deliverables: A paper destruction procedure, collection schedules, and certificates of destruction.
Prerequisites: Locked bins, a shredding vendor contract, and staff awareness.
Lead Time: Disposal job scheduled within 5 business days of a valid request.
SLA Response Target: Disposal request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Disposal completed and certified within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A failed or uncertified disposal of restricted data escalates to the data protection lead and the asset owner.
Threats Addressed: Sensitive paper in recycling, dumpster diving, and uncontrolled printouts.
KPIs and Metrics: Bins collected on schedule, destruction certificates received, and paper incidents.

Name: Integrity Verification
Summary: Use hashes, checksums, and signatures to confirm important data and files have not been altered.
Description: Reference values for critical datasets are stored separately and checked on a schedule. Failures are explained or escalated. Business data quality checks are separate.
In Scope: Hashing, checksums, and signatures that confirm important data and files have not been altered.
Out of Scope: Data quality checks for business errors, backup operation, and software signing.
Deliverables: An integrity verification standard, checksum records for critical data, and failure reports.
Prerequisites: A list of critical datasets, hashing or signing tools, and storage for reference values.
Lead Time: Integrity monitoring for a new system configured within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Integrity alert acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Critical integrity failure triaged within 4 hours
Escalation Path: An unexplained change to a critical dataset escalates to the incident commander and the data owner.
Threats Addressed: Silent corruption, tampering with financial or safety data, and altered evidence.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical datasets under verification, verification failures, and time to explain failures.

Name: Unauthorized-Change Detection
Summary: Alert on unexpected changes to critical files and database records.
Description: File integrity and database change monitoring compare changes with approved windows and raise alerts for anything outside them, including mass encryption by ransomware.
In Scope: File integrity and database change monitoring that alerts on unexpected changes to critical data.
Out of Scope: Change management approvals, application audit logging design, and backup restoration.
Deliverables: Change detection rules, an alert record, and a monthly unauthorized change summary.
Prerequisites: Approved change windows, monitoring agents or database audit, and SIEM integration.
Lead Time: Integrity monitoring for a new system configured within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Integrity alert acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Critical integrity failure triaged within 4 hours
Escalation Path: An unexplained change to a critical dataset escalates to the incident commander and the data owner.
Threats Addressed: Malicious data manipulation, unauthorized admin edits, and ransomware encryption of files.
KPIs and Metrics: Unauthorized changes detected, mean time to detect, and false positive rate.

Name: Backup Access Control
Summary: Protect backup systems with separate admin identities, MFA, immutability, and least privilege.
Description: Backup admin accounts are separate from everyday admin accounts, use MFA, and are reviewed. Recovery points are immutable, so an attacker with domain admin cannot delete them.
In Scope: Separate admin identities, MFA, immutability, and least privilege for backup systems and cloud vaults.
Out of Scope: Running the backup jobs, storage capacity, and application restore requests.
Deliverables: A backup access standard, an admin access review record, and an immutability configuration report.
Prerequisites: A backup platform with role-based access, separate admin accounts, and an identity provider.
Lead Time: New backup scope protected within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Backup security alert acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Backup access issue resolved within 1 business day / failed restore test reported within 2 business days
Escalation Path: Deletion or encryption of backups, or a failed restore of a critical system, escalates to the infrastructure lead and the incident commander immediately.
Threats Addressed: Ransomware actors deleting backups, insiders erasing recovery points, and shared backup admin accounts.
KPIs and Metrics: Backup admins with MFA, immutable recovery points, and access review completion.

Name: Backup Encryption
Summary: Encrypt backup data at rest and in transit, with keys held apart from the backup platform.
Description: Every backup set is encrypted, and the keys are escrowed outside the backup system so a single compromise does not expose both.
In Scope: Encrypting backup data at rest and in transit, with keys managed separately from the backup platform.
Out of Scope: Primary storage encryption, key management service operation, and backup scheduling.
Deliverables: A backup encryption standard, a coverage report per backup set, and a key escrow record.
Prerequisites: Backup platform encryption features, key management, and a backup set inventory.
Lead Time: New backup scope protected within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Backup security alert acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Backup access issue resolved within 1 business day / failed restore test reported within 2 business days
Escalation Path: Deletion or encryption of backups, or a failed restore of a critical system, escalates to the infrastructure lead and the incident commander immediately.
Threats Addressed: Theft of backup media, exposed cloud backups, and keys stored next to backups.
KPIs and Metrics: Backup sets encrypted, keys stored separately, and encryption exceptions.

Name: Restoration Validation
Summary: Prove by regular test restores that backups are complete, clean, and usable within recovery objectives.
Description: Restores are run on a schedule with system owners, timed against recovery objectives, and checked for malware. Failed restores are fixed and retested. Full DR failover is separate.
In Scope: Regular test restores that prove backups are complete, clean, and usable within recovery objectives.
Out of Scope: Full disaster recovery failover, application testing after restore, and backup job tuning.
Deliverables: A restore test schedule, restore test reports with timings, and a failed restore remediation list.
Prerequisites: Recovery objectives per system, a test environment, and system owner participation.
Lead Time: New backup scope protected within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Backup security alert acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Backup access issue resolved within 1 business day / failed restore test reported within 2 business days
Escalation Path: Deletion or encryption of backups, or a failed restore of a critical system, escalates to the infrastructure lead and the incident commander immediately.
Threats Addressed: Unusable backups found during a real incident, malware restored with data, and missed recovery times.
KPIs and Metrics: Restore tests passed, restore time versus objective, and systems tested per quarter.

Name: Affected-Data Identification
Summary: Identify which records, data types, and people are involved in a data security incident.
Description: Analysts use logs and data maps to produce a record count by data type and a confidence statement. The estimate drives notification decisions, which are made by privacy and legal.
In Scope: Identifying which records, data types, and people are involved in a data security incident.
Out of Scope: Notification decisions, containment actions, and forensic imaging of devices.
Deliverables: An affected data inventory, a record count by data type, and a confidence statement.
Prerequisites: Access logs, data maps, and analyst access to the affected systems.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Engaged on declaration of a data incident.
SLA Response Target: Data incident analyst engaged within 1 hour of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Initial affected-data estimate within 24 hours / refined scope within 72 hours
Escalation Path: An incident likely to involve regulated personal data escalates to the privacy lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Underestimated breaches, missed regulated data types, and late notification.
KPIs and Metrics: Time to first estimate, estimate accuracy at closure, and data types identified.

Name: Data Exposure-Scope Analysis
Summary: Work out how far an exposure spread: systems, time window, recipients, and onward sharing.
Description: The analysis produces a timeline and a list of affected systems and recipients, and is refined as evidence arrives. It sizes the incident. Remediation is a separate step.
In Scope: Determining how far exposure spread, including systems, time window, recipients, and onward sharing.
Out of Scope: Root cause remediation, regulator communication, and customer support scripts.
Deliverables: A scope analysis report, an exposure timeline, and a list of recipients or systems involved.
Prerequisites: Incident timeline, logs from affected systems, and sharing records.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Engaged on declaration of a data incident.
SLA Response Target: Data incident analyst engaged within 1 hour of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Initial affected-data estimate within 24 hours / refined scope within 72 hours
Escalation Path: An incident likely to involve regulated personal data escalates to the privacy lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Breaches that keep spreading, unknown third-party exposure, and missed systems.
KPIs and Metrics: Scope finalized within target, scope changes after notification, and logs available for scope.

Name: Incident Data-Sharing Revocation
Summary: Cut off shared links, partner feeds, and external access involved in a data incident.
Description: On the incident commander's direction, responders revoke shares and feeds and confirm each one is closed. Any residual exposure is recorded for the scope analysis.
