In Scope: Cutting off shared links, partner feeds, and external access involved in a data incident.
Out of Scope: Partner contract decisions, legal holds, and long-term sharing redesign.
Deliverables: A revocation action log, confirmation of revoked links and feeds, and a residual exposure note.
Prerequisites: An external sharing register, admin access to sharing platforms, and partner contacts.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Actions start on incident commander direction.
SLA Response Target: Containment action started within 1 hour of direction
SLA Resolution Target: Containment complete within 4 hours / remediation plan within 5 business days
Escalation Path: A containment step that will disrupt a critical business service escalates to the incident commander and the service owner for a decision.
Threats Addressed: Ongoing exposure through live links, attackers using partner feeds, and data spread after discovery.
KPIs and Metrics: Time to revoke after direction, shares revoked, and re-exposure events.

Name: Credential or Key Rotation
Summary: Rotate passwords, API keys, tokens, and certificates that may have been exposed in an incident.
Description: A rotation plan orders the work by risk and dependency, and every rotated credential is recorded. Breakages caused by rotation are logged so services come back quickly.
In Scope: Rotating passwords, API keys, tokens, and certificates suspected of exposure during an incident.
Out of Scope: Building secrets management, routine key rotation, and application redesign.
Deliverables: A rotation plan, a rotation completion record per credential, and a dependency break log.
Prerequisites: A credential inventory, secrets management tools, and system owners on call.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Actions start on incident commander direction.
SLA Response Target: Containment action started within 1 hour of direction
SLA Resolution Target: Containment complete within 4 hours / remediation plan within 5 business days
Escalation Path: A containment step that will disrupt a critical business service escalates to the incident commander and the service owner for a decision.
Threats Addressed: Attackers reusing stolen credentials, exposed API keys, and compromised signing keys.
KPIs and Metrics: Credentials rotated within target, services broken by rotation, and credentials missed.

Name: Protection-Gap Remediation
Summary: Fix the control gap that let a data incident happen, then prove the fix works.
Description: Root cause findings become change-managed fixes, such as closing a misconfiguration or adding encryption, with verification evidence. Process redesign and budget sit with the owners.
In Scope: Fixing the control gap that allowed a data incident, such as misconfiguration, missing encryption, or overbroad access.
Out of Scope: Business process redesign, budget approval, and post-incident review facilitation.
Deliverables: A remediation plan, change records for fixes, and verification evidence.
Prerequisites: Root cause findings, system owner commitment, and change approval.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Actions start on incident commander direction.
SLA Response Target: Containment action started within 1 hour of direction
SLA Resolution Target: Containment complete within 4 hours / remediation plan within 5 business days
Escalation Path: A containment step that will disrupt a critical business service escalates to the incident commander and the service owner for a decision.
Threats Addressed: Repeat incidents from the same gap and attackers returning through the same path.
KPIs and Metrics: Fixes verified, time to remediate, and repeat incidents from the same cause.

Name: Data-Access Reconstruction
Summary: Rebuild who accessed which data, when, and from where, using logs across platforms.
Description: Analysts produce a timeline and an access table from retained, time-synchronized logs, and state clearly where logs are missing. Disciplinary decisions are not part of this service.
In Scope: Rebuilding who accessed which data, when, and from where using logs across platforms.
Out of Scope: Disciplinary decisions, forensic disk analysis, and log platform administration.
Deliverables: An access reconstruction timeline, a user and record access table, and a data gaps note.
Prerequisites: Retained access logs, identity data, and time-synchronized sources.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Analyst assigned within 1 business day of request.
SLA Response Target: Investigation support request acknowledged within 2 hours
SLA Resolution Target: Initial reconstruction within 3 business days / findings documented within 10 business days
Escalation Path: An investigation that finds evidence of criminal activity or insider involvement escalates to legal and the investigations lead.
Threats Addressed: Unanswered questions after breaches, missed insider activity, and unsupported conclusions.
KPIs and Metrics: Reconstructions completed within target, log gaps found, and findings confirmed by review.

Name: Evidence Preservation
Summary: Preserve logs, snapshots, and data copies needed for investigation, with integrity and legal holds.
Description: Evidence is captured before rotation or overwrite, hashed, and held under legal hold. The service preserves. Forensic analysis is done by investigators.
In Scope: Preserving logs, snapshots, and data copies needed for investigation with integrity and legal holds.
Out of Scope: Forensic analysis, case management, and physical evidence handling.
Deliverables: A preservation request record, hash values for preserved data, and a retention hold confirmation.
Prerequisites: Legal hold process, storage for evidence, and access to systems of record.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Analyst assigned within 1 business day of request.
SLA Response Target: Investigation support request acknowledged within 2 hours
SLA Resolution Target: Initial reconstruction within 3 business days / findings documented within 10 business days
Escalation Path: An investigation that finds evidence of criminal activity or insider involvement escalates to legal and the investigations lead.
Threats Addressed: Evidence lost to log rotation, overwritten snapshots, and tampering claims.
KPIs and Metrics: Preservation completed within 24 hours, evidence with hashes, and lost evidence incidents.

Name: Findings Documentation
Summary: Write clear, evidence-backed findings for data incidents that legal, privacy, and leadership can rely on.
Description: Each report ties every finding to its evidence and comes with an executive summary. Legal reviews it before external use. Notification letters are drafted elsewhere.
In Scope: Writing clear, evidence-backed findings for data incidents that legal, privacy, and leadership can rely on.
Out of Scope: Notification letter drafting, public statements, and legal opinions.
Deliverables: An investigation findings report, an evidence reference index, and an executive summary.
Prerequisites: Completed analysis, legal review direction, and access to the case record.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Analyst assigned within 1 business day of request.
SLA Response Target: Investigation support request acknowledged within 2 hours
SLA Resolution Target: Initial reconstruction within 3 business days / findings documented within 10 business days
Escalation Path: An investigation that finds evidence of criminal activity or insider involvement escalates to legal and the investigations lead.
Threats Addressed: Conflicting incident narratives, unsupported regulatory submissions, and lost lessons.
KPIs and Metrics: Reports issued within target, review corrections required, and findings challenged.

Name: Secure Web Gateway Management
Summary: Manage secure web gateway policy, URL categories, TLS inspection rules, and user exceptions.
Description: The gateway sits between users and the internet and blocks malicious and unsanctioned destinations. Security owns the policy baseline and the exception register. Firewall rules are a separate service.
In Scope: Web proxy and secure web gateway policy, URL categories, TLS inspection rules, and user exception requests.
Out of Scope: Firewall rule management, endpoint agent deployment, and content filtering for guest Wi-Fi.
Deliverables: A gateway policy baseline, an exception register, and a monthly blocked-threat and bypass report.
Prerequisites: A deployed gateway or proxy, identity integration for user policies, and a category standard.
Lead Time: Policy change within 3 business days of approval. New site onboarding within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Category block or outage acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Emergency block within 1 hour / standard policy change within 3 business days
Escalation Path: A gateway outage that stops business traffic, or a bypass of inspection at scale, escalates to the network lead and the SOC.
Threats Addressed: Malicious downloads, phishing sites, command-and-control traffic, and uploads to unsanctioned cloud apps.
KPIs and Metrics: Users covered by the gateway, exceptions past expiry, and malicious sites blocked per month.

Name: DNS Security
Summary: Protect name resolution with filtered resolvers, hardening, DNSSEC where it applies, and DNS logging.
Description: Internal resolvers block known-bad and newly registered domains and send logs to the SIEM, where DNS tunneling and beaconing show up. Public domain registration is out of scope.
In Scope: Protective DNS filtering, DNSSEC where applicable, resolver hardening, and DNS logging for threat detection.
Out of Scope: Public domain registration, web hosting, and application load balancer configuration.
Deliverables: A resolver hardening baseline, a DNS block policy, and a weekly report of blocked malicious lookups.
Prerequisites: Control of internal resolvers, a protective DNS feed, and DNS logs sent to the SIEM.
Lead Time: DNS or wireless policy change within 5 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Malicious domain block acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Emergency block in place within 1 hour / standard change in 5 business days
Escalation Path: A DNS hijack, rogue access point at a critical site, or NAC failure open escalates to the network lead and the SOC.
Threats Addressed: DNS tunneling, domain hijacking, malware beaconing, and lookups of newly registered phishing domains.
KPIs and Metrics: Clients using protected resolvers, malicious lookups blocked, and DNS logs delivered without gaps.

Name: Wireless Network Security
Summary: Secure corporate, guest, and IoT wireless with certificate-based authentication, segmentation, and rogue AP detection.
Description: Each SSID maps to a defined segment. Corporate access uses certificates rather than shared keys, and the guest network cannot reach internal systems. Rogue and evil-twin access points are found and removed.
In Scope: Corporate, guest, and IoT wireless designs, authentication with certificates, rogue AP detection, and segmentation.
Out of Scope: Wireless coverage surveys for performance, guest marketing portals, and cellular networks.
Deliverables: A wireless security standard, an SSID and segment register, and a quarterly rogue AP report.
Prerequisites: A managed wireless platform, certificate-based authentication, and RF monitoring capability.
Lead Time: DNS or wireless policy change within 5 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Malicious domain block acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Emergency block in place within 1 hour / standard change in 5 business days
Escalation Path: A DNS hijack, rogue access point at a critical site, or NAC failure open escalates to the network lead and the SOC.
Threats Addressed: Rogue access points, evil-twin attacks, weak pre-shared keys, and guest users reaching internal networks.
KPIs and Metrics: SSIDs using certificate auth, rogue APs found and removed, and guest isolation test results.

Name: Network Access Control
Summary: Check device identity and posture before granting wired, wireless, or VPN network access.
Description: Unknown or non-compliant devices are quarantined until they are identified or fixed. The policy and quarantine procedure are owned by security. Device patching stays with endpoint teams.
In Scope: Admission control that checks device identity and posture before granting wired, wireless, or VPN network access.
Out of Scope: Endpoint patching, device purchasing, and user account provisioning.
Deliverables: A NAC policy set, a quarantine procedure, and a report of non-compliant and unknown devices.
Prerequisites: A NAC platform, switch and wireless integration, and a device inventory with ownership.
Lead Time: DNS or wireless policy change within 5 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Malicious domain block acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Emergency block in place within 1 hour / standard change in 5 business days
Escalation Path: A DNS hijack, rogue access point at a critical site, or NAC failure open escalates to the network lead and the SOC.
Threats Addressed: Unknown devices plugged into networks, non-compliant endpoints, and attackers with physical network access.
KPIs and Metrics: Ports under NAC enforcement, unknown devices quarantined, and posture failures remediated.

Name: Application Allowlisting
Summary: Allow only approved executables, scripts, and installers to run on endpoints and servers.
Description: Policies start in audit mode, move to enforcement by device group, and use a software approval workflow for new requests. This blocks most commodity malware and unapproved tools.
In Scope: Allowlisting policies that only let approved executables, scripts, and installers run on endpoints and servers.
Out of Scope: Software licensing, application packaging, and EDR alert triage.
Deliverables: An allowlist policy per device group, a software approval workflow, and a weekly blocked-execution report.
Prerequisites: An application control tool, a software inventory, and a pilot group for audit mode.
Lead Time: New device population covered within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Blocked-business-app ticket acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Standard allowlist or rule change within 2 business days
Escalation Path: A policy that blocks a critical business app at scale, or a mass policy disablement, escalates to the endpoint lead and the service desk lead.
Threats Addressed: Unapproved software, malware execution, living-off-the-land scripts, and ransomware binaries.
KPIs and Metrics: Devices in enforce mode, blocked executions per week, and approval requests completed within SLA.

Name: Host Firewall Management
Summary: Set host firewall baselines and manage rule exceptions for workstations and servers.
Description: A central baseline limits inbound services on every host and slows lateral movement. Exceptions are recorded with an end date. Network and cloud firewalls are separate services.
In Scope: Host firewall baselines, rule exceptions, and central policy for workstations and servers.
Out of Scope: Network firewall rules, cloud security groups, and EDR network isolation.
Deliverables: A host firewall baseline per platform, an exception register, and a compliance report.
Prerequisites: Central firewall management through endpoint tools, a device inventory, and application port requirements.
Lead Time: New device population covered within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Blocked-business-app ticket acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Standard allowlist or rule change within 2 business days
Escalation Path: A policy that blocks a critical business app at scale, or a mass policy disablement, escalates to the endpoint lead and the service desk lead.
Threats Addressed: Lateral movement, exposed remote services, and worm propagation between hosts.
KPIs and Metrics: Devices with baseline applied, exceptions past expiry, and inbound open ports per host.

Name: Connected-Device Inventory
Summary: Discover and record IoT and connected devices such as printers, cameras, sensors, and smart displays.
Description: Network discovery finds devices that never went through IT, and each device class gets an owner. The inventory is the starting point for patching and isolation.
In Scope: Discovering and recording IoT and connected devices, such as printers, cameras, sensors, and smart displays.
Out of Scope: Purchasing devices, IT asset depreciation, and OT control system inventory.
Deliverables: A connected-device inventory, an owner per device class, and a monthly new-device report.
Prerequisites: Network discovery tools, switch and DHCP data, and owner contacts.
Lead Time: New device class assessed within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Connected-device issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Isolation of a vulnerable device within 2 business days / firmware plan within 10 business days
Escalation Path: An unmanaged connected device with a known exploited flaw escalates to the security engineering lead and the device owner.
Threats Addressed: Unknown devices on corporate networks, unmanaged default credentials, and forgotten devices.
KPIs and Metrics: Devices with an owner, unknown devices found, and inventory accuracy at sample check.

Name: Firmware Security
Summary: Keep connected-device and endpoint firmware current, signed, and on supported versions.
Description: A baseline per model, vendor update feeds, and a currency report show which devices carry exploitable firmware or are past vendor support.
In Scope: Firmware currency, signing, and update processes for connected devices and endpoint hardware.
Out of Scope: Operating system patching, device replacement funding, and vendor support contracts.
Deliverables: A firmware baseline per model, a firmware currency report, and update procedures.
Prerequisites: A device inventory by model, vendor update feeds, and a test device.
Lead Time: New device class assessed within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Connected-device issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Isolation of a vulnerable device within 2 business days / firmware plan within 10 business days
Escalation Path: An unmanaged connected device with a known exploited flaw escalates to the security engineering lead and the device owner.
Threats Addressed: Exploitable firmware flaws, unsigned firmware, and devices beyond vendor support.
KPIs and Metrics: Devices on current firmware, devices with known exploited flaws, and end-of-support counts.

Name: Connected-Device Isolation
Summary: Place IoT and connected devices in restricted segments that allow only the traffic they need.
Description: Each device class has allowed flows, and everything else is blocked. A compromised camera or printer then cannot be used to reach the rest of the network.
In Scope: Placing IoT and connected devices in restricted network segments with only the traffic they need.
Out of Scope: Network core redesign, NAC deployment, and device purchasing.
Deliverables: A connected-device segment design, allowed-flow rules per class, and an isolation verification report.
Prerequisites: Device inventory, segment capacity on switches and Wi-Fi, and network team support.
Lead Time: New device class assessed within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Connected-device issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Isolation of a vulnerable device within 2 business days / firmware plan within 10 business days
Escalation Path: An unmanaged connected device with a known exploited flaw escalates to the security engineering lead and the device owner.
Threats Addressed: Compromised IoT devices used to pivot, botnet recruitment, and data leaks from smart devices.
KPIs and Metrics: Devices in isolated segments, flows outside policy, and isolation test pass rate.

Name: Cloud Asset Inventory
Summary: Keep a continuous inventory of cloud accounts, resources, owners, and tags across providers.
Description: Every account is connected to the inventory and every resource should carry an owner tag. Unknown accounts and unowned internet-facing resources are flagged first.
In Scope: Continuous inventory of cloud accounts, resources, owners, and tags across providers.
Out of Scope: Cloud cost optimization, application architecture, and CMDB for on-premises assets.
Deliverables: A cloud asset inventory, an untagged or unowned resource report, and an account register.
Prerequisites: Read access to all cloud accounts, a tagging standard, and an inventory or CSPM tool.
Lead Time: New cloud account or subscription covered within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Critical cloud finding flagged the same business day
SLA Resolution Target: Critical finding assigned to an owner within 2 business days
Escalation Path: An unknown internet-facing cloud asset or a runtime compromise escalates to the cloud security lead and the SOC the same day.
Threats Addressed: Shadow cloud accounts, forgotten resources exposed to the internet, and assets with no owner.
KPIs and Metrics: Accounts connected, resources with owner tags, and unknown accounts found.

Name: Serverless Security
Summary: Set and check security baselines for serverless functions, including permissions, secrets, and dependencies.
Description: Functions are checked for overprivileged roles, secrets in environment variables, vulnerable dependencies, and unvalidated event sources. Writing the function code stays with the owning team.
In Scope: Security baselines for functions, including permissions, secrets, dependencies, and event source controls.
Out of Scope: Writing the function code, platform cost management, and API product design.
Deliverables: A serverless security baseline, a function permission review, and a dependency scan report.
Prerequisites: Function inventory, deployment pipeline access, and scanning tools.
Lead Time: New function app onboarded to scanning within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Function security review acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Baseline findings returned within 5 business days
Escalation Path: A production function with admin-level cloud permissions, or a secret exposed in its configuration, escalates to the cloud security lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Overprivileged function roles, injected events, vulnerable dependencies, and leaked secrets in environment variables.
KPIs and Metrics: Functions meeting baseline, overprivileged roles, and critical dependency findings.

Name: Workload Runtime Monitoring
Summary: Run runtime sensors on cloud VMs and containers to catch malicious processes, drift, and exploitation.
Description: Sensors watch running workloads for reverse shells, cryptomining, and container escapes, and send alerts to the SOC. Building container images is a separate service.
In Scope: Runtime sensors on cloud VMs and containers that detect malicious processes, drift, and exploitation.
Out of Scope: Building container images, application performance monitoring, and incident command.
Deliverables: Runtime detection rules, a workload coverage report, and escalated runtime alerts.
Prerequisites: Agent or agentless sensor deployment, workload inventory, and SOC integration.
Lead Time: New cloud account or subscription covered within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Critical cloud finding flagged the same business day
SLA Resolution Target: Critical finding assigned to an owner within 2 business days
Escalation Path: An unknown internet-facing cloud asset or a runtime compromise escalates to the cloud security lead and the SOC the same day.
Threats Addressed: Cryptomining, container escape, reverse shells, and exploitation of web workloads.
KPIs and Metrics: Workloads with runtime coverage, mean time to triage, and confirmed runtime incidents.

Name: Cloud Entitlement Review
Summary: Review human and machine permissions in cloud accounts against actual use and least privilege.
Description: Access analyzers show unused permissions and privilege escalation paths. Account owners keep or remove each one, and dormant admin roles are cleaned up.
In Scope: Reviewing human and machine permissions in cloud accounts against actual use and least privilege.
Out of Scope: Workforce application recertification, cloud cost reviews, and role design for SaaS apps.
Deliverables: An entitlement review report, unused permission recommendations, and reviewer decisions.
Prerequisites: An entitlement management tool or access analyzer, account owners, and permission usage logs.
Lead Time: New cloud account added to entitlement reviews within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Review issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Review completed within 15 business days / unused privileged rights removed within 5 business days
Escalation Path: An unreviewed admin entitlement in a production cloud account escalates to the platform owner and the identity lead.
Threats Addressed: Overprivileged cloud identities, dormant admin roles, and privilege escalation paths.
KPIs and Metrics: Unused permissions removed, admin roles reviewed, and escalation paths closed.

Name: Workload Identity Management
Summary: Manage the lifecycle and least privilege of workload identities, service principals, and federated credentials.
Description: Workloads move from long-lived keys to federated, short-lived credentials, and orphaned service identities are removed. Human account provisioning is separate.
In Scope: Lifecycle and least privilege for workload identities, service principals, roles, and federated credentials.
Out of Scope: Human account provisioning, secrets vault operation, and application code changes.
Deliverables: A workload identity standard, a service identity inventory, and a stale identity cleanup report.
Prerequisites: Cloud identity APIs, deployment pipeline integration, and owner tags for workloads.
Lead Time: New workload moved to federated identity within 5 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Workload identity request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Federated identity configured within 5 business days / exposed key rotated within 4 hours
Escalation Path: A long-lived key for a production workload found in code or logs escalates to the platform owner and the SOC for rotation.
Threats Addressed: Long-lived keys for workloads, orphaned service principals, and lateral movement through workload roles.
KPIs and Metrics: Workloads using federated identity, long-lived keys remaining, and orphaned identities removed.

Name: Single Sign-On
Summary: Federate workforce applications to the identity provider with SAML or OIDC and set session policy.
Description: Applications are onboarded to SSO with a checklist, and apps that still use local passwords are listed for migration. MFA authenticator support is a separate service.
In Scope: Federating workforce applications to the identity provider with SAML or OIDC, including onboarding and session policy.
Out of Scope: MFA authenticator support, customer login, and application role design inside each app.
Deliverables: An SSO onboarding checklist, an application federation register, and a list of apps outside SSO.
Prerequisites: An identity provider, application support for federation, and an app owner.
Lead Time: New application onboarded within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: SSO outage acknowledged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Login outage restored within 1 hour / standard onboarding in 10 business days
Escalation Path: A widespread SSO outage, or a federation trust change outside change control, escalates to the identity on-call and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Password reuse across apps, unmanaged local accounts, and session hijacking.
KPIs and Metrics: Applications behind SSO, apps still with local passwords, and onboarding time.

Name: Credential Policy Management
Summary: Set password and authenticator policy for workforce accounts, including breached-password checks.
Description: The policy follows current guidance: long passphrases, no forced periodic changes, and blocking of known-breached passwords. Accounts found with breached passwords are reset.
In Scope: Password, passphrase, and authenticator policies for workforce accounts, including breached password checks.
Out of Scope: Customer account policy, privileged vaulting, and helpdesk password resets.
Deliverables: A credential policy standard, directory settings evidence, and a breached credential detection report.
Prerequisites: Directory admin access, a breached password list or service, and policy approval.
Lead Time: Policy change scheduled within 10 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Policy change request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved policy change applied within 10 business days / breached password reset forced within 1 business day
Escalation Path: A password spraying or credential stuffing campaign against workforce accounts escalates to the identity on-call and the SOC.
Threats Addressed: Password spraying, credential stuffing, weak or reused passwords, and stale credentials.
KPIs and Metrics: Accounts compliant with policy, breached passwords found and reset, and policy exceptions.

Name: Access Role Engineering
Summary: Mine current access and design business roles that bundle permissions by job function.
Description: Role mining and owner workshops produce a role model per application, so new joiners get role-based access instead of copying a colleague. Running access reviews is a separate service.
In Scope: Mining current access and designing business roles that bundle permissions by job function.
Out of Scope: Application coding, HR job architecture, and running access reviews.
Deliverables: A role model per application, a role mining report, and role definitions with owners.
Prerequisites: Entitlement exports, HR job data, and business owner workshops.
Lead Time: Role engineering engagement for a new application within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Role design request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft role model within 15 business days / SoD rule change within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A toxic combination granted in a financial system escalates to the identity lead and the control owner.
Threats Addressed: Excessive access from copy-a-user requests, role explosion, and access nobody can explain.
KPIs and Metrics: Access granted through roles, roles with owners, and direct entitlements reduced.

Name: Separation-of-Duties Enforcement
Summary: Define conflicting permission pairs and block or mitigate them at provisioning and review.
Description: An SoD rule set for key financial and operational systems stops one person from controlling a whole process. Approved exceptions need a mitigating control that the control owner monitors.
In Scope: Defining conflicting permission pairs and enforcing them at provisioning and review.
Out of Scope: Financial audit testing, fraud investigations, and application role redesign.
Deliverables: An SoD rule set, a violation report, and mitigating control records for approved exceptions.
Prerequisites: Entitlement data for key systems, business process owners, and an identity governance tool.
Lead Time: SoD rules for a newly in-scope application defined within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: SoD exception request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Exception decision within 3 business days / detected violation routed to the control owner within 1 business day
Escalation Path: A toxic combination in a financial system with no mitigating control escalates to the control owner and internal audit.
Threats Addressed: Fraud by a single person controlling a whole process, and unauthorized payments or changes.
KPIs and Metrics: SoD violations open, exceptions with mitigating controls, and violations blocked at request.

Name: Network Traffic Monitoring
Summary: Detect threats in network traffic using flow, packet, and metadata analysis at key network points.
Description: Sensors at the internet edge and core give the SOC visibility of command-and-control, lateral movement, and exfiltration that endpoint tools may miss.
In Scope: Network detection and response using flow, packet, and metadata analysis at key network points.
Out of Scope: Network performance monitoring, firewall rule changes, and full packet capture retention beyond the agreed period.
Deliverables: A sensor placement map, network detection rules, and a weekly network alert digest.
Prerequisites: Sensors or taps at internet and core points, flow logs, and SIEM integration.
Lead Time: New data source or use case onboarded within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: High-severity alert triaged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Confirmed incident escalated within 30 minutes / tuning request in 5 business days
Escalation Path: A detection that indicates active intrusion escalates to the incident commander immediately.
Threats Addressed: Command-and-control traffic, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and scanning from inside.
KPIs and Metrics: Network segments monitored, confirmed detections, and sensor uptime.

Name: Security Event Correlation
Summary: Combine events from many sources into higher-confidence SIEM alerts.
Description: Correlation rules join identity, endpoint, and network signals so a multi-stage attack shows up as one alert, not ten unrelated ones. Rules are tested and reviewed quarterly.
In Scope: SIEM correlation rules that combine events from many sources into higher-confidence alerts.
Out of Scope: Writing source-specific detections, log pipeline engineering, and incident command.
Deliverables: A correlation rule library, rule test records, and a quarterly correlation effectiveness review.
Prerequisites: Normalized logs in the SIEM, an asset and identity context feed, and detection engineering support.
Lead Time: New data source or use case onboarded within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: High-severity alert triaged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Confirmed incident escalated within 30 minutes / tuning request in 5 business days
Escalation Path: A detection that indicates active intrusion escalates to the incident commander immediately.
Threats Addressed: Multi-stage attacks missed by single alerts, alert floods hiding real incidents, and slow triage.
KPIs and Metrics: Alerts reduced through correlation, correlated incidents confirmed, and rule false positive rate.

Name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics
Summary: Baseline users, hosts, and service accounts and flag anomalies such as impossible travel or unusual access.
Description: UEBA models compare activity with each entity's own history and its peers and send anomalies to analysts. It does not track productivity.
In Scope: Behavioral baselines for users, hosts, and service accounts that flag anomalies like impossible travel or unusual access.
Out of Scope: HR monitoring of productivity, insider case adjudication, and identity provisioning.
Deliverables: UEBA models and thresholds, anomaly alert records, and a monthly model tuning report.
Prerequisites: Identity, endpoint, and access logs, a UEBA engine, and peer group data.
Lead Time: New data source or use case onboarded within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: High-severity alert triaged within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Confirmed incident escalated within 30 minutes / tuning request in 5 business days
Escalation Path: A detection that indicates active intrusion escalates to the incident commander immediately.
Threats Addressed: Compromised accounts, insider misuse, and service account abuse.
KPIs and Metrics: Anomalies investigated, true positive rate, and time to triage.

Name: Cyber Response Playbook Development
Summary: Write and maintain incident playbooks for ransomware, BEC, cloud compromise, and other likely scenarios.
Description: Playbooks set out roles, decisions, and legal steps so response is consistent at 3 a.m. They are tested in exercises and updated after real incidents.
In Scope: Writing and maintaining incident playbooks for ransomware, BEC, cloud compromise, insider data theft, and other scenarios.
Out of Scope: Running incidents, tabletop facilitation, and building automation in the SOAR platform.
Deliverables: A playbook library, a version history per playbook, and a gap list of scenarios without playbooks.
Prerequisites: Threat scenarios, team roles, and input from IT and legal.
Lead Time: New playbook drafted within 20 business days. Retainer review within 30 days of renewal notice.
SLA Response Target: Playbook request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft playbook within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A missing playbook for a high-likelihood scenario, or a lapsed retainer, escalates to the incident response lead and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Slow or inconsistent response, missed legal steps, and improvised containment.
KPIs and Metrics: Scenarios with current playbooks, playbooks tested in exercises, and playbook updates after incidents.

Name: Incident Response Retainer Management
Summary: Manage external IR retainers, including scope, hours, engagement steps, and readiness reviews.
Description: The team knows who may call the retainer, how fast the firm responds, and whether the insurer's panel allows it. Hours used and an annual readiness check are tracked.
In Scope: Managing external IR retainers, including scope, hours, engagement steps, and annual readiness reviews.
Out of Scope: Leading the incident, cyber insurance negotiation, and law firm selection.
Deliverables: A retainer summary card, an engagement procedure, and an annual readiness check report.
Prerequisites: A signed retainer, insurer panel requirements, and named authorized callers.
Lead Time: New playbook drafted within 20 business days. Retainer review within 30 days of renewal notice.
SLA Response Target: Playbook request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft playbook within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A missing playbook for a high-likelihood scenario, or a lapsed retainer, escalates to the incident response lead and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Delays engaging outside responders, unpaid or unused retainer hours, and panel conflicts with insurers.
KPIs and Metrics: Time to engage the retainer, hours used versus purchased, and readiness checks done.

Name: Cyber System Restoration
Summary: Restore systems after a cyber incident from clean sources and confirm the threat is gone.
Description: Systems are rebuilt or restored from verified clean backups or images and checked against indicators of compromise before return to service, so the attacker does not come back with them.
In Scope: Restoring systems after a cyber incident from clean sources with validation that the threat is gone.
Out of Scope: Disaster recovery for non-cyber events, application redevelopment, and insurance claims.
Deliverables: A restoration plan, clean-build verification records, and a return-to-service sign-off.
Prerequisites: Clean backups or images, IOC lists, and system owner availability.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Engaged on incident declaration.
SLA Response Target: Recovery lead engaged within 1 hour of containment
SLA Resolution Target: Critical service restored within agreed recovery objective / review held within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A restoration that would reintroduce the attacker, or misses recovery objectives, escalates to the incident commander and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Reinfection after restore, restoring backdoored systems, and extended outage.
KPIs and Metrics: Systems restored within objective, reinfections, and validation checks passed.

Name: Post-Incident Review
Summary: Run blameless reviews after significant incidents and track the improvements they produce.
Description: Reviews build the timeline, find root causes, and assign owned actions within two weeks of closure. They improve the system, not assign blame.
In Scope: Blameless reviews after significant incidents with root cause, timeline, and tracked improvements.
Out of Scope: Disciplinary action, legal liability findings, and running the incident.
Deliverables: A post-incident report, a timeline, and an action tracker with owners.
Prerequisites: Incident records, participant availability, and an independent facilitator.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Engaged on incident declaration.
SLA Response Target: Review scheduled within 5 business days of incident closure
SLA Resolution Target: Post-incident report and action list within 10 business days of closure
Escalation Path: Actions that are still unowned or unfunded 30 days after the review escalate to the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Repeat incidents and lessons not applied.
KPIs and Metrics: Reviews held within 10 business days, actions closed on time, and repeat root causes.

Name: Security Incident Communications
Summary: Manage internal and external communication during cyber incidents.
Description: Stakeholders get regular, consistent updates through out-of-band channels if needed. Legal approves external wording. Media spokesperson duties stay with corporate communications.
In Scope: Internal and external communication during cyber incidents, including status updates, stakeholder briefings, and holding statements.
Out of Scope: Legal notification decisions, media spokesperson duties, and customer support staffing.
Deliverables: A communications plan, stakeholder update templates, and an incident communications log.
Prerequisites: A stakeholder list, legal and comms contacts, and out-of-band communication channels.
Lead Time: Standing incident service. Engaged on incident declaration.
SLA Response Target: First stakeholder update within 1 hour of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Updates issued at the agreed cadence until closure / external statements approved by legal before release
Escalation Path: A leak of incident details, or a statement needed before facts are confirmed, escalates to the incident commander, legal, and corporate communications.
Threats Addressed: Leaked incident details, confusion among staff, and reputational damage from inconsistent messages.
KPIs and Metrics: Updates issued on schedule, stakeholders reached, and corrections needed after release.

Name: Vulnerability Disclosure Intake
Summary: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and run intake, triage, and researcher communication.
Description: Outside researchers have a clear way to report flaws and get a timely reply, which reduces the chance they go public first. Paid bug bounty management is not included.
In Scope: A public vulnerability disclosure policy, intake channel, triage, and researcher communication.
Out of Scope: Paid bug bounty program management, internal scanning, and legal safe harbor decisions.
Deliverables: A published disclosure policy, a report tracker, and a quarterly disclosure summary.
Prerequisites: A security contact address or form, a triage owner, and legal approval of the policy.
Lead Time: Disclosure channel live from day one. Researcher report triaged within 5 business days.
SLA Response Target: Researcher report acknowledged within 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Triage decision within 5 business days / fix status update every 30 days
Escalation Path: A report of an actively exploited flaw, or a researcher threatening public disclosure, escalates to the product security lead and legal.
Threats Addressed: Unreported flaws exploited in the wild, researchers going public first, and lost reports.
KPIs and Metrics: Reports acknowledged on time, valid reports, and time to fix.

Name: Security Strategy Development
Summary: Build a multi-year security strategy tied to business goals, threats, and risk appetite.
Description: The strategy sets a few clear objectives with measures, built from business strategy, the risk register, and leadership interviews. Project plans and budgets follow from it.
In Scope: A multi-year security strategy tied to business goals, threats, and risk appetite.
Out of Scope: Detailed project plans, budget approval, and technology product selection.
Deliverables: A security strategy document, strategic objectives with measures, and an executive briefing.
Prerequisites: Business strategy input, risk register, and leadership interviews.
Lead Time: Strategy refresh cycle starts within 20 business days of a request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft deliverable within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A strategic decision that conflicts with board risk appetite escalates to the CISO and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Spending that does not reduce key risks and security that lags business change.
KPIs and Metrics: Objectives with measures, strategy reviewed annually, and initiatives traced to objectives.

Name: Security Business Alignment
Summary: Meet business units regularly to align security priorities with their plans and risks.
Description: A named relationship owner per business unit keeps security informed of new initiatives early and keeps the business informed of security priorities. Risk acceptance stays with the business.
In Scope: Regular engagement with business units to align security priorities with their plans and risks.
Out of Scope: Business unit IT delivery, project funding, and risk acceptance on their behalf.
Deliverables: Business alignment notes, a business unit priority map, and an annual alignment summary.
Prerequisites: Business unit leaders, current strategy, and a relationship owner per unit.
Lead Time: Strategy refresh cycle starts within 20 business days of a request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft deliverable within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A strategic decision that conflicts with board risk appetite escalates to the CISO and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Security blocking business plans, surprises from new initiatives, and unmanaged business risk.
KPIs and Metrics: Business units engaged per year, priorities agreed, and late-engagement projects.

Name: Security Executive Reporting
Summary: Report security posture, risk, incidents, and program progress to executives and the board.
Description: A quarterly report and board pack focus on decisions needed and material risk, not raw operational metrics. Questions from the board are tracked to closure.
In Scope: Periodic reporting to executives and the board on security posture, risk, incidents, and program progress.
Out of Scope: Detailed operational metrics, regulatory filings, and incident response.
Deliverables: A quarterly executive report, a board briefing pack, and a decisions requested log.
Prerequisites: Metrics feeds, risk register, and a reporting calendar.
Lead Time: Strategy refresh cycle starts within 20 business days of a request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Draft deliverable within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A strategic decision that conflicts with board risk appetite escalates to the CISO and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Leadership unaware of material risk and decisions made without security input.
KPIs and Metrics: Reports issued on schedule, decisions captured, and board questions closed.

Name: Security Roles Definition
Summary: Define security roles, responsibilities, and a RACI across the organization.
Description: The RACI shows who owns each control and duty, and gaps are listed until someone accepts them. Hiring and team structure remain management decisions.
In Scope: Defining security roles, responsibilities, and RACI across the organization.
Out of Scope: HR job grading, hiring decisions, and team structure design.
Deliverables: A security RACI, role descriptions, and a gap list of unassigned responsibilities.
Prerequisites: Organization charts, control framework, and leader input.
Lead Time: Charter or role change drafted within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved role or charter update within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A gap in accountability for a critical control escalates to the CISO and the governance committee chair.
Threats Addressed: Controls nobody owns and duplicated or conflicting responsibilities.
KPIs and Metrics: Controls with an owner, roles reviewed per year, and unassigned responsibilities.

Name: Governance Committee Operations
Summary: Run the security governance committee with agendas, papers, decisions, and action tracking.
Description: The committee has a charter, an executive chair, and a calendar. Decisions and actions are recorded, which provides oversight evidence for audit.
In Scope: Running the security governance committee with agendas, papers, decisions, and action tracking.
Out of Scope: Board committee operations, project steering groups, and audit committee papers.
Deliverables: A committee charter, meeting packs, and a decisions and actions register.
Prerequisites: An executive chair, members named, and a meeting calendar.
Lead Time: Charter or role change drafted within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved role or charter update within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A gap in accountability for a critical control escalates to the CISO and the governance committee chair.
Threats Addressed: Risk decisions made informally, unresolved escalations, and lack of oversight evidence.
KPIs and Metrics: Meetings held per year, actions closed on time, and decisions recorded.

Name: Delegation of Authority
Summary: Record who may approve security exceptions, risk acceptance, and related spending at each level.
Description: A delegation matrix sets approval thresholds that line up with corporate delegation and risk appetite. It is reviewed every year and tested by audit.
In Scope: Recording who may approve security exceptions, risk acceptance, and spending at each level.
Out of Scope: Corporate finance delegation, contract signing authority, and HR approvals.
Deliverables: A security delegation of authority matrix, approval thresholds, and an annual review record.
Prerequisites: Risk appetite, corporate delegation policy, and executive approval.
Lead Time: Charter or role change drafted within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved role or charter update within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A gap in accountability for a critical control escalates to the CISO and the governance committee chair.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized risk acceptance and approvals by people without authority.
KPIs and Metrics: Approvals within delegation, matrix reviewed per year, and exceptions found by audit.

Name: Risk Analysis
Summary: Analyze security risks to rate likelihood and impact on a consistent method.
Description: Analysts apply the agreed method with the risk owner and record the evidence behind each rating. Ratings feed the register and treatment planning.
In Scope: Qualitative or quantitative analysis of security risks to rate likelihood and impact.
Out of Scope: Implementing controls, audit testing, and enterprise financial risk.
Deliverables: A risk analysis record, risk ratings with rationale, and register entries.
Prerequisites: A risk methodology, asset and threat input, and owner participation.
Lead Time: Risk assessment scheduled within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment or decision record within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A risk rated critical, or an acceptance beyond appetite, escalates to the CISO and the risk committee.
Threats Addressed: Underestimated risks, inconsistent ratings, and decisions without analysis.
KPIs and Metrics: Risks analyzed per quarter, ratings challenged, and analyses with documented evidence.

Name: Threat Scenario Analysis
Summary: Analyze realistic attack scenarios, such as ransomware or payment fraud, against key services.
Description: Each scenario is written up with impact estimates and notes on how well current controls would hold. Scenarios keep risk work tied to attacks that actually happen.
In Scope: Scenario-based analysis of realistic attacks against key services, such as ransomware or payment fraud.
Out of Scope: Threat intelligence collection, red team testing, and crisis exercises.
Deliverables: Threat scenario write-ups, impact estimates, and control effectiveness notes per scenario.
Prerequisites: Threat intelligence, critical service maps, and control owners.
Lead Time: Risk assessment scheduled within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment or decision record within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A risk rated critical, or an acceptance beyond appetite, escalates to the CISO and the risk committee.
Threats Addressed: Unprepared response to likely attacks and controls focused on the wrong threats.
KPIs and Metrics: Scenarios analyzed, scenarios linked to treatment, and scenarios refreshed annually.

Name: Treatment Planning
Summary: Choose and plan risk treatment actions with owners, budgets, and target dates.
Description: Each analyzed risk gets a treatment option and a plan, tracked monthly. Overdue actions and changes in residual risk are reported to the risk owner.
In Scope: Choosing and planning risk treatment actions with owners, budgets, and target dates.
Out of Scope: Delivering the projects, budget approval, and risk acceptance.
Deliverables: A treatment plan per risk, an action tracker, and a monthly treatment progress report.
Prerequisites: Analyzed risks, owners, and funding options.
Lead Time: Risk assessment scheduled within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment or decision record within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A risk rated critical, or an acceptance beyond appetite, escalates to the CISO and the risk committee.
Threats Addressed: Risks that stay open indefinitely and treatment that does not reduce risk.
KPIs and Metrics: Treatment actions on schedule, overdue actions, and residual risk change.

Name: Risk Acceptance
Summary: Run a formal process for owners to accept residual risk with an expiry, conditions, and the right approver.
Description: Acceptances are approved at the level the delegation matrix requires and expire, so accepted risk is reviewed again rather than forgotten.
In Scope: A formal process for owners to accept residual risk with expiry, conditions, and the right approval level.
Out of Scope: Risk analysis, exception approvals for technical standards, and insurance decisions.
Deliverables: A risk acceptance form, an acceptance register with expiry, and an expiry report.
Prerequisites: Delegation of authority, risk analysis, and owner sign-off.
Lead Time: Risk assessment scheduled within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Acceptance request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Decision recorded within 10 business days / expiry reminders 30 days ahead
Escalation Path: An acceptance above the requester's delegation, or beyond risk appetite, escalates to the CISO and the risk committee.
Threats Addressed: Silent risk acceptance, expired acceptances, and acceptance beyond appetite.
KPIs and Metrics: Acceptances with expiry, expired acceptances, and acceptances renewed after review.
Approver: Executive risk owner per delegation of authority

Name: Risk Transfer and Cyber Insurance
Summary: Support cyber insurance renewal and other risk transfer with accurate control evidence and coverage review.
Description: Security answers underwriting questionnaires with evidenced controls, reviews coverage against material scenarios, and flags gaps before renewal. Buying the policy and handling claims stay with finance and the broker.
In Scope: Cyber insurance coverage review, underwriting questionnaires, and contractual risk transfer.
Out of Scope: Buying the policy, claims handling, and legal opinions on coverage.
Deliverables: An insurance coverage summary, completed underwriting responses, and a coverage gap note.
Prerequisites: Broker access, control evidence, and finance contacts.
Lead Time: Renewal support starts 90 days before the policy renewal date.
SLA Response Target: Broker or underwriter question acknowledged within 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Evidenced underwriting responses returned 30 days before renewal
Escalation Path: A coverage gap for a material scenario, or a control answer that cannot be evidenced, escalates to the CISO and the CFO before submission.
Threats Addressed: Uninsured losses, denied claims due to inaccurate answers, and coverage gaps.
KPIs and Metrics: Underwriting answers verified, coverage gaps identified, and renewal completed on time.

Name: Key Risk Indicators
Summary: Define and track key risk indicators with thresholds that warn when risk is rising.
Description: Each KRI has an owner, a data source, and a threshold that triggers action, so rising risk shows before it turns into an incident.
In Scope: Defining and tracking key risk indicators with thresholds that warn when risk is rising.
Out of Scope: Operational KPIs for single teams, financial risk metrics, and metric tooling purchase.
Deliverables: A KRI catalog with thresholds, a monthly KRI dashboard, and breach notices.
Prerequisites: Risk register, data sources, and owners for each indicator.
Lead Time: New indicator or report added within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Indicator breach flagged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Risk report issued on the agreed cadence
Escalation Path: A key risk indicator breaching its threshold escalates to the risk owner and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Rising risk not noticed until an incident and metrics without action thresholds.
KPIs and Metrics: KRIs with thresholds, breaches actioned, and data feed reliability.

Name: Risk Reporting
Summary: Report top risks, trends, and treatment status to leadership and risk committees.
Description: A quarterly report and heat map give leadership current ratings and treatment status from a maintained register.
In Scope: Regular reporting on top risks, trends, and treatment status to leadership and risk committees.
Out of Scope: Board reporting on non-security risk, audit reports, and incident reports.
Deliverables: A quarterly risk report, a top risk heat map, and a treatment status summary.
Prerequisites: A maintained risk register, KRI data, and reporting calendar.
Lead Time: New indicator or report added within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Indicator breach flagged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Risk report issued on the agreed cadence
Escalation Path: A key risk indicator breaching its threshold escalates to the risk owner and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Leadership unaware of risk changes and risk decisions made on stale data.
KPIs and Metrics: Reports issued on time, risks with current ratings, and actions from report reviews.

Name: Emerging Risk Review
Summary: Scan for emerging technology, regulatory, and threat risks and add them to the register.
Description: A watchlist reviewed every quarter turns new attack methods, laws, and technology shifts into assessed risks before they arrive unannounced.
In Scope: Scanning for emerging technology, regulatory, and threat risks and adding them to the register.
Out of Scope: Threat intelligence operations, regulatory legal advice, and technology research.
Deliverables: An emerging risk watchlist, a quarterly emerging risk briefing, and register additions.
Prerequisites: Threat, regulatory, and technology inputs, and a review forum.
Lead Time: New indicator or report added within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Indicator breach flagged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Risk report issued on the agreed cadence
Escalation Path: A key risk indicator breaching its threshold escalates to the risk owner and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Surprise from new attack methods, new laws, or technology shifts.
KPIs and Metrics: Emerging risks reviewed, risks promoted to the register, and time from emergence to assessment.

Name: Obligations Register
Summary: Keep a register of security and privacy obligations mapped to controls and owners.
Description: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements are mapped once to the controls that meet them, which cuts duplicate audit work. Legal interpretation stays with counsel.
In Scope: A register of security and privacy legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations mapped to controls and owners.
Out of Scope: Legal interpretation, contract drafting, and control testing.
Deliverables: An obligations register, an obligation-to-control map, and owner assignments.
Prerequisites: Legal input, contract inventory, and control framework.
Lead Time: New obligation assessed within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Regulatory question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Impact assessment within 20 business days / regulator request response per regulator deadline
Escalation Path: A missed regulatory deadline, or an adverse regulator finding, escalates to the compliance lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Missed legal obligations, duplicated control work, and audit surprises.
KPIs and Metrics: Obligations mapped to controls, obligations without owner, and register updates.

Name: Regulatory Change Monitoring
Summary: Track new and changing laws, regulations, and standards that affect security obligations.
Description: Changes are logged, assessed for impact within weeks, and tracked to their effective date. A quarterly horizon report keeps leadership ahead of deadlines.
In Scope: Tracking new and changing laws, regulations, and standards that affect security obligations.
Out of Scope: Lobbying, legal advice, and implementing the changes.
Deliverables: A regulatory change log, impact assessments, and a quarterly regulatory horizon report.
Prerequisites: Regulatory feeds, legal contacts, and the obligations register.
Lead Time: New obligation assessed within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Regulatory question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Impact assessment within 20 business days / regulator request response per regulator deadline
Escalation Path: A missed regulatory deadline, or an adverse regulator finding, escalates to the compliance lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Late compliance with new rules and fines for unmet requirements.
KPIs and Metrics: Changes assessed within 20 business days, changes implemented by effective date, and missed changes.

Name: Regulator Engagement
Summary: Coordinate security responses to regulator inquiries, examinations, and information requests.
Description: Requests are logged, answered on time with consistent evidence, and reviewed by legal. An examination readiness pack is kept current.
In Scope: Coordinating security responses to regulator inquiries, examinations, and requests for information.
Out of Scope: Legal representation, breach notification decisions, and public relations.
Deliverables: A regulator request log, coordinated responses with evidence, and an examination readiness pack.
Prerequisites: Regulator contacts, legal coordination, and an evidence library.
Lead Time: New obligation assessed within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Regulatory question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Impact assessment within 20 business days / regulator request response per regulator deadline
Escalation Path: A missed regulatory deadline, or an adverse regulator finding, escalates to the compliance lead and legal immediately.
Threats Addressed: Inconsistent regulator responses, missed deadlines, and examination findings.
KPIs and Metrics: Requests answered on time, examination findings, and repeat findings.

Name: Contract Security Requirements
Summary: Provide standard security schedules and requirements for supplier contracts by service risk.
Description: Procurement and legal get risk-tiered clause sets, so critical suppliers sign enforceable security duties. Deviations are recorded and accepted at the right level.
In Scope: Standard security schedules and requirements for supplier contracts based on service risk.
Out of Scope: Contract negotiation ownership, pricing, and vendor selection.
Deliverables: A security schedule template, risk-tiered clause sets, and a contract review record.
Prerequisites: Procurement intake, vendor risk tier, and legal templates.
Lead Time: Contract security review within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Clause recommendations within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A vendor refusing required security terms for a critical service escalates to the third-party risk lead and legal.
Threats Addressed: Suppliers with no enforceable security duties and weak protection of company data.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical contracts with security schedules, deviations accepted, and review time.

Name: Audit and Notification Clauses
Summary: Put right-to-audit, breach notification, and cooperation clauses into supplier contracts.
Description: Standard clauses set how fast a supplier must report a breach and allow the company to verify controls. A renewal checklist closes gaps in older contracts.
In Scope: Right-to-audit, breach notification timelines, and cooperation clauses in supplier contracts.
Out of Scope: Conducting audits, incident response for the supplier, and insurance terms.
Deliverables: Standard audit and notification clauses, a clause gap report, and a renewal checklist.
Prerequisites: Contract inventory, legal templates, and critical supplier list.
Lead Time: Contract security review within 10 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Clause recommendations within 10 business days
Escalation Path: A vendor refusing required security terms for a critical service escalates to the third-party risk lead and legal.
Threats Addressed: Late notice of supplier breaches and inability to verify supplier controls.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical contracts with notification clauses, notification time in contract, and audit rights exercised.

Name: Vendor Risk Monitoring
Summary: Monitor vendors continuously through ratings, news, certifications, and reassessment triggers.
Description: Critical vendors are watched between assessments, and alerts such as an expired certification or a reported breach trigger reassessment.
In Scope: Ongoing monitoring of vendors through ratings, news, certifications, and reassessment triggers.
Out of Scope: Initial due diligence, contract negotiation, and vendor performance management.
Deliverables: A vendor monitoring dashboard, alert records, and reassessment triggers.
Prerequisites: A vendor inventory with tiers, monitoring tools, and owner contacts.
Lead Time: New critical vendor added to monitoring within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Vendor risk alert acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Vendor incident coordinated within 4 hours / offboarding completed within 10 business days of contract end
Escalation Path: A breach at a critical vendor or a vendor refusing to return data escalates to the third-party risk lead and the business owner.
Threats Addressed: Vendor posture decline, expired certifications, and unnoticed vendor breaches.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical vendors monitored, alerts actioned, and reassessments on time.

Name: Third-Party Incident Coordination
Summary: Coordinate with suppliers when their incident affects company data or services.
Description: The team assesses impact, gets answers from the supplier, and tracks follow-up assurance. The supplier still runs its own investigation.
In Scope: Coordinating with suppliers when they have an incident that affects company data or services.
Out of Scope: Running the supplier's investigation, legal claims, and customer notification.
Deliverables: A supplier incident record, impact assessment, and follow-up assurance actions.
Prerequisites: Supplier contacts, contract notification terms, and the data shared with each supplier.
Lead Time: New critical vendor added to monitoring within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Vendor risk alert acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Vendor incident coordinated within 4 hours / offboarding completed within 10 business days of contract end
Escalation Path: A breach at a critical vendor or a vendor refusing to return data escalates to the third-party risk lead and the business owner.
Threats Addressed: Delayed awareness of supplier breaches, cascading outages, and unmanaged data exposure.
KPIs and Metrics: Supplier incidents assessed within 24 hours, follow-ups closed, and notice time from supplier.

Name: Vendor Offboarding
Summary: End vendor relationships securely, with access removed, data returned or deleted, and assets recovered.
Description: A checklist runs from contract end notice to deletion certificate, so former vendors do not keep access, data, or orphaned integrations.
In Scope: Ending vendor relationships securely, including access removal, data return or deletion, and asset recovery.
Out of Scope: Contract termination negotiation, invoice disputes, and replacement vendor selection.
Deliverables: An offboarding checklist, access removal evidence, and data deletion certificates.
Prerequisites: Contract end notice, a list of vendor access and data, and the business owner.
Lead Time: New critical vendor added to monitoring within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Vendor risk alert acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Vendor incident coordinated within 4 hours / offboarding completed within 10 business days of contract end
Escalation Path: A breach at a critical vendor or a vendor refusing to return data escalates to the third-party risk lead and the business owner.
Threats Addressed: Former vendors retaining access or data and orphaned integrations.
KPIs and Metrics: Offboardings completed on time, access removed, and deletion certificates received.

Name: Supplier Criticality Analysis
Summary: Rate suppliers by how critical they are to operations, data, and security.
Description: Criticality tiers decide how deeply each supplier is assessed and highlight concentration on single vendors. Sourcing strategy stays with procurement.
In Scope: Rating suppliers by how critical they are to operations, data, and security, to set assessment depth.
Out of Scope: Vendor selection, sourcing strategy, and financial health analysis.
Deliverables: A supplier criticality rating, a tiered supplier list, and concentration risk notes.
Prerequisites: Supplier inventory, service mapping, and business owner input.
Lead Time: Supply chain assessment starts within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A critical supplier with no alternative, or a tampered component, escalates to the third-party risk lead and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Under-assessed critical suppliers and concentration risk on single vendors.
KPIs and Metrics: Suppliers tiered, critical suppliers with assessments, and concentration risks noted.

Name: Software Supply Chain Assurance
Summary: Get assurance that acquired software is securely built, signed, maintained, and supplied with SBOMs.
Description: Software suppliers answer a focused questionnaire and provide SBOMs and vulnerability disclosure commitments. The result is a risk summary per critical product.
In Scope: Assurance that acquired software is securely built, signed, maintained, and comes with SBOMs and vulnerability disclosures.
Out of Scope: Internal application security testing, open-source license compliance, and software purchasing.
Deliverables: A software supplier assurance questionnaire, SBOM intake records, and a risk summary per product.
Prerequisites: Software inventory, procurement intake, and vendor contacts.
Lead Time: Supply chain assessment starts within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A critical supplier with no alternative, or a tampered component, escalates to the third-party risk lead and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Compromised updates, vulnerable components, and abandoned software.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical software with SBOMs, vendor attestations received, and critical component findings.

Name: Component Provenance Verification
Summary: Verify that hardware and software components come from authorized sources and have not been tampered with.
Description: Receiving checks and signature verification catch counterfeit hardware, tampered firmware, and malicious packages before they are deployed.
In Scope: Verifying hardware and software components come from authorized sources and have not been tampered with.
Out of Scope: Building components, manufacturing quality, and logistics.
Deliverables: A provenance verification procedure, verification records, and a counterfeit or tamper report.
Prerequisites: Approved supplier lists, receiving inspection, and signature verification tools.
Lead Time: Supply chain assessment starts within 15 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 15 business days
Escalation Path: A critical supplier with no alternative, or a tampered component, escalates to the third-party risk lead and the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Counterfeit hardware, tampered firmware, and malicious packages.
KPIs and Metrics: Components verified, failed verifications, and unauthorized source purchases.

Name: Roadmap Planning
Summary: Build a sequenced security roadmap of initiatives, dependencies, and milestones.
Description: The roadmap turns strategy and risk into a realistic sequence that respects team capacity, with a quarterly status update. Project delivery sits with the initiative owners.
In Scope: A sequenced security roadmap of initiatives, dependencies, and milestones tied to strategy and risk.
Out of Scope: Project delivery, product selection, and budget approval.
Deliverables: A multi-year roadmap, an initiative register, and a quarterly roadmap status update.
Prerequisites: Strategy, risk register, and capacity input.
Lead Time: Planning cycle aligned to the annual budget calendar. Ad hoc requests within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan or assessment delivered within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A roadmap item blocked by funding for a critical risk escalates to the CISO and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Unfocused spending, initiatives competing for the same teams, and delayed risk reduction.
KPIs and Metrics: Initiatives on schedule, roadmap items tied to risks, and changes approved.

Name: Budget and Resource Planning
Summary: Plan security budget, headcount, and partner spend against the roadmap and run costs.
Description: An annual plan and a resource model connect spend to risk areas, and tracking shows variance early. Corporate finance processes still apply.
In Scope: Planning security budget, headcount, and partner spend against the roadmap and run costs.
Out of Scope: Corporate finance processes, purchasing, and hiring decisions.
Deliverables: An annual security budget plan, a resource model, and a spend tracking report.
Prerequisites: Roadmap, current spend, and finance calendar.
Lead Time: Planning cycle aligned to the annual budget calendar. Ad hoc requests within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan or assessment delivered within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A roadmap item blocked by funding for a critical risk escalates to the CISO and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Underfunded critical controls and surprise overspend.
KPIs and Metrics: Budget variance, critical initiatives funded, and spend per risk area.

Name: Capability Maturity Assessment
Summary: Rate the maturity of security capabilities against a model and set improvement targets.
Description: Owners and assessors agree current and target scores with evidence, and the gaps become roadmap input. This is not a certification audit.
In Scope: Rating maturity of security capabilities against a model to set improvement targets.
Out of Scope: External certification audits, control testing, and benchmarking purchases.
Deliverables: A maturity assessment report, current and target scores, and a gap list.
Prerequisites: A maturity model, capability owners, and evidence access.
Lead Time: Planning cycle aligned to the annual budget calendar. Ad hoc requests within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan or assessment delivered within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A roadmap item blocked by funding for a critical risk escalates to the CISO and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Overestimated capability and improvement without priorities.
KPIs and Metrics: Capabilities assessed, gaps closed per year, and target maturity reached.

Name: Security Continuous Improvement Planning
Summary: Gather lessons from incidents, audits, metrics, and exercises into a prioritized improvement plan.
Description: One backlog collects improvement items from every source and is re-planned each quarter, so lessons learned turn into changes.
In Scope: Collecting lessons from incidents, audits, metrics, and exercises into a prioritized improvement plan.
Out of Scope: Running the improvement projects, post-incident review facilitation, and audit testing.
Deliverables: A continuous improvement backlog, a quarterly improvement plan, and progress tracking.
Prerequisites: Inputs from incidents, audits, metrics, and exercises.
Lead Time: Improvement planning cycle runs each quarter.
SLA Response Target: Improvement suggestion acknowledged in 5 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Improvement plan updated each quarter
Escalation Path: An improvement action that stalls for two quarters escalates to the CISO.
Threats Addressed: Repeated findings and lessons that never become changes.
KPIs and Metrics: Improvements delivered per quarter, repeat findings, and backlog age.

Name: Records of Processing Activities
Summary: Keep records of processing activities with purposes, data categories, recipients, transfers, and retention.
Description: Each processing activity has a current record that its process owner attests every year. The register can be exported for a regulator on request.
In Scope: Maintaining records of processing activities with purposes, data categories, recipients, transfers, and retention.
Out of Scope: Data mapping fieldwork, legal advice on each record, and systems inventory outside personal data.
Deliverables: A records of processing register, an annual attestation by process owners, and a regulator-ready export.
Prerequisites: Process owners, data maps, and a privacy management tool or register.
