Summary: Map the people, systems, sites, suppliers, and data each critical process depends on.
Description: Dependency maps show hidden links that would break a recovery plan and are refreshed after major change.
In Scope: Mapping people, systems, sites, suppliers, and data each critical process depends on.
Out of Scope: Network diagrams, application architecture, and supplier contracting.
Deliverables: A dependency map per process, a single dependency list, and an update log.
Prerequisites: Process owners, application inventory, and supplier list.
Lead Time: BIA cycle scheduled within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: BIA results within 20 business days of workshops
Escalation Path: A critical process without agreed recovery objectives escalates to the continuity lead and the business executive.
Threats Addressed: Hidden dependencies that break recovery plans.
KPIs and Metrics: Processes mapped, dependencies validated, and updates after change.

Name: Disruption Scenario Analysis
Summary: Analyze disruption scenarios, such as site loss, cyberattack, or supplier failure, for their impact.
Description: A small set of plausible scenarios is analyzed for impact and tied to continuity strategies.
In Scope: Analyzing disruption scenarios, such as site loss, pandemic, cyberattack, or supplier failure, for impact.
Out of Scope: Threat intelligence, insurance modeling, and crisis exercise delivery.
Deliverables: A scenario set, impact analysis per scenario, and recommended strategies.
Prerequisites: BIA results, risk register, and scenario input.
Lead Time: Assessment starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A single point of failure for a critical service with no mitigation escalates to the continuity lead and executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Unprepared response to plausible disruptions.
KPIs and Metrics: Scenarios analyzed, strategies linked, and scenarios refreshed.

Name: Single-Point-of-Failure Identification
Summary: Find single points of failure in people, technology, sites, and suppliers behind critical processes.
Description: A register of single points of failure with risk ratings and recommended mitigations shows where one loss stops a critical process.
In Scope: Finding single points of failure in people, technology, sites, and suppliers that support critical processes.
Out of Scope: Fixing the points of failure, procurement, and architecture redesign.
Deliverables: A single point of failure register, risk ratings, and recommended mitigations.
Prerequisites: Dependency maps, owner interviews, and supplier data.
Lead Time: Assessment starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Assessment report within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A single point of failure for a critical service with no mitigation escalates to the continuity lead and executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Outages from a single person, system, or supplier.
KPIs and Metrics: Points of failure found, mitigations in place, and open high-risk items.

Name: Continuity Strategy Selection
Summary: Choose continuity strategies, such as workarounds, alternate sites, or manual processing, for each critical process.
Description: Options are compared on cost and ability to meet recovery objectives, and the owner selects one.
In Scope: Choosing continuity strategies, such as workarounds, alternate sites, or manual processing, for each critical process.
Out of Scope: Implementing the strategy, budget approval, and IT recovery engineering.
Deliverables: A strategy options analysis, a selected strategy per process, and cost estimates.
Prerequisites: BIA results, recovery objectives, and owner input.
Lead Time: Strategy work starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Strategy recommendation within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A strategy that cannot meet recovery objectives without new funding escalates to the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Strategies that cannot meet objectives and wasted continuity spend.
KPIs and Metrics: Processes with selected strategies, strategies tested, and cost per process.

Name: Alternate Work Site Arrangements
Summary: Arrange alternate work locations, including remote work, other offices, and recovery seats.
Description: Seat allocations and remote work readiness are tested, so staff know where to go when a site is lost.
In Scope: Arrangements for alternate work locations, including remote work, other offices, and recovery seats.
Out of Scope: Real estate leasing decisions and IT disaster recovery site management.
Deliverables: An alternate site plan, seat allocation lists, and readiness test records.
Prerequisites: Site capacity data, remote work capability, and facilities input.
Lead Time: Strategy work starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Strategy recommendation within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A strategy that cannot meet recovery objectives without new funding escalates to the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Inability to work after site loss.
KPIs and Metrics: Staff with alternate arrangements, readiness tests passed, and seat shortfalls.

Name: Workforce Continuity Arrangements
Summary: Plan for staff shortages with cross-training, succession for key roles, and surge staffing.
Description: Key roles have named backups and cross-training records, so a critical process does not stop when one person is unavailable.
In Scope: Plans for staff shortages, including cross-training, succession for key roles, and surge staffing.
Out of Scope: HR workforce planning, recruitment, and payroll.
Deliverables: Key role succession lists, cross-training records, and a staffing contingency plan.
Prerequisites: Key role list, manager input, and HR coordination.
Lead Time: Strategy work starts within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Strategy recommendation within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A strategy that cannot meet recovery objectives without new funding escalates to the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Loss of key people during disruption.
KPIs and Metrics: Key roles with backups, cross-training completed, and gaps per process.

Name: Continuity Plan Development
Summary: Write business continuity plans with roles, procedures, contacts, and recovery steps for each critical process.
Description: Plans follow a standard format, are approved by the process owner, and are kept in one library. IT recovery runbooks are separate.
In Scope: Writing business continuity plans with roles, procedures, contacts, and recovery steps per critical process.
Out of Scope: IT disaster recovery runbooks, crisis communications strategy, and emergency evacuation plans.
Deliverables: Business continuity plans, plan approval records, and a plan library.
Prerequisites: BIA, selected strategies, and owner availability.
Lead Time: New plan drafted within 20 business days of BIA completion.
SLA Response Target: Plan question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan approved within 30 business days / maintenance updates within 10 business days of change
Escalation Path: A critical process without a current approved plan escalates to the continuity lead and the business executive.
Threats Addressed: Confused response during disruption and missed recovery objectives.
KPIs and Metrics: Plans approved, plans meeting standard, and plans used in exercises.

Name: Continuity Plan Maintenance
Summary: Keep continuity plans current after changes in people, systems, sites, and suppliers.
Description: Plans are refreshed at least yearly and after change triggers, and stale contacts are found before an event, not during it.
In Scope: Keeping plans current after changes in people, systems, sites, and suppliers.
Out of Scope: Writing new plans for new processes and exercise delivery.
Deliverables: A plan maintenance schedule, update records, and stale plan report.
Prerequisites: Plan library, change triggers, and owner reminders.
Lead Time: New plan drafted within 20 business days of BIA completion.
SLA Response Target: Plan question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan approved within 30 business days / maintenance updates within 10 business days of change
Escalation Path: A critical process without a current approved plan escalates to the continuity lead and the business executive.
Threats Addressed: Outdated contacts and procedures that fail during real events.
KPIs and Metrics: Plans updated within 12 months, stale contacts found, and updates after change.

Name: Plan Activation Criteria
Summary: Set clear criteria and authority for activating continuity plans and escalating to crisis management.
Description: An activation matrix says who may invoke a plan and when, so time is not lost arguing during a disruption.
In Scope: Clear criteria and authority for activating continuity plans and escalating to crisis management.
Out of Scope: Running the crisis, IT incident declaration, and emergency services decisions.
Deliverables: Activation criteria, an activation decision log, and an authority matrix.
Prerequisites: Plans, crisis management structure, and leadership agreement.
Lead Time: New plan drafted within 20 business days of BIA completion.
SLA Response Target: Plan question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan approved within 30 business days / maintenance updates within 10 business days of change
Escalation Path: A critical process without a current approved plan escalates to the continuity lead and the business executive.
Threats Addressed: Delayed activation and confusion over who decides.
KPIs and Metrics: Activations within target, criteria used in exercises, and authority disputes.

Name: Supplier Continuity Capability Review
Summary: Review critical suppliers' continuity and recovery capability, plans, and test results.
Description: Suppliers are rated on evidence of real recovery capability, and weak ratings lead to required actions.
In Scope: Reviewing critical suppliers' continuity and recovery capability, plans, and test results.
Out of Scope: Security assessments, commercial negotiations, and supplier selection.
Deliverables: A supplier continuity review, a capability rating, and required actions.
Prerequisites: Critical supplier list, supplier contacts, and contract terms.
Lead Time: Supplier review within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review report within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A critical supplier without credible continuity escalates to the continuity lead and the third-party risk lead.
Threats Addressed: Supplier outages that halt critical processes.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical suppliers reviewed, low ratings, and actions closed.

Name: Supplier Contingency Arrangements
Summary: Prepare contingency options for critical supplier failure, such as alternates, stock buffers, or exit plans.
Description: Each critical supplier has a tested fallback, so a supplier outage does not become a long business outage.
In Scope: Contingency options for critical supplier failure, such as alternate suppliers, stock buffers, or exit plans.
Out of Scope: Sourcing strategy, contract negotiation, and inventory management.
Deliverables: Contingency plans per critical supplier, an alternate supplier list, and exit plan records.
Prerequisites: Supplier criticality ratings, procurement input, and owner engagement.
Lead Time: Supplier review within 20 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review report within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A critical supplier without credible continuity escalates to the continuity lead and the third-party risk lead.
Threats Addressed: Long disruption from a single supplier failure.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical suppliers with contingency, contingencies tested, and exit plans current.

Name: Disaster Recovery Plan Development
Summary: Write IT disaster recovery plans with procedures, roles, and dependencies for each critical system.
Description: DR plans cover every critical system, are approved by the system owner, and are tested on schedule.
In Scope: IT disaster recovery plans with recovery procedures, roles, and dependencies for critical systems.
Out of Scope: Business continuity plans, backup operation, and application redesign.
Deliverables: DR plans per system, a plan approval record, and a DR plan library.
Prerequisites: Recovery objectives, system architecture, and owner availability.
Lead Time: DR plan for a new critical system within 30 business days of go-live.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan or sequence approved within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A critical system with no DR plan, or a sequence that misses recovery objectives, escalates to the infrastructure lead and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Prolonged outages after disasters and improvised recovery.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical systems with plans, plans tested, and plans meeting standard.

Name: Recovery Sequencing
Summary: Order system recovery by dependency and business priority so critical services come back first.
Description: A dependency-ordered runbook keeps teams from restoring an application before the identity, network, and database services it needs.
In Scope: Ordering system recovery by dependency and business priority so critical services come back first.
Out of Scope: Writing individual DR plans, business process prioritization, and change management.
Deliverables: A recovery sequence, a dependency-ordered runbook, and a priority tier list.
Prerequisites: Dependency maps, recovery objectives, and system owners.
Lead Time: DR plan for a new critical system within 30 business days of go-live.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Plan or sequence approved within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A critical system with no DR plan, or a sequence that misses recovery objectives, escalates to the infrastructure lead and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Recovering systems in the wrong order and missed recovery objectives.
KPIs and Metrics: Sequences validated in tests, dependency errors found, and objectives met.

Name: Backup and Replication Operations
Summary: Run backup and replication jobs, monitor success, and fix failures for critical systems.
Description: Job reports and failure tickets keep protection coverage visible, and replication lag is watched against each system's RPO.
In Scope: Running backup and replication jobs, monitoring success, and fixing failures for critical systems.
Out of Scope: Backup access control design, restore validation tests, and storage procurement.
Deliverables: Backup and replication job reports, failure tickets, and a monthly protection coverage report.
Prerequisites: Backup and replication platforms, system inventory, and storage capacity.
Lead Time: New system added to replication within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Replication failure alert acknowledged within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Replication restored within 4 hours / capacity gap plan within 10 business days
Escalation Path: Replication lag beyond RPO on a critical system, or recovery site unavailability, escalates to the infrastructure lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: Data loss beyond tolerance and missing backups when needed.
KPIs and Metrics: Job success rate, systems protected, and replication lag.

Name: Recovery Site Management
Summary: Keep recovery sites or cloud recovery regions ready, with capacity, access, and current configuration.
Description: Readiness checks and drift reports confirm the recovery environment matches production closely enough to use.
In Scope: Maintaining recovery sites or cloud regions with capacity, access, and current configuration.
Out of Scope: Production data center operation, real estate, and business continuity seats.
Deliverables: A recovery site readiness report, configuration drift report, and access test results.
Prerequisites: Recovery site contract or cloud region, configuration management, and access arrangements.
Lead Time: New system added to replication within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Readiness issue acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Drift or access gap fixed within 10 business days
Escalation Path: Replication lag beyond RPO on a critical system, or recovery site unavailability, escalates to the infrastructure lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: Recovery sites that are not ready when needed.
KPIs and Metrics: Readiness checks passed, drift items, and access tests completed.

Name: Recovery Capacity Planning
Summary: Plan the compute, storage, network, and licenses needed to recover critical systems.
Description: A recovery capacity model shows shortfalls before a disaster does and feeds the next budget cycle.
In Scope: Planning compute, storage, network, and license capacity needed to recover critical systems.
Out of Scope: Production capacity planning, budget approval, and procurement.
Deliverables: A recovery capacity model, a shortfall list, and a capacity plan.
Prerequisites: System inventory, recovery objectives, and current capacity data.
Lead Time: Capacity model for a new critical system within 15 business days of DR plan approval.
SLA Response Target: Capacity question acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Shortfall assessment within 10 business days / funded plan in the next budget cycle
Escalation Path: A recovery capacity shortfall that would miss RTO for a tier-0 system escalates to the infrastructure lead and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Recovery that fails because of insufficient capacity.
KPIs and Metrics: Capacity shortfalls, critical systems covered, and plan updated after change.

Name: Failover Execution
Summary: Fail over to recovery sites or regions during a declared disaster.
Description: Failover follows approved DR plans with a running log and status updates. Declaring the disaster is a leadership decision.
In Scope: Executing failover to recovery sites or regions during a declared disaster.
Out of Scope: Deciding to declare a disaster, business process workarounds, and application bug fixes.
Deliverables: A failover log, a status update stream, and a post-failover report.
Prerequisites: Approved DR plans, recovery site readiness, and failover authority.
Lead Time: Standing service. Executed on a DR declaration.
SLA Response Target: Failover team engaged within 30 minutes of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Critical services failed over within RTO / validation complete within 4 hours of recovery
Escalation Path: A failover that will miss RTO, or failback with data loss risk, escalates to the incident commander and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Prolonged outage and data loss during disasters.
KPIs and Metrics: Failovers within RTO, steps failed, and data loss versus RPO.

Name: Failback Coordination
Summary: Coordinate the return from the recovery site to primary with data sync and minimal disruption.
Description: Failback is planned like a change, with sync verification and a window, so the return does not cause a second outage or data loss.
In Scope: Coordinating return from the recovery site to primary with data sync and minimal disruption.
Out of Scope: Failover execution, primary site repair, and business communications strategy.
Deliverables: A failback plan, a data sync verification record, and a failback completion report.
Prerequisites: Repaired primary site, sync capability, and change window.
Lead Time: Standing service. Executed on a DR declaration.
SLA Response Target: Failover team engaged within 30 minutes of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Critical services failed over within RTO / validation complete within 4 hours of recovery
Escalation Path: A failover that will miss RTO, or failback with data loss risk, escalates to the incident commander and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Data loss during failback and second outages.
KPIs and Metrics: Failbacks without data loss, failback duration, and issues found.

Name: Recovered Service Validation
Summary: Confirm recovered services work, their data is complete, and security controls are in place.
Description: Business testers and security checks sign off before users return, so a service is not declared up while still broken or unprotected.
In Scope: Validating recovered services work correctly, data is complete, and security controls are in place.
Out of Scope: User acceptance testing for new features and post-incident review.
Deliverables: A validation checklist, test results per service, and a sign-off record.
Prerequisites: Validation scripts, business testers, and security checks.
Lead Time: Standing service. Executed on a DR declaration.
SLA Response Target: Failover team engaged within 30 minutes of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Critical services failed over within RTO / validation complete within 4 hours of recovery
Escalation Path: A failover that will miss RTO, or failback with data loss risk, escalates to the incident commander and the CIO.
Threats Addressed: Services declared up but not working and recovery without security controls.
KPIs and Metrics: Services validated before release, validation failures, and post-recovery incidents.

Name: Important Service Identification
Summary: Identify important business services whose disruption would harm customers, markets, or the firm.
Description: The board approves a short list of important services with the reasoning recorded, as operational resilience regulators expect.
In Scope: Identifying important business services whose disruption would harm customers, markets, or the firm.
Out of Scope: Process-level BIA, product strategy, and regulatory legal advice.
Deliverables: An important business service list, rationale per service, and board approval record.
Prerequisites: Leadership input, customer impact data, and regulatory expectations.
Lead Time: Service identification cycle within 30 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved service list or tolerances within 30 business days
Escalation Path: An important service operating beyond its impact tolerance escalates to the accountable executive and the board.
Threats Addressed: Disruption to services that matter most to customers and regulators.
KPIs and Metrics: Services identified, approval on time, and annual review completed.

Name: Impact Tolerance Setting
Summary: Set the maximum tolerable disruption for each important business service.
Description: Impact tolerances say how long and how badly a service may be disrupted before harm becomes intolerable, and testing checks they can be met.
In Scope: Setting maximum tolerable disruption for each important business service.
Out of Scope: Building recovery capability and setting IT system RTOs.
Deliverables: Impact tolerance statements, rationale, and board approval.
Prerequisites: Important service list, impact data, and executive input.
Lead Time: Service identification cycle within 30 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved service list or tolerances within 30 business days
Escalation Path: An important service operating beyond its impact tolerance escalates to the accountable executive and the board.
Threats Addressed: Disruption beyond what customers or markets can bear.
KPIs and Metrics: Services with tolerances, tolerances tested, and breaches.

Name: End-to-End Service Mapping
Summary: Map each important service end to end across people, processes, technology, facilities, and suppliers.
Description: End-to-end maps expose weak points that a system-by-system view misses.
In Scope: Mapping each important service end to end across people, processes, technology, facilities, and suppliers.
Out of Scope: Network diagrams and application architecture details.
Deliverables: End-to-end service maps, a vulnerability list, and an update log.
Prerequisites: Service owners, dependency data, and supplier lists.
Lead Time: Service identification cycle within 30 business days of request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved service list or tolerances within 30 business days
Escalation Path: An important service operating beyond its impact tolerance escalates to the accountable executive and the board.
Threats Addressed: Hidden weaknesses that break important services.
KPIs and Metrics: Services mapped, vulnerabilities found, and maps current.

Name: Resilience Self-Assessment
Summary: Produce the annual operational resilience self-assessment against tolerances, mapping, and testing.
Description: The self-assessment pulls mapping, test results, and open gaps into one document for board approval.
In Scope: Annual self-assessment of operational resilience against tolerances, mapping, and testing results.
Out of Scope: External audit and regulatory submission writing by legal.
Deliverables: A resilience self-assessment document, a gap list, and board approval record.
Prerequisites: Service maps, test results, and owner input.
Lead Time: Self-assessment cycle within 30 business days of the annual start.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Self-assessment report within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A resilience gap that leaves a service unable to stay within tolerance escalates to the accountable executive.
Threats Addressed: Regulatory findings and unseen resilience gaps.
KPIs and Metrics: Self-assessment approved on time, gaps found, and gaps closed.

Name: Resilience Gap Remediation
Summary: Plan and track fixes for resilience gaps found through mapping, testing, or incidents.
Description: Gaps become owned actions with dates, reported quarterly until the service can stay within tolerance.
In Scope: Planning and tracking remediation of resilience gaps found through mapping, testing, or incidents.
Out of Scope: Delivering the remediation projects and budget approval.
Deliverables: A remediation plan, an action tracker, and a quarterly progress report.
Prerequisites: Gap list, owners, and funding.
Lead Time: Self-assessment cycle within 30 business days of the annual start.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Self-assessment report within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A resilience gap that leaves a service unable to stay within tolerance escalates to the accountable executive.
Threats Addressed: Services staying unable to meet tolerance.
KPIs and Metrics: Gaps closed on time, overdue actions, and residual gaps.

Name: Exercise Program Planning
Summary: Plan a multi-year exercise program covering critical processes, scenarios, and participants.
Description: The program makes sure every critical plan is exercised over the cycle, not just the convenient ones.
In Scope: Planning a multi-year exercise program covering critical processes, scenarios, and participants.
Out of Scope: Running each exercise and crisis management training.
Deliverables: An exercise program plan, a schedule, and a coverage map.
Prerequisites: Critical process list, scenarios, and leadership support.
Lead Time: Exercise scheduled within 20 business days of the annual plan.
SLA Response Target: Exercise request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Exercise report within 10 business days of the exercise
Escalation Path: An exercise that shows a critical plan cannot work escalates to the continuity lead and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Plans that are never tested and untrained teams.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical processes exercised, exercises run on schedule, and coverage gaps.

Name: Continuity Tabletop Exercises
Summary: Facilitate discussion-based exercises that walk teams through a disruption scenario.
Description: Teams talk through decisions against their plan with a facilitator, and the gaps found become actions.
In Scope: Facilitated discussion-based exercises that walk teams through a disruption scenario.
Out of Scope: Live failover tests and cyber incident tabletop exercises.
Deliverables: An exercise plan, a facilitator guide, and an exercise report with actions.
Prerequisites: Scenario, participants, and plan documents.
Lead Time: Exercise scheduled within 20 business days of the annual plan.
SLA Response Target: Exercise request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Exercise report within 10 business days of the exercise
Escalation Path: An exercise that shows a critical plan cannot work escalates to the continuity lead and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Teams unprepared for decisions during disruption.
KPIs and Metrics: Exercises held, actions raised, and actions closed.

Name: Full-Scale Recovery Exercises
Summary: Run live exercises that move work or systems to alternate arrangements to prove recovery.
Description: Live exercises, with safety controls and a rollback plan, show whether a strategy really works when people use it.
In Scope: Live exercises that move work or systems to alternate arrangements to prove recovery.
Out of Scope: Real disaster recovery and tabletop discussions.
Deliverables: An exercise plan with safety controls, an exercise log, and a results report.
Prerequisites: Approved plan, change window, and leadership support.
Lead Time: Exercise scheduled within 20 business days of the annual plan.
SLA Response Target: Exercise request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Exercise report within 10 business days of the exercise
Escalation Path: An exercise that shows a critical plan cannot work escalates to the continuity lead and the executive sponsor.
Threats Addressed: Recovery strategies that fail when actually used.
KPIs and Metrics: Exercises completed, objectives met, and issues found.

Name: OT Security Policy
Summary: Set the OT security policy and standards for control systems, aligned to IEC 62443-2-1 and NIST SP 800-82.
Description: The policy is the core of the OT cybersecurity management system. It covers remote access, change, removable media, backups, and incident duties, with a site applicability statement for each plant. Process safety procedures stay under IEC 61511.
In Scope: An OT security policy and supporting standards for control systems, aligned to IEC 62443-2-1 and NIST SP 800-82, covering remote access, change, removable media, and incident duties.
Out of Scope: IT security policy, process safety management procedures under IEC 61511, and engineering design standards.
Deliverables: An OT security policy, a site applicability statement per plant, and an annual CSMS review record with exceptions.
Prerequisites: Operations leadership sponsorship, site engineering input, and the corporate policy framework.
Lead Time: Site applicability review within 20 business days. Policy changes follow the annual CSMS review cycle.
SLA Response Target: Policy or governance request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved policy change or RACI update within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A site operating control systems with no named OT security owner escalates to the OT security lead and the plant manager.
Threats Addressed: Unmanaged control system risk, inconsistent practices between plants, and security changes made without regard to safety.
KPIs and Metrics: Sites attesting to the policy, open policy exceptions per site, and policy reviewed within 12 months.

Name: IT/OT Responsibility Model
Summary: Agree who owns each OT security duty across IT, control system engineering, operations, and vendors.
Description: A site-level RACI settles who patches, backs up, monitors, and approves remote access for each system, including what the OEM or system integrator does under contract. Unowned duties are listed until someone takes them.
In Scope: A RACI that splits OT security duties between IT, control system engineering, operations, and system integrators or OEM vendors at each site.
Out of Scope: Organization design, HR job grading, and the commercial terms of vendor service contracts.
Deliverables: An IT/OT RACI, a site responsibility matrix covering patching, backups, monitoring, and remote access, and a list of unowned duties.
Prerequisites: Site leaders, IT and engineering input, and current vendor and integrator service scopes.
Lead Time: Site applicability review within 20 business days. Policy changes follow the annual CSMS review cycle.
SLA Response Target: Policy or governance request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved policy change or RACI update within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A site operating control systems with no named OT security owner escalates to the OT security lead and the plant manager.
Threats Addressed: Gaps where nobody patches or backs up controllers, and conflicting changes from IT and engineering.
KPIs and Metrics: Duties with a named owner, sites with an approved matrix, and incidents traced to unclear ownership.

Name: OT Risk Assessment
Summary: Assess control system cyber risk by zone per IEC 62443-3-2 and set a target security level for each.
Description: Workshops with engineering and operations weigh safety, environmental, and production consequence and set a target security level (SL-T) per zone. The result drives conduit rules, monitoring, and hardening priorities.
In Scope: Initial and detailed cyber risk assessment of control systems per IEC 62443-3-2, setting a target security level per zone and weighing safety, environmental, and production consequence.
Out of Scope: Process hazard analysis facilitation, IT risk assessment, and insurance engineering surveys.
Deliverables: A zone-level risk assessment report, a target security level (SL-T) per zone, and a ranked treatment list.
Prerequisites: An OT asset inventory, current network drawings, and site engineering and operations time for workshops.
Lead Time: Site applicability review within 20 business days. Policy changes follow the annual CSMS review cycle.
SLA Response Target: Policy or governance request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Approved policy change or RACI update within 30 business days
Escalation Path: A site operating control systems with no named OT security owner escalates to the OT security lead and the plant manager.
Threats Addressed: Cyberattacks that cause unsafe conditions, loss of production, environmental release, or equipment damage.
KPIs and Metrics: Sites assessed, zones with an approved SL-T, and high risks with a funded treatment.

Name: OT Asset Inventory
Summary: Inventory PLCs, DCS controllers, HMIs, historians, engineering workstations, and network gear by Purdue level.
Description: Passive discovery and site walkdowns build an inventory with firmware versions and owners, reconciled against engineering drawings. Active scanning is not used on live control networks.
In Scope: Inventory of PLCs, RTUs, DCS controllers, HMIs, historians, engineering workstations, and network gear by Purdue level, built from passive discovery and walkdowns.
Out of Scope: IT asset inventory, spare parts stores, and the financial fixed-asset register.
Deliverables: An OT asset inventory with firmware and Purdue level, a new-device report, and a reconciliation against engineering drawings.
Prerequisites: Passive monitoring or a site walkdown, current P&IDs and network drawings, and site access.
Lead Time: Initial site baseline within 30 business days of passive sensors going live or a site walkdown.
SLA Response Target: New or unknown OT device acknowledged within 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Inventory or criticality record updated within 10 business days of a change
Escalation Path: An unknown device that talks to a controller or safety system escalates to the site OT engineer and the OT security lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Unknown or forgotten devices, unmanaged vendor equipment, and vulnerable assets nobody tracks.
KPIs and Metrics: Assets with owner and firmware recorded, unknown devices found, and walkdown reconciliation variance.

Name: OT Asset Criticality Classification
Summary: Rate OT assets by the safety, environmental, and production consequence of compromise.
Description: Consequence, not IT tiering, decides which controllers and HMIs get the strongest protection and monitoring. The crown-jewel list per site is reviewed after major process changes.
In Scope: Rating OT assets by safety, environmental, and production consequence of compromise so protection and monitoring follow consequence.
Out of Scope: Safety integrity level (SIL) determination, reliability-centered maintenance ratings, and IT service tiering.
Deliverables: A consequence-based criticality rating per asset, the rating method, and a crown-jewel list per site.
Prerequisites: The OT asset inventory, process engineering input, and consequence data from hazard studies.
Lead Time: Initial site baseline within 30 business days of passive sensors going live or a site walkdown.
SLA Response Target: New or unknown OT device acknowledged within 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Inventory or criticality record updated within 10 business days of a change
Escalation Path: An unknown device that talks to a controller or safety system escalates to the site OT engineer and the OT security lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Effort spent on low-consequence assets while safety and high-consequence assets stay exposed.
KPIs and Metrics: Assets rated, crown-jewel assets meeting required controls, and ratings reviewed after major change.

Name: OT Configuration Records
Summary: Keep verified known-good backups of controller logic, firmware, HMI projects, and switch configs.
Description: Offline backups and a baseline per critical asset let a site rebuild after an incident and spot unauthorized logic or firmware changes. Backups are test-restored, not just taken.
In Scope: Known-good backups of controller logic, firmware versions, HMI projects, and switch configs, with change detection against the baseline.
Out of Scope: Engineering approval of logic changes, process tuning, and vendor warranty claims.
Deliverables: Configuration baselines and offline backups per critical asset, a backup schedule, and a logic and firmware drift report.
Prerequisites: Vendor engineering tools or an OT backup platform, the asset inventory, and engineer time to verify backups.
Lead Time: Initial site baseline within 30 business days of passive sensors going live or a site walkdown.
SLA Response Target: New or unknown OT device acknowledged within 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Inventory or criticality record updated within 10 business days of a change
Escalation Path: An unknown device that talks to a controller or safety system escalates to the site OT engineer and the OT security lead the same day.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized logic or setpoint changes, controllers that cannot be rebuilt after an incident, and undetected tampering.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical assets with a verified backup in the last 90 days, drift findings, and successful test restores.

Name: Zone and Conduit Design
Summary: Design OT security zones and conduits per IEC 62443-3-2 and 3-3.
Description: Assets are grouped into zones by function and consequence, and each conduit carries only the traffic it needs. Designs are checked against the target security level before build.
In Scope: Designing security zones and conduits per IEC 62443-3-2 and 3-3, grouping assets by function and consequence and defining what each conduit may carry.
Out of Scope: Process control system design, enterprise network core architecture, and cabling installation.
Deliverables: A zone and conduit diagram, conduit requirements per zone pair, and a design review record against the target security level.
Prerequisites: The asset inventory, the OT risk assessment, and current network drawings.
Lead Time: Firewall rule change within 10 business days, implemented in an approved change window. Design work scoped within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Conduit rule or design request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Standard rule change within 10 business days / emergency block within 4 hours with operations approval
Escalation Path: A path from the enterprise network or internet directly to Level 0-2 escalates to the OT security lead and the site OT engineer the same day.
Threats Addressed: Flat control networks where malware spreads from IT to controllers, and uncontrolled vendor connections.
KPIs and Metrics: Sites with an approved zone model, conduits meeting requirements, and open design exceptions.

Name: IT/OT Demilitarized Zone
Summary: Run the Level 3.5 IT/OT DMZ so no traffic passes directly between enterprise and control networks.
Description: Historian replication, jump hosts, and patch and antivirus staging are brokered through the DMZ, each with an owner. A quarterly test confirms no direct path has crept back in.
In Scope: Running the Level 3.5 IT/OT DMZ with brokered services, such as historian replication, jump hosts, and patch and antivirus staging, so no traffic crosses directly.
Out of Scope: Enterprise data center firewalls, historian application support, and cloud analytics projects.
Deliverables: A DMZ design, a permitted-services register with owners, and a quarterly test that no direct IT-to-OT path exists.
Prerequisites: DMZ infrastructure, firewall management, and a named owner for each brokered service.
Lead Time: Firewall rule change within 10 business days, implemented in an approved change window. Design work scoped within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Conduit rule or design request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Standard rule change within 10 business days / emergency block within 4 hours with operations approval
Escalation Path: A path from the enterprise network or internet directly to Level 0-2 escalates to the OT security lead and the site OT engineer the same day.
Threats Addressed: Direct IT-to-OT connections, ransomware crossing from the enterprise into plants, and data exfiltration from historians.
KPIs and Metrics: Direct paths found, DMZ services with an owner, and firewall rules reviewed per year.

Name: Industrial Protocol Filtering
Summary: Limit industrial protocol write and program commands to authorized engineering hosts.
Description: Industrial firewalls with deep packet inspection allow reads broadly but restrict Modbus, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, and S7 writes and logic downloads to named hosts. Rules usually run in alert-only mode before enforcement.
In Scope: Deep packet inspection rules on industrial firewalls that limit Modbus/TCP, DNP3, EtherNet/IP (CIP), and S7comm write and program commands to authorized engineering hosts.
Out of Scope: Process engineering changes, protocol gateway configuration for production, and vendor protocol support.
Deliverables: Protocol filtering rules per conduit, an allowlist of hosts allowed to write or program, and a blocked-command report.
Prerequisites: Industrial firewalls or DPI-capable sensors, protocol knowledge, and engineering input on legitimate write traffic.
Lead Time: Firewall rule change within 10 business days, implemented in an approved change window. Design work scoped within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Conduit rule or design request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Standard rule change within 10 business days / emergency block within 4 hours with operations approval
Escalation Path: A path from the enterprise network or internet directly to Level 0-2 escalates to the OT security lead and the site OT engineer the same day.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized writes to controllers, malicious setpoint or logic downloads, and protocol abuse from compromised hosts.
KPIs and Metrics: Conduits with protocol filtering, blocked write or program commands, and rules running in alert-only mode.

Name: OT Vendor Remote Access Control
Summary: Give vendors and integrators time-boxed, MFA-protected remote access through a jump host, approved per session.
Description: No always-on vendor connections. Each session is requested, approved by the site, and opened for a set window through the DMZ jump host with named accounts.
In Scope: Vendor and integrator remote access through a jump host in the IT/OT DMZ, with named accounts, MFA, time-boxed sessions, and per-session approval by the site.
Out of Scope: Vendor service contracts, the corporate IT VPN service, and the engineering work the vendor performs.
Deliverables: A remote access procedure, a vendor account register, and a per-session approval log.
Prerequisites: A secure remote access gateway, vendor contacts with named users, and an approval role at each site.
Lead Time: Vendor remote access account set up within 5 business days of an approved request. Scheduled sessions need 1 business day of notice.
SLA Response Target: Scheduled session request reviewed within 4 hours / emergency session within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Approved session enabled for a time-boxed window / suspicious session terminated immediately
Escalation Path: An unscheduled or unsupervised session into a control or safety zone escalates to the site OT engineer and the SOC immediately.
Threats Addressed: Compromised vendor credentials, always-on remote connections, and unsupervised vendor changes to live control systems.
KPIs and Metrics: Sessions with a recorded approval, always-on connections removed, and vendor accounts with MFA.

Name: OT Remote Session Supervision
Summary: Watch and record remote sessions into control systems, with authority to end them.
Description: A site supervisor monitors vendor sessions live where the risk calls for it, and every session is recorded. Sessions that drift outside the approved scope are terminated.
In Scope: Live monitoring and recording of remote sessions into control systems, with a site supervisor able to terminate a session.
Out of Scope: Vendor performance management and engineering approval of the change being made.
Deliverables: Session recordings, a supervision log per session, and a report of terminated sessions.
Prerequisites: Session recording on the jump host, trained supervisors at the site, and a session schedule.
Lead Time: Vendor remote access account set up within 5 business days of an approved request. Scheduled sessions need 1 business day of notice.
SLA Response Target: Scheduled session request reviewed within 4 hours / emergency session within 30 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Approved session enabled for a time-boxed window / suspicious session terminated immediately
Escalation Path: An unscheduled or unsupervised session into a control or safety zone escalates to the site OT engineer and the SOC immediately.
Threats Addressed: Malicious or mistaken vendor actions during remote sessions and use of a session beyond its approved scope.
KPIs and Metrics: Sessions supervised live, sessions terminated, and recordings reviewed after a change.

Name: Controller and HMI Hardening
Summary: Apply vendor-supported secure configuration to PLCs, RTUs, and HMIs.
Description: Controllers stay in RUN with the keyswitch removed, default passwords are changed, and unused web servers and services are disabled. Changes go in at planned outages, and exceptions carry compensating controls.
In Scope: Vendor-supported secure configuration for PLCs, RTUs, and HMIs, including keyswitch in RUN, changed default passwords, and disabled web servers and unused services.
Out of Scope: Process logic changes, HMI screen design, and controller replacement projects.
Deliverables: A hardening baseline per controller and HMI model, a compliance report, and exceptions with compensating controls.
Prerequisites: The asset inventory, vendor hardening guides, and planned outage windows.
Lead Time: Hardening baseline for a new asset type within 20 business days. Changes go in at the next planned outage or maintenance window.
SLA Response Target: Hardening request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Hardening applied in the next planned outage or maintenance window after vendor confirmation
Escalation Path: A hardening change that could affect safety or production is routed through management of change before work starts.
Threats Addressed: Remote program downloads, default credentials, and exploitation of embedded web servers.
KPIs and Metrics: Controllers left in REMOTE or PROGRAM mode, default credentials remaining, and baseline compliance.

Name: Engineering Workstation Security
Summary: Secure the engineering workstations used to program controllers.
Description: Engineering workstations have no email or internet, a short list of users, vendor-qualified endpoint protection, and controlled media. A compromised workstation can push malicious logic, so they are treated as crown jewels.
In Scope: Securing engineering workstations used to program controllers, with restricted interactive use, no internet or email, vendor-approved endpoint protection, and controlled media.
Out of Scope: Standard IT desktops, engineering software licensing, and logic changes in projects.
Deliverables: An engineering workstation baseline, a list of who may use each workstation, and a compliance report.
Prerequisites: A workstation inventory, vendor-qualified security tools, and site engineers.
Lead Time: Hardening baseline for a new asset type within 20 business days. Changes go in at the next planned outage or maintenance window.
SLA Response Target: Hardening request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Hardening applied in the next planned outage or maintenance window after vendor confirmation
Escalation Path: A hardening change that could affect safety or production is routed through management of change before work starts.
Threats Addressed: Compromised engineering workstations used to push malicious logic to controllers.
KPIs and Metrics: Workstations meeting baseline, workstations with internet access, and access exceptions.

Name: OT Application Control
Summary: Allowlist the software that may run on HMIs, historians, and OT servers.
Description: Policies run in audit mode first, are confirmed with the control system vendor, and are then enforced in a maintenance window. Allowlisting suits OT hosts because their software changes rarely.
In Scope: Application allowlisting on HMIs, historians, and OT servers, run in audit mode first and then enforced after vendor qualification.
Out of Scope: IT application allowlisting and vendor software updates.
Deliverables: Application control policies, a blocked-execution report, and the approved software list per host.
Prerequisites: Vendor compatibility confirmation, a test system or spare host, and a maintenance window to switch to enforce mode.
Lead Time: Hardening baseline for a new asset type within 20 business days. Changes go in at the next planned outage or maintenance window.
SLA Response Target: Hardening request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Hardening applied in the next planned outage or maintenance window after vendor confirmation
Escalation Path: A hardening change that could affect safety or production is routed through management of change before work starts.
Threats Addressed: Malware and unapproved tools running on OT hosts.
KPIs and Metrics: Hosts in enforce mode, blocked executions, and hosts still in audit mode after 90 days.

Name: OT Vulnerability Assessment
Summary: Match OT asset versions against ICS advisories and rank them by consequence and reachability.
Description: CISA ICS advisories and vendor bulletins are checked against the inventory using passive data and vendor-safe queries. A reachable flaw on a crown-jewel controller ranks above a higher CVSS score on an isolated one.
In Scope: Matching OT asset versions against CISA ICS advisories and vendor bulletins, using passive data and vendor-safe queries, with consequence and reachability used to rank them.
Out of Scope: Active network scanning that could disrupt the process, IT vulnerability scanning, and penetration testing.
Deliverables: An OT vulnerability report, a ranked advisory list per site, and recommended mitigations.
Prerequisites: An asset inventory with firmware versions, advisory feeds, and safe assessment methods agreed with the site.
Lead Time: New site added to advisory tracking within 20 business days of its inventory baseline.
SLA Response Target: New ICS advisory affecting site assets triaged within 5 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Mitigation decision within 10 business days / patch deployed at the next planned outage after vendor qualification
Escalation Path: A known exploited vulnerability on a reachable controller or HMI escalates to the OT security lead and the plant manager for an interim mitigation.
Threats Addressed: Exploitable flaws in controllers, HMIs, and OT software that are reachable from IT or vendors.
KPIs and Metrics: Advisories triaged within 5 business days, reachable critical flaws, and mitigations applied.

Name: OT Patch Qualification
Summary: Qualify OT patches with the control system vendor and a test bench before the next planned outage.
Description: Only vendor-approved patches are tested, and they are deployed during outages or turnarounds, which may be months apart. Compensating controls cover the gap.
In Scope: Confirming each OT patch is approved by the control system vendor, testing it on a test bench or spare, and scheduling it for the next planned outage.
Out of Scope: Deploying the patches, vendor support contracts, and IT patching.
Deliverables: A patch qualification record, vendor approval evidence, and the qualified patch list for the next outage.
Prerequisites: Vendor-approved patch lists, a test bench or spare, and engineering time.
Lead Time: New site added to advisory tracking within 20 business days of its inventory baseline.
SLA Response Target: New ICS advisory affecting site assets triaged within 5 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Mitigation decision within 10 business days / patch deployed at the next planned outage after vendor qualification
Escalation Path: A known exploited vulnerability on a reachable controller or HMI escalates to the OT security lead and the plant manager for an interim mitigation.
Threats Addressed: Unpatched exploitable systems and patches that crash controllers or HMIs.
KPIs and Metrics: Patches qualified within 60 days of vendor release, qualified patches deployed, and patch-caused trips.

Name: Compensating Control Management
Summary: Track compensating controls for OT flaws that cannot be patched until an outage, or at all.
Description: Tighter conduit rules, extra monitoring, or a disabled service stand in for the patch. Each control is verified and reviewed before it expires.
In Scope: Compensating controls, such as tighter conduit rules, monitoring, or disabling a vulnerable service, for flaws that cannot be patched until an outage or at all.
Out of Scope: Funding asset replacement and vendor end-of-life decisions.
Deliverables: A compensating control register, verification that each control works, and an expiry review.
Prerequisites: Vulnerability findings, engineering input, and a risk acceptance process.
Lead Time: New site added to advisory tracking within 20 business days of its inventory baseline.
SLA Response Target: New ICS advisory affecting site assets triaged within 5 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Mitigation decision within 10 business days / patch deployed at the next planned outage after vendor qualification
Escalation Path: A known exploited vulnerability on a reachable controller or HMI escalates to the OT security lead and the plant manager for an interim mitigation.
Threats Addressed: Unpatchable flaws left exposed for years.
KPIs and Metrics: Unpatched flaws with a verified compensating control, controls verified per year, and expired exceptions.

Name: OT Account Management
Summary: Manage named accounts, roles, and joiner-mover-leaver changes on OT domains and HMIs.
Description: Operators, engineers, and vendors get named accounts in a separate OT domain where possible, reviewed quarterly and removed promptly when people leave.
In Scope: Named accounts, role-based access, and joiner-mover-leaver control for operators, engineers, and vendors on OT domains and HMIs.
Out of Scope: Enterprise directory administration and operator role assignment in the process.
Deliverables: An OT account register, quarterly access reviews, and a leaver removal report.
Prerequisites: A separate OT domain or local account inventory, role definitions, and an HR leaver feed.
Lead Time: New OT account set up within 3 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Access granted within 3 business days / removed within 1 business day of a person leaving
Escalation Path: A shared or default account with write access to controllers or safety systems escalates to the OT security lead.
Threats Addressed: Former staff and vendors with access, excessive privilege, and accounts nobody tracks.
KPIs and Metrics: Accounts with an owner, time to remove leavers, and reviews completed.

Name: Shared Account Control
Summary: Control the shared operator and vendor accounts that control systems still require.
Description: Where a system cannot support named users, the shared credentials are vaulted, checked out, rotated, and tied to a logbook so changes can be traced to a person.
In Scope: Controlling shared operator and vendor accounts that systems still need, with vaulting, check-out, rotation, and logbook attribution.
Out of Scope: Removing shared accounts where the vendor does not support it, and IT server privileged access.
Deliverables: A shared account register, a check-out log, and password rotation records.
Prerequisites: A shared account list, a vault or logbook, and operator procedures.
Lead Time: New OT account set up within 3 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Access granted within 3 business days / removed within 1 business day of a person leaving
Escalation Path: A shared or default account with write access to controllers or safety systems escalates to the OT security lead.
Threats Addressed: Actions that cannot be traced to a person, and passwords still known by former staff.
KPIs and Metrics: Shared accounts vaulted, rotations completed on schedule, and unattributed changes.

Name: OT Removable Media Control
Summary: Control USB drives and contractor laptops entering control environments.
Description: Media is scanned at kiosks before use, only approved media is allowed, and violations are reported per site. Removable media is one of the most common ways malware reaches isolated control networks.
In Scope: Scanning kiosks, approved encrypted media, and rules for USB and laptop use inside control environments.
Out of Scope: IT endpoint USB policy and business data transfer.
Deliverables: A removable media standard, scanning kiosk logs, and media violation reports.
Prerequisites: Scanning kiosks at site entry points, approved media, and operator training.
Lead Time: New OT account set up within 3 business days of approval.
SLA Response Target: Access request acknowledged within 1 business day
SLA Resolution Target: Access granted within 3 business days / removed within 1 business day of a person leaving
Escalation Path: A shared or default account with write access to controllers or safety systems escalates to the OT security lead.
Threats Addressed: Malware carried into control systems on USB drives and contractor laptops.
KPIs and Metrics: Media scanned before use, violations per site, and infected media caught at kiosks.

Name: Passive OT Network Monitoring
Summary: Monitor control networks passively with sensors that decode industrial protocols.
Description: SPAN or TAP sensors at Levels 1-3 give the SOC visibility of new connections, reconnaissance, and controller commands without sending any traffic to the process.
In Scope: Passive OT network detection using SPAN or TAP sensors at Levels 1-3 that decode industrial protocols without sending traffic to the process.
Out of Scope: Active polling or scanning, process historian analytics, and IT network monitoring.
Deliverables: A sensor placement plan per site, OT detection rules, and a weekly OT alert summary.
Prerequisites: SPAN or TAP ports on OT switches, sensors, and SOC integration.
Lead Time: New site onboarded within 20 business days of sensor installation, plus a 30-day baselining period.
SLA Response Target: High-severity OT alert acknowledged by the SOC within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Control room and site OT engineer notified within 30 minutes / no SOC containment without operations approval
Escalation Path: An alert that suggests manipulation of control or safety functions escalates to the control room shift supervisor and the OT incident lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: Malware on control networks, new or rogue connections, and attacker reconnaissance using industrial protocols.
KPIs and Metrics: Sites and zones monitored, sensor uptime, and confirmed OT detections.

Name: Process Anomaly Detection
Summary: Detect suspicious setpoint, mode, firmware, and logic changes and process values out of range.
Description: Rules tuned with process engineering separate tampering from normal operations. Operator alarm management under ISA-18.2 stays with the control room.
In Scope: Detecting unusual setpoint changes, controller mode changes, firmware or logic downloads, and process values out of range that may show tampering.
Out of Scope: Process optimization, safety system logic, and operator alarm management (ISA-18.2).
Deliverables: Process anomaly rules, alert records, and a quarterly tuning review with process engineering.
Prerequisites: Historian or protocol data, engineering baselines, and analytics capability.
Lead Time: New site onboarded within 20 business days of sensor installation, plus a 30-day baselining period.
SLA Response Target: High-severity OT alert acknowledged by the SOC within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Control room and site OT engineer notified within 30 minutes / no SOC containment without operations approval
Escalation Path: An alert that suggests manipulation of control or safety functions escalates to the control room shift supervisor and the OT incident lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: Malicious setpoint or logic changes and spoofed sensor values that hide them.
KPIs and Metrics: Anomalies investigated, true positives, and false positives per week.

Name: OT Alert Escalation
Summary: Route OT alerts between the SOC, the control room, and OT engineering with process-safe guidance.
Description: The SOC acknowledges and informs, and operations decides what happens to the process. The escalation matrix makes clear what the SOC may and may not do on its own.
In Scope: Routing OT alerts between the SOC, the site control room, and OT engineering with process-safe guidance on what the SOC may and may not do.
Out of Scope: Incident command, process shutdown decisions, and IT alert triage.
Deliverables: An OT escalation matrix, an escalation log, and a contact roster per site.
Prerequisites: Site contacts, SOC procedures, and an agreement with control room operations.
Lead Time: New site onboarded within 20 business days of sensor installation, plus a 30-day baselining period.
SLA Response Target: High-severity OT alert acknowledged by the SOC within 15 minutes
SLA Resolution Target: Control room and site OT engineer notified within 30 minutes / no SOC containment without operations approval
Escalation Path: An alert that suggests manipulation of control or safety functions escalates to the control room shift supervisor and the OT incident lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: SOC actions that trip the process, and slow site awareness of a real attack.
KPIs and Metrics: Escalations within 30 minutes, failed contacts, and site feedback on escalations.

Name: OT Incident Playbooks
Summary: Maintain OT incident playbooks with safety-first steps and named engineering and operations roles.
Description: Playbooks cover scenarios such as ransomware in the DMZ, a compromised engineering workstation, or an unauthorized logic change, with site supplements, and are exercised every year.
In Scope: OT incident playbooks for scenarios such as ransomware in the DMZ, a compromised engineering workstation, or unauthorized logic change, with safety-first steps and named engineering roles.
Out of Scope: IT incident playbooks and process safety emergency procedures.
Deliverables: OT playbooks per scenario, site-specific supplements, and exercise records.
Prerequisites: Site engineering input, emergency response procedures, and IR team roles.
Lead Time: Standing service. Engaged when an OT incident is declared.
SLA Response Target: OT incident lead engaged within 30 minutes of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Containment decision with operations within 2 hours / restoration within the site's recovery objective
Escalation Path: An incident that threatens safety or environmental release follows the site emergency response plan and escalates to the plant manager immediately.
Threats Addressed: Unsafe, slow, or improvised response to OT incidents.
KPIs and Metrics: Playbooks per site, playbooks exercised per year, and updates after incidents.

Name: Process-Safe Containment
Summary: Contain OT incidents without creating a safety or production hazard.
Description: Containment options per zone, such as isolating the DMZ, blocking a conduit, or moving to local or manual control, are agreed with operations in advance and decided together on the day.
In Scope: Choosing containment with operations, such as isolating the IT/OT DMZ, blocking a conduit, or moving to manual or local control, so the process stays in a safe state.
Out of Scope: Process shutdown decisions, which belong to operations, and IT containment actions.
Deliverables: A containment options matrix per zone, a containment decision log, and a safety check record.
Prerequisites: The site OT engineer on call, the zone and conduit design, and playbooks.
Lead Time: Standing service. Engaged when an OT incident is declared.
SLA Response Target: OT incident lead engaged within 30 minutes of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Containment decision with operations within 2 hours / restoration within the site's recovery objective
Escalation Path: An incident that threatens safety or environmental release follows the site emergency response plan and escalates to the plant manager immediately.
Threats Addressed: Malware spreading through plants and containment steps that cause an unsafe trip.
KPIs and Metrics: Containment within target, safety events during containment, and options tested in exercises.

Name: Control System Restoration
Summary: Restore controllers, HMIs, and OT servers from verified known-good backups and confirm the process with operations.
Description: Restoration uses backups checked for integrity, then operations signs off that the process behaves before normal running resumes.
In Scope: Restoring controllers, HMIs, and OT servers from verified known-good backups and confirming the process with operations before handover.
Out of Scope: Buying replacement equipment and IT system restoration.
Deliverables: A restoration runbook, a restoration log, and a process check record signed by operations.
Prerequisites: Verified configuration backups, spare hardware, and vendor support.
Lead Time: Standing service. Engaged when an OT incident is declared.
SLA Response Target: OT incident lead engaged within 30 minutes of declaration
SLA Resolution Target: Containment decision with operations within 2 hours / restoration within the site's recovery objective
Escalation Path: An incident that threatens safety or environmental release follows the site emergency response plan and escalates to the plant manager immediately.
Threats Addressed: Extended production outage and restoring logic that is already compromised.
KPIs and Metrics: Restorations within objective, backup verification failures, and post-restore trips.

Name: Safety Instrumented System Protection
Summary: Protect safety instrumented systems with separation, controlled links, and change control per IEC 61511.
Description: The SIS is kept separate from the basic process control system, engineering access is limited, and SIS changes go through safety change control. SIL verification stays with process safety.
In Scope: Security controls for safety instrumented systems, including separation from the BPCS, read-only links, keyswitch control, and SIS change control, as IEC 61511 requires.
Out of Scope: SIS design, SIL verification, and process hazard analysis.
Deliverables: An SIS security assessment, a required control list, and a verification record.
Prerequisites: An SIS inventory, safety engineering input, and network drawings.
Lead Time: Cyber review joins the next scheduled PHA or MOC cycle. Standalone reviews start within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review findings within 15 business days, or before the MOC is approved
Escalation Path: A security weakness that could defeat a safety instrumented function escalates to the process safety lead and the OT security lead before startup.
Threats Addressed: Attacks that disable or change safety functions before an unsafe event.
KPIs and Metrics: SIS with verified separation, open access exceptions, and findings closed before restart.

Name: Safety-Security Risk Alignment
Summary: Add cyber causes to PHA and HAZOP studies so control-dependent safeguards are tested for cyber failure.
Description: A cyber PHA asks what happens if an attacker controls the systems a safeguard relies on, and records joint risks that process safety and OT security both track.
In Scope: Adding cyber causes to PHA and HAZOP studies (cyber PHA) so safeguards that depend on control systems are checked for cyber failure.
Out of Scope: Running the hazard studies and safety certification.
Deliverables: A cyber-informed hazard review record, joint risk register entries, and recommendations.
Prerequisites: The PHA revalidation schedule, safety engineers, and the OT risk assessment.
Lead Time: Cyber review joins the next scheduled PHA or MOC cycle. Standalone reviews start within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review findings within 15 business days, or before the MOC is approved
Escalation Path: A security weakness that could defeat a safety instrumented function escalates to the process safety lead and the OT security lead before startup.
Threats Addressed: Cyber-caused hazards missing from safety studies and safeguards that rely on systems an attacker can control.
KPIs and Metrics: PHAs with cyber input, joint risks tracked, and recommendations closed.

Name: Management of Change Security Review
Summary: Add a security review to the site management of change (MOC) process for control system changes.
Description: Every MOC touching control systems, new connections, or vendor work gets a short security checklist, with conditions to meet before startup.
In Scope: A security checklist inside the site management of change (MOC) process for control system changes, vendor work, and new connections.
Out of Scope: Engineering design approval and change scheduling.
Deliverables: A security checklist for MOC, a review record per change, and required conditions.
Prerequisites: Access to the MOC system, change details, and site engineers.
Lead Time: Cyber review joins the next scheduled PHA or MOC cycle. Standalone reviews start within 10 business days.
SLA Response Target: Review request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Review findings within 15 business days, or before the MOC is approved
Escalation Path: A security weakness that could defeat a safety instrumented function escalates to the process safety lead and the OT security lead before startup.
Threats Addressed: Changes that open new network paths or weaken controls without anyone noticing.
KPIs and Metrics: MOCs with a security review, conditions met before startup, and incidents from unreviewed changes.

Name: Control Room Security
Summary: Secure control rooms, rack rooms, and engineering offices against unauthorized physical access.
Description: Badge control, CCTV, and console security protect the places where one person could change or stop the process. Access lists are reviewed every year.
In Scope: Access control, CCTV, and console security for control rooms, rack rooms, and engineering offices.
Out of Scope: General site security operations and control room ergonomics.
Deliverables: A control room access list, an access review record, and a camera coverage check.
Prerequisites: A badge system, site security, and control room supervisors.
Lead Time: Site physical assessment scheduled within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Physical security issue at a control asset acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Temporary control within 4 hours / permanent fix within 20 business days
Escalation Path: Unauthorized entry to a control room or tampering with a field cabinet escalates to site security and the OT incident lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: Unauthorized console use, sabotage, and tampering with OT servers and network gear.
KPIs and Metrics: Access reviews completed, unauthorized entries, and coverage gaps.

Name: Field Device Tamper Protection
Summary: Protect remote field cabinets, RTUs, and unmanned stations against tampering.
Description: Locks, seals, and alarmed enclosures on field cabinets and substations report tampering to the control center. Seal audits confirm nothing was opened unnoticed.
In Scope: Locks, seals, alarmed enclosures, and door contacts on remote field cabinets, RTUs, and unmanned substations or pump stations.
Out of Scope: Device replacement and field maintenance scheduling.
Deliverables: A field cabinet protection standard, a seal and lock audit, and tamper alarm records.
Prerequisites: A field device inventory, maintenance crews, and alarm integration to the control center.
Lead Time: Site physical assessment scheduled within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Physical security issue at a control asset acknowledged within 1 hour
SLA Resolution Target: Temporary control within 4 hours / permanent fix within 20 business days
Escalation Path: Unauthorized entry to a control room or tampering with a field cabinet escalates to site security and the OT incident lead immediately.
Threats Addressed: Tampering, theft, and unauthorized laptop connections at remote sites.
KPIs and Metrics: Cabinets with tamper alarms, seal breaches, and audits completed.

Name: Product Security Requirements
Summary: Define security requirements for connected products and embedded devices against IEC 62443-4-2.
Description: Requirements are set at concept phase and traced to release, covering authentication, signed firmware, secure defaults, and logging. Waivers need formal approval.
In Scope: Security requirements for connected products and embedded devices, mapped to IEC 62443-4-2 component requirements and target markets.
Out of Scope: Writing firmware, certification lab testing, and marketing claims.
Deliverables: A product security requirements set, a traceability matrix to 62443-4-2, and requirement waivers with approval.
Prerequisites: Product scope, target markets and standards, and engineering input.
Lead Time: Engagement starts at the product concept phase, within 10 business days of program kickoff.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Requirements or threat model within 15 business days / test report within 10 business days of test end
Escalation Path: A release candidate with unresolved critical findings escalates to the product security lead and the product owner before release approval.
Threats Addressed: Products shipped with default passwords, unsigned firmware, or unauthenticated maintenance interfaces.
KPIs and Metrics: Requirements met at release, approved waivers, and late requirement changes.

Name: Product Threat Analysis
Summary: Threat-model products across their field interfaces, update paths, and cloud services.
Description: Following IEC 62443-4-1, each product gets a threat model updated every major release, including how integrators and asset owners will actually deploy it.
In Scope: Threat modeling for products per IEC 62443-4-1 practice 2, covering field interfaces, update paths, cloud services, and integrator misuse.
Out of Scope: Enterprise threat intelligence and penetration testing.
Deliverables: A product threat model, a ranked threat list, and mitigation requirements.
Prerequisites: Architecture diagrams, an interface list, and engineering participation.
Lead Time: Engagement starts at the product concept phase, within 10 business days of program kickoff.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Requirements or threat model within 15 business days / test report within 10 business days of test end
Escalation Path: A release candidate with unresolved critical findings escalates to the product security lead and the product owner before release approval.
Threats Addressed: Exploitable design flaws found only after products are installed in the field.
KPIs and Metrics: Products with a current threat model, threats mitigated, and models updated each major release.

Name: Embedded Software Security Testing
Summary: Test firmware and embedded software with static analysis, fuzzing, and binary analysis.
Description: Testing looks for memory corruption, hardcoded credentials, and open debug ports such as JTAG and UART before release, and retests fixes.
In Scope: Security testing of firmware and embedded software, including static analysis, protocol fuzzing, binary composition analysis, and checks for debug ports such as JTAG and UART.
Out of Scope: Functional testing, certification lab testing, and IT application testing.
Deliverables: A test plan, a findings report, and retest results.
Prerequisites: Firmware builds, test hardware, and engineering contacts.
Lead Time: Engagement starts at the product concept phase, within 10 business days of program kickoff.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Requirements or threat model within 15 business days / test report within 10 business days of test end
Escalation Path: A release candidate with unresolved critical findings escalates to the product security lead and the product owner before release approval.
Threats Addressed: Memory corruption flaws, hardcoded credentials, and debug interfaces left open on production units.
KPIs and Metrics: Critical findings fixed before release, test coverage, and flaws found after release.

Name: Product Vulnerability Response
Summary: Run the product PSIRT from intake through coordinated disclosure and CSAF advisories.
