Description: Reports from researchers and customers are triaged, fixed, and disclosed per ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111. Actively exploited flaws are also reported to regulators where the EU Cyber Resilience Act applies.
In Scope: PSIRT handling of product vulnerabilities per ISO/IEC 30111 and 29147, from intake through coordinated disclosure, CVE assignment, and CSAF advisories.
Out of Scope: Enterprise vulnerability management and support for issues that are not security issues.
Deliverables: A security advisory in CSAF format, a fix tracking record, and CVE records where needed.
Prerequisites: An intake channel, engineering owners per product, and an advisory publishing channel.
Lead Time: PSIRT intake live from day one.
SLA Response Target: Researcher or customer report acknowledged within 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: CSAF advisory and fix or mitigation within 90 days for high severity / actively exploited flaws reported to regulators within 24 hours where the EU Cyber Resilience Act applies
Escalation Path: An actively exploited product vulnerability escalates to the product security lead, legal, and customer communications the same day.
Threats Addressed: Customers exposed to known flaws, uncoordinated public disclosure, and missed regulatory reporting.
KPIs and Metrics: Time to advisory, fixes released within target, and exploited flaws.

Name: Product Security Update Delivery
Summary: Deliver signed, tested security updates and tell asset owners which updates suit their installed versions.
Description: Updates are signed with protected keys and released with clear notes, so customers' OT teams can qualify them for their next outage.
In Scope: Signed, tested security updates for products in the field, with release notes that tell asset owners which updates are qualified for their installed versions.
Out of Scope: Feature releases, field service visits, and customer contracts.
Deliverables: An update release plan, signing records, and an update adoption report where telemetry allows.
Prerequisites: Update build infrastructure, protected signing keys, and release engineering.
Lead Time: PSIRT intake live from day one.
SLA Response Target: Researcher or customer report acknowledged within 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: CSAF advisory and fix or mitigation within 90 days for high severity / actively exploited flaws reported to regulators within 24 hours where the EU Cyber Resilience Act applies
Escalation Path: An actively exploited product vulnerability escalates to the product security lead, legal, and customer communications the same day.
Threats Addressed: Fleets left unpatched and malicious or tampered updates.
KPIs and Metrics: Updates released on schedule, fleet adoption, and failed or rolled-back updates.

Name: End-of-Support Management
Summary: Define and publish security support periods and end-of-support dates for products.
Description: Published support periods let customers plan replacement long before a product stops receiving security fixes.
In Scope: Defining and publishing security support periods and end-of-support dates for products so customers can plan replacement.
Out of Scope: Product lifecycle strategy and commercial pricing.
Deliverables: A support period policy, end-of-support notices, and a customer migration guide.
Prerequisites: The product roadmap, legal input, and customer communications.
Lead Time: PSIRT intake live from day one.
SLA Response Target: Researcher or customer report acknowledged within 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: CSAF advisory and fix or mitigation within 90 days for high severity / actively exploited flaws reported to regulators within 24 hours where the EU Cyber Resilience Act applies
Escalation Path: An actively exploited product vulnerability escalates to the product security lead, legal, and customer communications the same day.
Threats Addressed: Customers running unsupported products with known flaws.
KPIs and Metrics: Products with a published support period, notices issued on time, and units still in the field past support.

Name: Product Security Certification
Summary: Prepare products and the development process for certifications such as ISASecure and IEC 62443-4-1 and 4-2.
Description: A readiness assessment and evidence pack shorten time to certification and stop gaps from blocking sales or market entry.
In Scope: Preparing products and the development process for certifications such as ISASecure CSA or SDLA, IEC 62443-4-1 and 4-2, and market conformity schemes.
Out of Scope: Running the certification lab and paying certification fees.
Deliverables: A certification readiness assessment, an evidence pack, and a remediation plan.
Prerequisites: Product documentation, test results, and a certification body contact.
Lead Time: Certification readiness planned within 20 business days of a request.
SLA Response Target: Request acknowledged in 3 business days
SLA Resolution Target: Evidence pack within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A certification gap that blocks a sale or market entry escalates to the product security lead and the product owner.
Threats Addressed: Lost sales and blocked market access for uncertified products.
KPIs and Metrics: Certifications achieved, readiness gaps, and time to certify.

Name: SBOM Provision
Summary: Produce SBOMs for every product release and share them, with VEX statements, with customers.
Description: SBOMs in SPDX or CycloneDX come from the build pipeline. VEX statements tell customers whether a listed vulnerability is actually exploitable in the product.
In Scope: Producing SBOMs in SPDX or CycloneDX for each product release, sharing them with customers, and publishing VEX statements on whether listed vulnerabilities are exploitable.
Out of Scope: Open-source license compliance and fixing the vulnerable components.
Deliverables: An SBOM per product release, an SBOM sharing procedure, and VEX statements for high-profile vulnerabilities.
Prerequisites: SBOM tooling in the build pipeline, release records, and a customer request channel.
Lead Time: SBOM generation added to the release pipeline for a new product line within 15 business days.
SLA Response Target: Customer SBOM request acknowledged in 2 business days
SLA Resolution Target: SBOM delivered within 5 business days of a customer request / refreshed with every release
Escalation Path: An SBOM that shows a known exploited component in a shipped release escalates to the product security lead and the PSIRT the same day.
Threats Addressed: Hidden vulnerable components and customers unable to judge their exposure.
KPIs and Metrics: Releases with an SBOM, SBOM requests met on time, and VEX statements issued.

Name: Building Automation System Security
Summary: Secure BAS and BMS platforms for HVAC, lighting, metering, and elevators.
Description: Supervisory servers and field controllers are inventoried and hardened, internet exposure is removed, and integrator remote access is brought under control. Fire alarm and life-safety systems are excluded.
In Scope: Security for BAS and BMS platforms, including HVAC, lighting, metering, and elevator controllers, supervisory servers, and integrator remote access.
Out of Scope: Fire alarm and life-safety system design under NFPA 72 and building maintenance.
Deliverables: A BAS asset list, a security baseline for supervisory servers and field controllers, and an assessment report.
Prerequisites: The BAS inventory from the integrator, vendor contacts, and facilities engineering.
Lead Time: Building system assessment scheduled within 20 business days.
SLA Response Target: Building system security issue acknowledged within 4 business hours
SLA Resolution Target: Internet-exposed controller removed from exposure within 1 business day / other findings planned within 20 business days
Escalation Path: A building automation system reachable from the internet, or with an unknown vendor remote connection, escalates to the facilities engineering lead and the SOC the same day.
Threats Addressed: Internet-exposed BACnet or Niagara controllers, default credentials, and unmanaged integrator remote access.
KPIs and Metrics: BAS assets inventoried, exposed controllers, and integrator connections under control.

Name: Building Systems Network Separation
